items.title: Human-first room conversation: human-only posts, member replies in shared threads, and a thread side panel in one contextual right pane
items.summary: Add a Control-authorized Space append that stores a human post or thread reply in Session Core without starting a model turn, let any member holding that decision reply in any room thread (Session Core still applies an owner-only check to Space threads), keep thread counters at write time, and record a per-thread agent-engagement fact so an agent that has spoken in a thread hears follow-ups. Render threads in a generalised right-hand AuxPane (standard header, resize, focus hand-off) bound to ?thread=, so the thread deep links that Activity already emits finally open the thread.
items.whyItMatters: Every room post is a model invocation today, and non-owners cannot reply although the UI offers Reply. Until people can talk to each other in shared threads, a Space is a shared AI prompt box rather than a Teams or Slack room. Mentions, notifications, search, reactions and edits all attach to these entries, and the AuxPane is the host for runs, members and agent sessions later.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (posting and thread counters); qm (multi-author continuation and engagement rule); Slack (thread panel, pop-out window, Threads view) for the pattern; Grok Bot for the pane mechanics
others: Teams (reply in place from an inbox thread card via a tree-grid compose box)
Buzz (one shared right panel for threads, canvas, members and agent sessions)
Slack help text on the Threads view (DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-01] Human-first rooms 4 of 5 sources and threads 5 of 5 (table-stakes); the agent engagement rule only in qm (unique) [R-t1-12-01] thread panel 3 of 5 (Slack, Teams, Buzz); contextual right pane 3 of 5 (Grok Bot, Teams, Slack); table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-01] buzz: a message is an event tagged with the channel id; posting is a plain append and agents receive it only through mention or subscription rules. A reply carries root and parent ids; ingest rejects unknown parents, sets depth, and upserts thread_metadata (reply_count, descendant_count, last_reply_at, broadcast flag) in the same transaction, so clients never count replies. qm: any member of the scope can continue a thread and each entry has a speaker label; botHasStakeInThread (agent spoke or was mentioned, LRU cache with a 5 min negative TTL) decides whether a human reply becomes an ambient agent turn. [R-t1-12-01] Message carries thread_root_id; the pane route ?thread=<id> renders root plus replies with its own composer and scroll state; follow state per user feeds a Threads list with per-thread unread; pop-out opens the same route in a new window. The shell is one <AuxPane kind title actions onBack onDismiss> with an open -> closing (inert + aria-hidden, ~300 ms linger) -> closed state machine, width persisted per user, a role=separator handle with aria-valuenow and arrow-key resize, focus moved to the first enabled control, and a width breakpoint that decides docked vs overlay.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-01-01] No route appends a human message without a model turn (the composer always calls streamChat; the gateway messages route is GET only). Session Core AppendMessage already exists and carries the Space decision fields, but it calls authorize_thread_owner(Mutate) at grpc.rs:4504, so non-owner replies are refused while the UI offers Reply. No thread side panel, reply counts or also-send-to-room, and no agent engagement record. Some docs claim a human-only flow; the code does not have it (doc-vs-code discrepancy). [R-t1-12-01] The third column exists with a responsive collapse, but it cannot host a thread, run, member list or any interactive content; it has no standard header or resize. There is no thread panel, no followed-threads view and no consumer of the ?thread_id= links Activity generates. A shared-read refusal on the transcript currently renders as an empty thread rather than a "you cannot read these turns" state.

items.approach: [R-t1-01-01] Control Plane (user-core): mint a digest-bound space:post decision (or reuse thread:append) for member posts and replies. Model Plane (Session Core): for Space-bound threads accept AppendMessage from any member holding that decision (keep the owner check for non-Space threads), stamp the audience revision, write thread_metadata counters in the same transaction, and add an agent_thread_stake table (thread, agent_ref, reason spoke|mentioned). Gateway (Frontend Plane Rust): new routes POST /api/v1/spaces/{space_ref}/threads and POST /api/v1/spaces/{space_ref}/threads/{thread_id}/messages that reuse the decision minting in inject_personal_thread_context (spaces.rs:49-184) with a client idempotency_key and call CreateThread/AppendMessage without invoking a model; dispatch an ambient agent turn only when the entry mentions a bound agent or a stake exists, running with the invoker's grants. Frontend: split Send from Ask/@agent in SpaceRoomComposer, add a thread side panel with reply counts and an also-post-to-room toggle, and show an 'agent is following this thread' chip. Application Plane projects counters and unread. [R-t1-12-01] Frontend Plane only for the first slice. (1) Build AuxPane in features/spaces/components, lifting the separator and persisted-width logic from the Inbox/Chat canvas code, keeping the existing 720 px collapse. (2) Add kind "thread": read ?thread= in SpacePage, fetch with the existing getSpaceThreadTranscript path (Model Plane Session Core stays the transcript owner), render root plus replies and the existing composer in reply mode; show an explicit "you cannot read these turns" state for refusals instead of an empty list. (3) Follow/unread-per-thread and a Threads view need the participant/unread projection (S1.7) in Application Plane and later push realtime. Pop-out window = same route in a new tab.

Gateway Space write routes (no-invoke create and append)
F-t1-007 (R-t1-01-02) mentions, so agents are summoned explicitly
Model Plane Session Core thread transcript read via the gateway (exists)
S1.7 participant/unread projection in Application Plane (for follow state and per-thread unread)
Push realtime or the Application delivery/projection outbox (category 09) for live replies
Run console components for the later run/agent-session kind (F-t1-004 (R-t1-12-03))
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (Session Core append, thread metadata) with a Control Plane space:post/thread:append decision; Frontend Plane (gateway routes, AuxPane, thread panel)
items.risks: [R-t1-01-01] Two write paths on one transcript can drift unless both go through the same Session Core entry append. A non-owner append must stamp the audience revision so earlier rows stay hidden from later joiners. Agent turns in shared threads must use the invoker's grants, not the thread owner's. ZDR orgs must not persist human text beyond the Session Core retention rule. Existing tests assume every post is a turn. Agents that silently do not answer need a visible state. [R-t1-12-01] Partial transcripts under deny-by-default shared reads must be shown as such. Keep the room-definition rule that configuration does not live in the room (docs/space-defenition.md: a room that shows configuration becomes a Copilot side panel): the pane should host conversation, run and approval content only. Focus traps and layout thrash at medium widths.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t1-01-01] Partly: shared-thread completion (per-entry audience filtering, participant/unread projections) is open as S1.7 in apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md:1709-1726. The human-only post and the engagement rule are not planned in code.

items.title: Addressed agent wake-up: several agents per message, per-binding respond_to/subscribe trigger policy, offer-to-add, then optional ambient participation
items.summary: Stop treating every room post as a model turn. Add a human-only post path, then let a message wake an agent only when it is addressed (one or several agents, with an address lock in the composer) or matches a binding trigger rule, with per-binding respond_to (owner|allowlist|anyone|nobody) and subscribe (mentions|all|rules) fields and an offer-to-add dialog for an unbound agent. Later add an optional cheap ambient judge with standing orders and an auditable ledger, and a room tool so an agent may stay silent.
items.whyItMatters: A Space is meant to feel like Slack/Teams for people first, with agents joining on demand. Today the composer sends every post through the chat stream, so people cannot simply talk to each other and an agent cannot be silent. This is the single change that makes a Space a room instead of a chat with a bot, and every other agent feature (cards, multi-agent, personal agents) builds on addressed-only wake-up.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (addressing/trigger policy); qm (ambient participation)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Addressing/trigger policy 3 of 5 sources (common); ambient judge 1 of 5 (unique, QM); explicit room I/O 2 of 5 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Buzz binding fields respond_to owner|allowlist|anyone|nobody (fails closed) and subscribe mentions|all|rules; rules are first-match-wins over (content, author, kind, channel) with a timeout and length cap; the composer keeps a persistent per-composer set of addressed agents and records implicit mentions as provenance so edits can strip them; unaddressed messages reach agents only as overheard context. Mention of an agent the author owns but the room lacks opens an Invite+send vs send-as-reference dialog with a fresh authorization per destination; wake publishes the message first, then starts the agent with a replay floor. QM ambient: per-room cursor, a cheap judge prompt (identity + standing orders + do-not-act backdrop + new batch) returns {act, reason, asked_by}; every judgment is stored for admins; ChannelPolicy {orders, bots: ignore|rollup|action|user, ambientEnabled} edited with compare-and-swap and history. QM room tool: post/reach/react/edit/read_thread actions where post rejects destination arguments and a turn that ends without a post is silent.

verevonToday.gap: trigger_modes is enforced at the gateway but there is no author gate, no rule triggers, no policy editor, one agent per message, no address lock, no offer-to-add for unbound or paused agents, and no human-only post (the default assistant answers everything). No ambient judge, standing orders or ledger; no room tool for silence. Control decisions carry no turn-origin (direct|ambient|automation) field.

items.approach: Gateway (Frontend Plane): add a human-only post route under /api/v1/spaces/{ref}/ that stores the message in the Application Plane and does not call the Model Plane unless the addressed-agent set is non-empty or a binding rule matches (the route itself is expected to land with the category-01 human messaging work). Replace the single mentionedAgentRef with an addressed-agent list and keep apply_mention_binding_policy (spaces.rs:4483-4573) as the enforcement point for every addressed agent. Application Plane (convex-core spaceAgents): add respond_to, subscribe and bounded rule fields to the binding. Frontend: policy editor in the Agent tab, composer address lock, offer-to-add dialog that binds and invokes in one Control-decided step. Control: add a turn_origin enum to space decisions and pin human-only walls with negative tests. Phase 3 (optional, default off): a small judge-model service in the Model Plane over Application room events with a room policy object that can only tighten org policy, every judgment stored for admins; a typed `space` room tool (post, react, read_thread) backed by Application room APIs under the turn decision so silence is allowed.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (gateway + composer); Application Plane (binding schema); Model Plane (ambient judge, room tool); Control Plane (turn_origin)
items.risks: People used to the always-on assistant may miss it: make the default room agent an explicit binding. Ambient judge cost and false positives: ship default-off with stored judgments. Agents may stay silent when they should answer: keep a rule that an addressed human always gets a reply.

items.title: Space realtime substrate: typed seq-numbered event projection, resumable per-Space SSE through the gateway, and authorization at subscribe and at every delivery
items.summary: Have the Application Plane emit one typed, metadata-only Space event envelope with a per-Space monotonic seq (reusing the leased Convex outbox pattern already used for lifecycle events), let the gateway terminate one resumable SSE per tab (Last-Event-ID, cursor_too_old snapshot frame, heartbeats under 15 s, a watchdog, the 6 s poll kept as fallback), and send every frame through one fail-closed chokepoint that holds a live Control read decision for (user, Space, audience revision) and closes the stream on revocation or audience change.
items.whyItMatters: All five references push room events; Verevon polls the full thread list every 6 s, so other members see posts and agent replies late, and every live feature (shared run streams, unread counts, presence, calls) has nothing to ride on. Checking authority at subscribe and at every delivery keeps the push tier from becoming a side door around Control decisions and ZDR.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (WatchGrokBotTranscripts: one multiplexed, sequenced stream with updated_seq cursors, cursor_too_old and cleared{generation} frames); Buzz for operations (WebSocket hardening and resume policy); QM for the watchdog; Buzz (typed events with a u32 kind as the only dispatch switch; per-tenant Redis topics with refcounted dynamic SUBSCRIBE, measured 64x ingress reduction); Buzz (single fail-closed fan-out chokepoint filter_fanout_by_access shared by local and cross-node paths; subscribe checks access then registers)
others: Buzz (axum WebSocket, 5 s auth timeout, 30 s ping with 3 missed pongs, bounded send queue, close frame on rolling restart)
QM (SSE open timeout and 30 s silence timeout, resync on every reconnect)
Slack (gateway servers hold sockets, channel servers fan out; DOC)
Teams (Trouter push, relaxed poll when push is healthy; DOC/REA)
QM (session tape as WAL; Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY bus, payload capped near 7.5 KB, resync on reconnect)
Grok Bot (generation counter with cleared and cursor_too_old)
Slack and Teams do server-side access checks but publish no detail (DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-09-01] 5 of 5 for a push channel; table-stakes. 4 of 5 for stream-health watchdog with a polling safety net; 3 of 5 for gap-free resume [R-t1-09-03] 3 of 5 for a typed append-only room log (common); 2 of 5 for a tenant-scoped cross-node bus (differentiator) [R-t1-09-02] 1 of 5; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-09-01] Client opens one stream after auth and sends per-room cursors {room, generation, after_seq}. Server replies connected{stream_id, server_time}, replays rows with seq > after_seq from a bounded window (or sends cursor_too_old so the client re-snapshots), then live frames (rows, deletes, ephemeral presence/typing, agent state, roster change, heartbeat). Client opens live first then backfills and dedupes by id; resume is triggered by online/focus/visibilitychange events (min 5 s apart), never by writing to a half-open socket from a watchdog. On silence the client falls back to polling with jittered reconnect, and while healthy it polls at a relaxed 60-180 s to heal silent drift. [R-t1-09-03] Envelope {id, room_id, seq, kind, author, created_at, refs, body_ref}; append-only; consumers dispatch on kind and ignore unknown kinds; derived state (membership, reply counts, presence snapshots) is emitted as server-authored projection events; a generation bump invalidates replicas. Bus topics {tenant}:room:{id}; a node subscribes only while it has local subscribers (refcount, delayed unsubscribe about 500 ms) and forces client resync after a bus reconnect because messages in the gap are lost. [R-t1-09-02] Subscription registry indexed by (room, kind). On every outbound event: tenant label equality, per-kind audience rules, room membership from a 10 s cache, fail closed on lookup error. On subscribe: load accessible rooms, apply the token scope upper bound, repair negative cache entries against the database, then register. On revocation: publish an idempotent cache-invalidate hint (loss tolerable) and a separate connection-control command that closes affected sockets on every node, so hints and kill commands are never conflated.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-09-01] No WebSocket, SSE or Convex subscription for rooms (SRC: SPACE_TIMELINE_POLL_MS = 6_000 with a code comment that the poll becomes the fallback once a durable delivery projection lands). Last-Event-ID resume exists only for the sender's own turn stream. The room has no cursor, no gap detection, no heartbeat and no stall watchdog, and each poll and each visibility resume refetches the full projection. [R-t1-09-03] SRC: Convex has Space lifecycle, audience, deletion and presence tables with leased outboxes, but no room-message-level event table or per-Space seq. NATS is plain and best-effort between planes, and Convex can optionally mirror mp.v1.* subjects from Model Plane NATS (MODEL_PLANE_NATS_URL). A code comment in space_membership_nats.rs says the JetStream topology for the GDPR consumer is not provisioned, so do not assume JetStream for fan-out. The R-4 projection that the audit says is built at source was not found as a table. [R-t1-09-02] No live delivery path, so no per-delivery check. Authority is re-checked by the browser every 30 s (fail-closed) and per request through Control decisions; revocation reaches Session Core over a plain, best-effort NATS subject (aqencia.controlplane.space.membership_changed) backed by a durable revocation table. A stream would need its own chokepoint honouring audience snapshots and the 2-minute decision TTL.

items.approach: [R-t1-09-01] Frontend Plane gateway (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs or a new spaces_stream module): GET /api/v1/spaces/{id}/events as an axum SSE returning frames connected, event{seq, kind, refs}, ephemeral, heartbeat, cursor_too_old and closing. Frames carry ids and metadata only, so ZDR holds and the client reads bodies through the existing decision-gated read path. Source is the Space event projection and NATS subjects of this item (R-t1-09-03); the authorization chokepoint is this item (R-t1-09-02). Reuse the Redis token-bucket limiter for subscribe attempts. SPA: new src/features/spaces/lib/space-stream.ts owning EventSource, Last-Event-ID resume, watchdog and jittered backoff, applying frames to the store in F-t1-033 (R-t1-09-06); keep the current poll code as degraded mode. Reserve frame kinds for later surfaces (call signalling, extra event kinds) and ignore unknown kinds. [R-t1-09-03] Application Plane convex-core: new spaceEvents table (space_ref, seq, kind, refs, created_at; index space_ref+seq) written by a single-writer mutation that increments a per-Space counter, plus a bounded retention purge and removal through the existing space deletion reconcilers. Producers: Convex Space mutations, and ingestion of Session Core thread/run events from NATS (Model Plane must emit thread-appended and run-state events; verify which mp.v1 subjects exist today). A leased outbox publishes to plain NATS subjects verevon.space.{org}.{space}.events with ids and kinds only; the gateway refetches content through authorized read paths, which also neutralises unsigned-NATS injection. Write a short ADR that Session Core remains the content owner and this stays a projection that is rebuilt from a snapshot when a gap is detected. [R-t1-09-02] In the gateway push module: subscription state {decision, expires_at, audience_revision}; a single deliver(frame) function is the only way bytes reach a socket. Subscribe only after a Control read decision (confirm in user-core decision.go that an existing read intent fits a long-lived stream; otherwise add a stream-read intent there). Re-mint before expiry; on failure close with a typed code and let the client fall back to the decision-gated poll. Subscribe the gateway to aqencia.controlplane.space.membership_changed as a hint that closes matching sockets, with decision expiry as the hard backstop. Frames never include agent content; for per-thread visibility include thread refs only when the decision covers them.

items.planeOwner: Application Plane (event projection, NATS fan-out); Frontend Plane (gateway SSE, SPA client); Control Plane (stream-read decision)
items.risks: [R-t1-09-01] Long-lived connections outlive 2-minute Control decisions, so re-authorization mid-stream is mandatory. Gateway replicas need connection-aware scaling and drain (see F-t1-091 (R-t1-09-11)). Reconnect storms after deploys need jitter. Replay buffers and frames must hold metadata only under ZDR. [R-t1-09-03] Duplicate truth with Session Core if the projection starts carrying content. Per-Space single-writer seq may contend in a busy Space (coalesce high-rate agent events into run_progress kinds). Retention and ZDR deletion must cover the projection table. Co-owned notifications work (F-t1-060 (R-t1-05-10)) should reuse the same outbox rather than add a second one. [R-t1-09-02] Decision minting load (one per subscriber per 2 min). Because NATS is best-effort, revocation latency can reach the decision TTL; consider re-checking the audience revision against Control on each heartbeat for high-sensitivity Spaces.

items.title: Agent work visible to the whole room: shared live run stream, activity/plan/tool cards, an ambient activity strip, typed transcript rows and steer/cancel
items.summary: Let any member with a thread read decision attach to a running agent turn (offset-keyed text deltas, tool steps, a snapshot for late joiners, computer-action frames), render the work as semantic cards (one card per tool call, plan states pending/in_progress/completed/error, completed work collapsed) and typed transcript rows with grouping, add an activity strip near the composer with latch and minimum-display rules and click-through to the run in the AuxPane, and give the working row Stop, Steer and Skip.
items.whyItMatters: In-room activity cards are the one agent capability all five references share (5 of 5). Verevon already renders this in AgentRunConsole and the /chat live run panel, but in a Space the run stream reaches only the sender and others see a status line. People cannot cooperate with an agent whose work they cannot see.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (render classes); slack (stream wire contract); grokbot (live state); buzz (steer/interrupt policies); QM (AG-UI-shaped SSE per run: RUN_STARTED, TOOL_CALL_START/RESULT, text deltas {offset, delta}, run snapshot, RUN_FINISHED; joinable by any authorized viewer); Buzz for the strip interaction; Grok Bot for the latch/threshold rules and the row-kind contract; QM for collapsing completed work
others: Grok Bot (computer_actions frame {type, x, y, button, count, at_ms} for live cursor visualisation)
Buzz (headline rotation about every 2.2 s, hover list of working agents, agent badge with managed-by owner, address prefix)
QM (prompts over 2 lines collapse, completed tool steps collapse into one disclosure, paged history that does not yank the reader)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-07-02] Activity/plan cards 5 of 5 (table-stakes); presence/live state 4 of 5 (table-stakes); steer/interrupt 2 of 5 (differentiator); owner-only observer 1 of 5 [R-t1-09-04] 2 of 5; differentiator [R-t1-12-03] activity strip 2 of 5 (Buzz, Grok Bot; differentiator); typed rows 3 of 5 (Buzz, Grok Bot, QM; table-stakes for human+agent rooms)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-07-02] Buzz classifies each tool call into render classes (message, file-edit, file-read, shell, plan, permission, error, thought) over a raw-event floor; one card per call mutated in place with verb-object-outcome summaries ('Ran tests: 1248 passed'); completed work collapses into one timed disclosure. Slack's chat.startStream/appendStream/stopStream with task_update and plan blocks is the vendor-neutral wire contract. Grok Bot pushes AgentLiveState {is_running, is_composing, is_retrying, activity{kind,tool,target}, awaiting{reason,since}, stale_after_ms, has_running_subagents}; clients treat anything past stale_after as unknown (Buzz: unknown is never offline) and feed one derived working signal to sidebar, composer and card. Buzz steer policy enum queue|steer|interrupt|owner-interrupt with explicit prompt framing ('new message arrived while you were working' / 'new request supersedes previous'); Grok Bot adds skip-this-step without failing the run. [R-t1-09-04] GET /runs/{id}/events authorised by room read decision. Server first replays tool entries since the cursor and the current text length, then streams deltas keyed by byte offset so a late joiner can splice; a terminal snapshot carries the final text. Client falls back to the snapshot endpoint on an offset gap. For computer-use, action frames are batched onto the same stream for a cursor overlay. [R-t1-12-03] Per room: typingUsers (presence TTL) plus workingAgents (run state from the owner projection). A committed-ids latch admits an agent to the visible set when it commits to a turn (not while reading) and releases it only at run end; a phase label shows only after a minimum display threshold. Headline = derive(lastStep) from the run event stream, rotated on a timer, with non-owners getting a generic "working". Rows: Row = message | send-message | event | notice | approval | attachment | spend | synthetic(day, unread, group); agent rows carry {agentRef, ownerRef}; a grouping pass folds consecutive machine rows of the same run into a group row with count and expand.

Application Plane: a realtime projection of run live state from Model Plane run events (coalesced), replacing the poll, with stale_after semantics. Controls: Stop/Steer/Skip on the working row and Work tab; add an interrupt-policy field to the agent binding (queue|steer|interrupt|owner-interrupt); Model Plane steer vs supersede framing and interrupted-effect markers so cancel never races an effect. Later: versioned typed card envelope with fallback text for unsupported kinds (sandboxed iframe only, never raw HTML) and an owner-only run drawer linked from each room turn, frames ephemeral under ZDR. [R-t1-09-04] Application Plane room stream emits run_started{run_ref, thread_ref}. New gateway route GET /api/v1/spaces/{id}/threads/{tid}/runs/{rid}/events authorised by a Control thread-read decision for non-owners, proxying the Model Gateway run events (already seq-based) with Last-Event-ID passthrough, coalescing token deltas to about 50-100 ms, with offset-keyed deltas and a terminal snapshot. Stream through the gateway and never persist there (ZDR). Add a per-thread privacy flag so a turn can hide intermediate tool output from other viewers. For browser agents, reuse the existing live-frame stream and Quarry execution receipts (Model proposes, Quarry executes) as computer-action frames; render in SpaceRoomTimeline as a live exchange block with Stop only for those allowed. [R-t1-12-03] Frontend Plane: put the latch and threshold logic and the headline derivation in a pure module under features/spaces/lib with unit tests, fed by Model Plane run step events through the gateway; click opens the AuxPane run kind (F-t1-001 (R-t1-12-01)) built from AgentRunConsole step components (as SPACE_PAGE_AUDIT S2.5 already asks). items.title: Make zero-data-retention binding in every plane, with typed refusals and content-free telemetry
items.summary: Session Core must act on the zero_data_retention flag in the signed Control decision (today it decodes the flag and discards it): refuse durable thread, message and memory writes under ZDR with a typed code. Prove the same for the other durable stores a Space touches (sandbox-manager process output and snapshots, notification and feed projections, agent_memory and Letta), commit the typed ZDR refusal UI, and add a cross-plane ZDR test matrix. Keep telemetry content-free; add a consent gate only if analytics are ever added.
items.whyItMatters: ZDR is a stated Verevon promise and an architecture rule (it must propagate). Any plane that ignores it is a compliance defect that a regulated buyer will find. GrokBot shows the pattern users expect: a persistent feature is blocked with a visible reason instead of silently storing.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot
others: qm, teams, buzz (consent-gated or scrubbed telemetry)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: ZDR-blocks-persistence: 1 of 5 (grokbot), unique. Consent-gated, scrubbed telemetry: 4 of 5 (grokbot, qm, teams, buzz), table-stakes.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: The backend reports privacy mode; every persistent feature checks it at connect or write time and returns a typed no-storage error that the UI maps to a visible block state with a reason. For telemetry, analytics start disabled or deferred with a capped buffer until consent resolves, are dropped on opt-out, use closed label sets and scrub errors before send.

verevonToday.gap: Session Core ignores the claim, so ZDR is enforced at the edge (gateway, Control, notification-core) but not at the store that persists threads and memory. No cross-plane test proves every durable write path refuses under ZDR; the sandbox-manager and agent_memory paths are unchecked; the typed refusal UI is uncommitted. Telemetry hygiene is currently fine because no third-party SDK was found, but nothing guards it.

items.approach: Model Plane: in session-core CreateThread, message append and agent_memory writes, branch on claims.zero_data_retention and either persist nothing or return a typed zdr_persistence_unavailable status; model-gateway maps it to the existing typed refusal codes; letta-bridge and sandbox-manager (workspace, snapshot, process output) take the same flag from the decision. Application Plane: Space-originated notifications under ZDR carry reference-only payloads (coordinate with category 05 notification work). Frontend Plane: commit zdr-refusals.ts and render one block state per refusal code. Add a ZDR conformance test (one case per durable write path, per plane) and a CI label allowlist so Prometheus labels and error reports stay content-free. Only if analytics are added: consent state machine with a capped deferred buffer.
dependencies: ZDR claim carried in every plane contract

items.risks: Feature regressions for ZDR orgs (persistent computers, memory, schedules) must be explicit rather than silent. A missing claim must fail closed. Pre-existing rows written before a posture change are a retention question, handled by the retention item.

items.title: Space governance admin: effect-policy admin UI with safe presets and typed denials first, then posting rules, agent/model allowlist, locked switches, autonomy posture and rollout flags
items.summary: Phase 1 (priority): an org-admin API and UI over the per-org space_effect_policies rows with safe presets and an effective-policy view, plus typed, actionable denial reasons mapped from Control codes in gateway and UI. Phase 2: per-Space role rules (who may post, use @everyone, invite agents), an allowlist of agents and models that may join Spaces, org-locked switches shown as locked with a reason, a strict/standard/open autonomy posture with tighten-only composition, and agent rate limits separate from human traffic. Phase 3: an admin registry of all Spaces (owners, orphans, archive) and Control-owned feature flags, preview rings and agent-capability kill switches that are rollout controls only, never an authorization input.
items.whyItMatters: Every shared Space effect is deny-by-default and no human admin can write the policy rows (none exist in dev), so most shipped shared features cannot be switched on or verified live. Admin policy is how Teams and QM make AI rooms governable; without it every new capability adds another hidden switch.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (policy administration), qm (admin console), grokbot (typed access-status reasons); teams; teams (layered providers resolved by ring, tenant and account with a local override and editor page, plus Labs/Insider/Public preview programmes)
others: qm (posture tiers and model probe fingerprint)
grokbot (admin switches per capability with lock explanations)
buzz (separate rate tiers for humans and agents)
grokbot (typed dynamic configs with fallback values and validators)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-02-05] admin console 3 of 5 (table-stakes); policy admin 2 of 5 (common); typed access reasons 2 of 5 (differentiator); flags 2 of 5 [R-t1-10-09] Admin-locked settings: 3 of 5 (slack, teams, grokbot); agent and model allowlist: 2 of 5 (teams, qm); agent and human rate limits: 2 of 5 (buzz, qm); posture tiers and posting rules: 1 of 5 each (qm, slack DOC). [R-t1-11-07] 4 of 5 sources (buzz, grokbot, slack, teams) = table-stakes.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-02-05] Teams: every feature area has policies; precedence is direct assignment, then highest-ranked group, then global default; batch assignment has a status log. QM: separate admin service over signed HTTP, admin only from a durable grants store, every mutation audited, bulk actions as jobs with per-item status. GrokBot: one access-status call returns GRANTED, UNAVAILABLE or PAYMENT_REQUIRED plus a typed reason, and the UI has one component per reason. [R-t1-10-09] Settings resolve as policy over user over default per key with a source tag, and the UI receives the list of enforced keys to render a lock with an explanation. A posture enum with rank gives effective = strictest along the scope chain and maps to approval requirements, private-network deny and screening mode. A model is enabled only after a successful probe stored as a fingerprint of definition and credential. Per-principal-kind token buckets are keyed by org, principal and action. [R-t1-11-07] Config service returns typed values per (org, ring, user); client caches with fallbacks and validators; preview programme is a per-org or per-user ring with feature descriptions shown in a Labs panel.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-02-05] A service-only write path for effect policies exists but no human admin can reach it; no assignment beyond one row per org; no typed denial surfacing verified; no admin view of all Spaces; no rollout flags. [R-t1-10-09] No per-Space role rules, no agent or model catalogue, no org-enforced switches with lock UI, no org or Space posture that sets or caps the autonomy rung, and the limiter cannot separate an agent flood from human traffic (an agent shares its org's bucket). [R-t1-11-07] Only plan entitlement booleans exist (FeatureFlags map[string]bool in billing-core, entitlements described in the org-core README) and the client reads them from the billing payload. No remote-config or ring service, no preview programme and no per-org staged rollout or kill switch for Space/agent features was found; Model Plane-side agent toggles were not checked.

items.approach: [R-t1-02-05] Control Plane: a gateway-delegated, org-admin-gated route (new capability in org-core rbac catalog.go) wrapping the existing effect-policy upsert with preset validation (presets must not enable retention-bearing effects under ZDR). Gateway: /api/v1/admin/spaces/policy (GET effective, PUT) and a denial mapper returning {state, reason, actor_role}. Frontend: a Space policy section in WorkspaceSettingsPage and one component per denial reason. Phase 2: Space registry page over Control registered_spaces plus the Convex projection; flags in billing-core or org-core next to entitlements. No impersonation. Group-level assignment waits for teams. [R-t1-10-09] Control user-core: extend the effect policy with space_role_rules (post, mention_all, invite_agent per role), agent_allowlist (org catalogue with allowed, blocked, pending, referencing capability-core registry ids), enforced_switches {key, value, locked, reason} and autonomy_posture with a tighten-only chain org to Space to user; carry the rule revision in decision claims. model-gateway maps posture to an AutonomyRung ceiling used as the minimum with any plan grant; execution-core's check_autonomy_rung already enforces it. capability-core records the model probe fingerprint. Gateway rate_limit.rs adds principal kind and a per-Space bucket. Frontend: one admin Space-policy section (shared with this item (R-t1-02-05)) with lock chips and reasons. [R-t1-11-07] Control Plane org-core (with audit-core events for every change): flag registry with type, default, validator, ring and per-org overrides; gateway returns resolved values in the navbar payload; Model Plane reads the same flags for agent capability gating; Labs panel in settings. Keep authorization in ACLs and approvals, and make flag evaluation fail to the safe default.
dependencies: Room lifecycle (F-t1-022 (R-t1-02-04)) for archive and orphan handling
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (user-core effect policy, flags, registry) with Frontend Plane (admin UI) and Model Plane (posture and capability caps)
items.risks: [R-t1-02-05] Must stay deny-by-default; presets must not silently enable retention-bearing effects under ZDR. Admin views of room content must respect ZDR and thread_read_entitled. Do not reveal policy details to non-admins beyond what they need. Flags must not override deny-by-default effect policies. [R-t1-10-09] Friction for personal agents, so defaults must be sensible. Strict posture can cause approval fatigue, so batch approvals. Moving from one row per org to per-Space rows needs a migration. The limiter fails open by design, so quotas need a documented fail mode. [R-t1-11-07] Flag debt; flags misused as authorization; a client-side flag is a UX hint, not an enforcement point.

items.title: Identity-bound @mentions for people and agents with mention records, role-gated group handles, invite-from-mention and ranked @/# pickers
items.summary: Send mentions as structured subject refs (mentioned_person_refs next to the existing mentioned_agent_ref), validate each against the Control roster in the gateway, store mention records on the entry and emit a content-free mention signal. Replace text-only @person insertion with one typeahead for people, agents and later @room/@here and groups (role-gated); mentioning an owned agent that is not in the room offers to invite it. Polish the picker: rank by recent interaction plus prefix, scroll past six results, and add # references to threads, runs and documents.
items.whyItMatters: [R-t1-01-02] A mention record is the prerequisite for notifications, inbox slices, quotas and audit. Without it people cannot summon each other in a Space and @person is visibly broken (it inserts text that does nothing). The agent half already follows the right rule, so extending it to people keeps one identity model. [R-t1-04-10] Cheap polish that keeps addressing inside ACLs and makes referencing threads, runs and documents possible. The core scoping is already correct.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (identity binding); slack and teams (group handles and role-gated @channel/@team); grokbot
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-02] 4 of 5 sources (table-stakes) [R-t1-04-10] 3 of 5 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-02] The composer keeps a Map<label, subjectId>; the send payload is text plus mentions[] of subject ids, separate from the body. The server validates each id against the room roster, rejects unresolved or ambiguous ones (namesakes get qualified labels, pasted mentions are re-verified and send awaits bindings), stores mention records, and checks broadcast handles against a role policy. Notifications fan out from mention records only. buzz also lets an owner invite an owned agent from the typeahead and re-checks authority at publish, keeping the draft on failure. [R-t1-04-10] A pure scoping function computes the candidate id set from conversation type and membership (group: its members; 1:1: the other bots and groups containing this bot; unadded team bots hidden), composer context exposes getMentionMembers/getMentionPeople/getNoMentionMembers, plus reference providers for PRs, skills and MCP items; buzz mentionRanking ranks by recent interaction and prefix.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-01-02] @agent is shipped and re-resolved server-side (the browser sends only mentioned_agent_ref). @person is text insertion only: no mention record, no notification, no highlight. notification-core uses explicit per-service-principal type allowlists, so a Space mention type has to be added (a generic comment.mentioned type exists). No @room/@here or group handles. No inline invite for an owned agent that is not bound to the room (baseline evidence is absence only, so low evidence). [R-t1-04-10] @ lists roster humans and active agents (max 6, prefix match), so it is already room-scoped, but it has no ranking, no references to threads, runs or documents, and a picked person is only text with no routing.

items.approach: [R-t1-01-02] Frontend: unified typeahead (people, agents, 'your agents not in this room', later @room/@here/user groups) with a label-to-subject map; emit mentioned_person_refs[] next to mentioned_agent_ref and render mention chips. Gateway: validate every ref against the Control roster on the same path as agent re-resolution (spaces.rs:4399-4498), reject ambiguous labels, never trust body text. Model Plane: keep mentions in entry metadata. Application Plane notification-core: add a content-free space.mention type to the Space sender's allowlist (payload carries refs and a deep link only, recipient must pass thread read entitlement, ZDR-safe). Invite-then-send calls the existing agents/bind route, then sends; any failure aborts the send and restores the draft; the server rechecks membership at publish. @room gated by Space role. [R-t1-04-10] Frontend Plane: add recency ranking, scrolling and a # provider in SpaceRoomComposer.tsx; person mention routing belongs to the notifications category.
dependencies: F-t1-001 (R-t1-01-01) human-first posting so a mention has an entry to attach to
notification-core type allowlist change for the Space sender
F-t1-032 (R-t1-01-08) draft restore for the invite-then-send path
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane gateway with Model Plane entry metadata and Application Plane notification-core
items.risks: [R-t1-01-02] A mention of a member who lacks thread read entitlement must not leak content in the notification. ZDR orgs need content-free notifications. @room and group handles need a role policy to avoid noise. Auto-binding an owned agent must not grant more than the room policy allows. [R-t1-04-10] Low.

items.title: Space notifications: typed signals for mentions, replies, approvals and agent completions, refs-only payload, rate limits, per-room levels and thread follow/mute
items.summary: Let conversation-core, capability-core and Control publish typed signals (mention, reply, approval_needed, agent_done, agent_awaiting, invite) into notification-core through a per-service, per-type producer allowlist, with one shared refs-only payload (signal, space, thread, message or run ref, actor, urgency, actions, trace id, deep link) and a rate limit. Add per-room levels (All, Mentions, Off), a hide-preview flag that defaults on for ZDR orgs, and per-user thread follow/mute with auto-follow reasons, applying a fixed rule order (a mention passes, then mute, then thread rules).
items.whyItMatters: No Space event produces a notification today: the producer allowlist only admits run_completed and run_failed, and mention.received is seeded but never produced. People will not notice a mention or an agent waiting on them, which undercuts both the Teams/Slack and the agent half of the vision.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack (payload and gating); Grok Bot for the agent-turn contract and the only implemented rate limiter; Slack (levels and privacy flag); Teams for explicit auto-follow rules; Buzz for the decision order
others: Grok Bot (turn finished vs awaiting user)
Teams (banner and feed, feed only, off per channel)
Buzz (follow before first reply, per-user state synced across devices)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-05-01] 4 of 5 sources; table-stakes (low-noise defaults are Buzz-only DOC intent; the implemented limiter is Grok Bot-only SRC) [R-t1-05-04] 3 of 5 sources; table-stakes (follow and mute alone: 2 of 5 in this record set, common in real Slack)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-05-01] Slack validates one schema-checked payload (team, channel, message and thread ids plus a trace id) and runs it through display-allowed and DND gates, with telemetry for received, click, reply and action. Grok Bot's agent-turn notification carries agent id, message preview, last message id and an awaiting_user_response flag, so 'done' and 'needs you' are different signals. Teams keeps the signal enum closed (call, mention, chat, channel, other) so routing rules stay manageable. Grok Bot throttles at a minimum interval of 5000 ms and 10 per 300 s window and only notifies the active device. Buzz default: rooms silent (mentions still pass), DMs urgent-only, workflow and approval on, agent chatter off. Buzz lesson: it declared agent job kinds but never emitted them, leaving dead settings rows, so declare only signals that have a producer. [R-t1-05-04] Slack: a global level with per-conversation exceptions, separate desktop and mobile settings and a no-text-in-notifications flag mirrored into the native layer. Teams: auto-follow when mentioned, when my message gets a reply and when I reply, plus a 'replies to followed threads' setting. Buzz decision function: mention always passes, then channel mute, then thread rules (participated, followed, authored, muted roots), then slot enabled, then an alert-while-viewing check; mutes, stars and sections live in one per-user replaceable state with last-writer-wins merge across devices.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-05-01] The producer allowlist (isNotificationTypeAuthorized) lets verevon-gateway send only notification.created to the delegated user itself, support-worker its ticket and SLA types, and capability-core only modelplane.run_completed and modelplane.run_failed. mention.received is seeded in channel config but has no producer. @person mentions are inserted as plain text with no server record. There is no signal taxonomy and no deep-link contract for Space or thread. The per-user run watcher ('notify me when this run finishes') is the only Space-adjacent producer. [R-t1-05-04] notification-core has per-event by per-channel preferences and the gateway proxies them, but there is no per-room level, no hide-preview flag, no desktop and mobile split and no UI in Spaces. A grep of verevonv3 src/features found no thread follow or mute (INF); the Space definition names pause and mute only for an agent's presence in a room, not for notifications.

items.approach: [R-t1-05-01] conversation-core: persist a mention record on post (refs only, no body) and emit mention and reply events. capability-core: extend beyond run_completed and run_failed to agent_done, agent_awaiting and approval_needed. Control: emit invite. notification-core: extend isNotificationTypeAuthorized per service and signal, add the Space signal types, and define the payload as a shared contract; the body is refs-only for ZDR orgs and a preview is included only when retention mode allows (check at enqueue, matching the worker's existing refusal of async ZDR delivery). Deep link as a stable route (web path plus a verevon:// form) carrying space, thread and message ids plus the trace id. Seed defaults in notification-core config: mentions, approvals and agent-awaiting-you on; room posts and agent progress off; per-room override comes in this item (R-t1-05-04). Add a per-recipient and per-agent-sender token bucket in the router. The device-routing half of the cross-device cluster (active-device suppression) ships with push in F-t1-035 (R-t1-05-05). [R-t1-05-04] Application Plane: add space_ref-scoped preference rows and hide_preview to notification-core; store thread subscriptions beside spaceReadMarkers (per-member state already lives there); implement the Buzz decision order in the router from this item (R-t1-05-01). Register follow and mute as actions in the AI-first action registry so an agent may auto-follow on the user's behalf but can never mute a human's mentions. Frontend Plane: bell menu in the room header, follow control on threads and a Settings page that lists overrides.
dependencies: Server-side mention records in conversation-core (shared with the Messaging category)
Product decision on badge and default semantics (documented here, reused by F-t1-009 (R-t1-05-02))
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (notification-core, conversation-core) with producers in Model Plane capability-core and Control Plane
items.risks: [R-t1-05-01] Notification storms from chatty agents; ZDR preview leakage if retention mode is not checked at enqueue; defaults that are too quiet hide things until the inbox (F-t1-009 (R-t1-05-03)) exists; allowlist widening must stay per service and per type so no service can notify arbitrary recipients. [R-t1-05-04] Preference sprawl and inconsistency between room and global levels unless precedence is documented; auto-follow rules too aggressive inside agent threads; agent-driven mute must be impossible for mentions.

items.title: Cross-room attention: a server-side unread/working aggregate stream, then a Home 'needs you' inbox with Agents and Activity destinations
items.summary: Keep a per-Space latest-activity aggregate (last seq, author kind, run state) in the Application Plane, join it with the durable per-member read markers into a per-user {unread, mentions, needs_you} map pushed over the realtime stream (mark-all-read, defined badge semantics, presence and typing as ephemeral leases on the same path). Build a Home destination in the Core sidebar on top of it: a refs-only per-user ActivityItem inbox with slices (All, Mentions, Threads, Needs action, Agents, Reminders), inline reply or jump, dismiss and snooze, a capped agent 'waiting on you' lane, and cross-room Agents and Activity views. Name it so it is not confused with the existing support Inbox.
items.whyItMatters: Sidebar dots come from a browser store that only the open room fills, and Activity is room-scoped, so a person in several Spaces cannot see what needs them. A cross-room inbox is table stakes in Teams, Slack and buzz, and the agent needs-you queue (Grok Bot, QM) is its agent-era form.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Teams (typed catalog and slices); Grok Bot for the agent needs-you queue; Buzz for the open, re-implementable version; Teams (aggregation and consistency checks); Slack for badge semantics; QM (GET /v1/session-state/events: working, awaiting_approval or idle per thread plus participants, filtered server-side) for the aggregate; Buzz for presence leases; Buzz (Agents, Workflows and inbox as first-class sidebar destinations, one shared right panel); Teams for app-bar mechanics
others: QM (SSE state stream, '99+ waiting on you' badge)
Grok Bot (typed roster change events: agent created, updated, deleted, room members)
Slack (presence servers; pushes presence only for users visible on screen; DOC)
Teams (app bar with pin/unpin, See-all flyout and keyboard drag-and-drop with spoken narration)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-05-03] Inbox: 3 of 5 sources, table-stakes; agent needs-you queue: 2 of 5, differentiator [R-t1-05-02] 3 of 5 sources; table-stakes [R-t1-09-05] 3 of 5 for the cross-room stream (common); 3 of 5 for presence and typing as leases (common) [R-t1-12-02] 4 of 5 (Buzz, Slack, QM, Teams); table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-05-03] Teams materialises about 60 typed activity kinds and exposes slices (Mentions, Threads, Tag mentions, VIP, Reminders, Drafts, Saved, Requests) as saved filters with show rules. Buzz assembles the inbox fan-out-on-read (mention join plus needs-action query, capped at 100 rows) grouped by conversation root, in a list plus detail layout with filter chips and an inline reply composer. Grok Bot unifies approvals, NEEDS_INPUT tasks, hand-off requests and routine failures into one queue with a reason and dismissable trays. QM pushes {threadRef, state, participants} over one SSE stream with stale-delta rejection and refetch on resync. Buzz also collapses notes from one agent within 5 minutes into a single card; borrow that grouping rule for the Agents slice. [R-t1-05-02] Server keeps a per-member read marker per room (and per followed thread) and a per-room latest-activity aggregate. Unread equals latest activity later than last read, for rooms the user has not muted, counted only for event kinds allowed to badge. Teams aggregates missed chats, channels and activity into one hub with consistency-checked counters and typed navigation errors. The client receives a compact map over the realtime stream with a sequence number and a periodic consistency check; mark-all-read bulk-writes the markers. [R-t1-09-05] Server keeps a latest-activity aggregate per room; a per-user stream emits deltas for readable rooms; the client compares last seq with the user's read marker to compute unread. Presence key with EX 180 s against a 60 s heartbeat; typing as a 5 s window; ephemeral kinds skip the database, audit and search; agents get the same lease so a dead agent shows offline in about 3 minutes. [R-t1-12-02] File-based routes per destination; a pinned header component holds search plus fixed feature entries, below it fixed conversation groups plus user sections; a narrow rail switches tenants. Teams models the app bar as {appId, pinned, order} with a keyboard drag state machine (pickup, move, place/cancel) announced through a live region. Build as a <Rail> of route entries from a typed destinations registry, checked for permission the way QM does.

There is no cross-room inbox, no mention, reply or reaction items, no slices and no inline reply. The in-room Needs-attention lens is strong but covers approvals only: agent questions and hand-offs are not distinct item kinds, items cannot be dismissed or snoozed, and the state arrives by 6 s poll. [R-t1-05-02] A durable per-member lastReadAt exists in convex-core with sensible rules (no marker means nothing is new; your own post is never unread), but the sidebar's unread dots come from a browser-local store (publishSpaceUnread) that only the open room fills. The generic notification feed already has unread-count and mark-all-read routes, but Spaces do not feed it. [R-t1-09-05] No cross-room aggregate (SRC: the live-work store only holds rooms whose page has published; an unobserved room shows no dot, deliberately). items.approach: [R-t1-05-03] Application Plane: a per-user attention projection (extend notification-core or a sibling) storing refs only, fed by conversation-core (mentions, replies), capability-core (run finished or failed, approval awaiting, agent question, hand-off) and Control (invites). Bodies are fetched at render time through the gateway under the viewer's current ACL so ZDR rooms stay content-free and Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL. Add 'agent_question' and 'handoff' kinds beside approvals in capability-core. Frontend Plane: an Inbox route with the slices above, reusing activity-grammar salience (critical, attention, normal, muted) as the item renderer; the sidebar and nav needs-you count comes from the this item (R-t1-05-02) stream. Approvals opened from the inbox go through the existing signed Control decision flow. [R-t1-05-02] Application Plane: conversation-core maintains the per-Space latest-activity aggregate on post write; join it with spaceReadMarkers into a per-user unread map (reuse the existing unreadThreadIds rules server-side). Expose it through one SSE or WebSocket stream with sequence numbers and resync frames; QM's multiplexed session-state stream is the transport reference. Frontend Plane: sidebar counts, a 'more unread' pill and a mark-all-read action registered in the action registry; retire the browser-only unread store once the map is authoritative. Derive badge eligibility from the signal classes defined in F-t1-008 (R-t1-05-01). [R-t1-09-05] Application Plane convex-core: spaceActivity aggregate table updated from the event projection (F-t1-003 (R-t1-09-03)); gateway GET /api/v1/spaces/events as a per-user multiplexed SSE, filtered by Control read decisions (F-t1-003 (R-t1-09-02)) so aggregates never leak titles or counts for unreadable rooms. SPA publishes deltas into space-live-work.ts, which already shares one store between page, sidebar and composer. Presence and typing: keep the Convex leases (spacePresence.ts), publish deltas as ephemeral frames on the room stream, throttle in large rooms. Add the rule that anything read back later lives server-side to the Space section of CLAUDE.md and correct the stale sidebar claim in SPACE_PAGE_AUDIT section 18. The notifications category owns the unread UX (this item (R-t1-05-02)) and global presence UI (F-t1-042 (R-t1-01-09)); build one stream and one aggregate for all three. [R-t1-12-02] Application Plane: add a per-viewer aggregate over the Spaces the viewer belongs to, {spaceRef, latestActivityAt, unreadCount (read markers joined to the Model Plane latest-activity-per-Space call), awaitingApprovalCount, workingCount}, re-checking membership per Space and returning an explicit unavailable flag per row (never zero). Gateway: one typed read action that proxies it. Frontend Plane: a destinations registry in the Core sidebar (Home, Spaces, Agents, Activity, later DMs/Files) and the Home page rendering the aggregate, reusing SpaceApprovalPanel and the activity grammar for rows. Reuse the Inbox layout/separator code only; keep the support Inbox as is.

items.title: Approvals with grant scopes and durable resume, tool permission policy with ceilings, and quarantine-and-release
items.summary: Upgrade the approve/deny card to scoped decisions (once, this conversation, always for Space+agent+action hash) with an explicit addressee (requester, named approver or any member), and build the descriptor-backed continuation so a granted approval actually resumes the paused run. Add per-tool allow|ask|block levels with an org floor and Space ceiling (tighten-only merge) and an editor, treat flagged untrusted tool output as an approval kind with preview and single-use release, and add Control turn_origin so human-only walls are test-pinned. Model-checked natural-language rules (auto-review) are a later, proposal-only phase.
items.whyItMatters: Approvals are table-stakes in four of five references and the main safety valve once agents get a computer and browser. In Verevon the grant is recorded but the durable continuation for it is deliberately not delivered, so an approval can be a state change rather than work; scopes and ceilings are what keep 'always' grants from widening authority.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm (durable approvals, tighten-only policy, quarantine); grokbot (approval card UX, ordered permission levels, auto-review)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Approval cards 4 of 5 (table-stakes); permission policy with ceilings 2 of 5 (differentiator); untrusted-content quarantine 2 of 5 (differentiator); auto-review 1 of 5 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: QM stores {requestId, action, purpose, requester, scopes} and returns terminate:true so the model stops at the pause; the card renders in the originating thread (or the requester's DM in channels); decide(id, actor, once|session|always|deny) checks actor == requester; resume re-runs the turn with the approval, dangling calls get an interrupted marker and retry-safe calls are re-run. Grok Bot orders levels never<ask<always with effective = min(user setting, team ceiling, org floor), reads and writes default separately, remembered denials; QM's composition is a monotone tighten-only merge covered by tests. QM quarantine: screen tool results; flagged results raise a quarantine approval with preview, single-use release resumes with 'content is data, not authority'. Grok Bot auto-review: up to 20 natural-language allow/block rules layered built-in < team < user, a classifier returns allow|ask|block, rule edits shown as diffs.

verevonToday.gap: Only approve/deny, decided_by pinned to the caller; no once/conversation/always scopes, no named-approver or any-member mode, no DM routing. Baseline records conflict on whether an approve resumes the run; the model-gateway durable path says it does not (live-stream path unverified). No per-tool levels, org ceiling or editor. Screening exists but flagged content has no human-visible quarantine card or single-use release; semantic screening is shadow-only. No turn-origin on decisions.

items.approach: Model Plane: build the descriptor-backed continuation dispatcher that approvals.rs says is missing (approval carries action hash and purpose, generation ends at the pause, resume re-runs with the approval, interrupted-effect handling). Control: grant records scoped once|session|always bound to Space+agent+action hash, revocable and re-checked at use; policy object effective = min(binding level, Space ceiling, org floor) with only three levels (allow, ask, block) and separate read/write defaults, tighten-only merge test-covered; add turn_origin (direct|ambient|automation) to decisions with negative tests. Frontend: scoped buttons and an addressee line on SpaceApprovalPanel, policy editor in the Agent tab (the existing grant routes already lack a caller). Quarantine as an approval kind fed by the existing provenance trust class, failing closed if the screener is down. Auto-review only as a Model Plane proposal that Control still signs, never for irreversible or credential actions. Adopt the consequence-stated wording from the dropped outbound-call item (R-t1-03-12 (dropped)) for every irreversible effect: the card says what cannot be recalled before the human approves.

items.risks: 'Always' grants widening authority: bind to Space, agent and action hash, make revocable. Model-judged authorisation can be fooled: proposal only. Policy complexity: keep three levels.

items.title: Personal agents with an owner-controlled access list and add policy, a private assistant beside the room, and configurable room bindings
items.summary: Let each person own a personal agent (visibility owner/org/room, a primary-agent setting, per-user sessions) that can be invited into a room with the owner's consent and is revoked with its owner, plus a private assistant panel inside a Space with a reviewed 'share to room' escalation. Every agent definition gets an access list (owner, manager, collaborator; users first, teams and org later) and an add policy (owner_only, nobody, anyone) edited with an expected-state token; binding an agent needs the room manager role and the agent's add policy. Shared room agents become configurable per binding (model from the org-approved list, language, proactivity, thread policy).
items.whyItMatters: The brief asks for Grok-Bot-style personal agents that work like a person, and a personal Space cannot hold an agent today. Without an owner-controlled access list, a personal agent in a shared room would either be unusable or widen its owner's reach, which the Space authority rule forbids.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (personal/team agents, primary bot, clone-to-team); teams and slack (private-vs-group assistant panel with escalation); grokbot
others: buzz (personal agents as supervised local processes)
qm (session scope derived once at admission)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-07-04] Personal agents 3 of 5 (common); shared room agent 3 of 5 (common); private assistant panel 2 of 5 (differentiator); personal-to-team conversion 1 of 5 (unique) [R-t1-02-03] 2 of 5 (grokbot, buzz); differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-07-04] Grok Bot agent record with visibility OWNER|TEAM and a user MAIN_AGENT setting; the primary agent coordinates the owner's other agents and runs a proactive check-in routine; sessions keyed by (agent, user, surface); Team Bots share setup (plugins, routines, memory, computer) with isolated per-teammate sessions and per-person connector accounts; CloneAgentToTeam(personal_secret_names) -> CLONED|UNSUPPORTED|NO_TEAM excludes personal secret names and triages memory promotion. Teams channel agent config: keywords, model preference, default language, proactive help on/off, knowledge sources. Slack/Teams side panel is bound to the current context with a private session and an escalate-to-group dialog that posts a reviewed copy into the room. QM/Buzz derive SessionScope once at admission and use it as the single key for sessions, queues and cancel. [R-t1-02-03] agent_access(agent_id, principal_type user|group|team|link, principal_id, role owner|manager|collaborator) plus agent.add_policy. Binding an agent requires the room's manager role and the agent's policy (owner_only means the actor must be the agent owner). Edits carry expected_state_token; a stale token is refused with a repeat-the-change message; owner and managers are always retained.

[R-t1-02-03] Control Plane: store agent_access and add_policy as authority (agents are already service subjects in space_memberships), and make the bind decision check both the room role and the agent policy. Application Plane keeps the agent definition and a display projection; filter the installable list by the caller's add right. Frontend: access panel on the agent and policy badge in the bind dialog. Coordinate with the agents category on where agent ownership is recorded.

items.title: Audience-safe agent context and memory: source labels, audience-bound memory, owner-signed declassify, review-then-share and explicit room/team knowledge scopes
items.summary: Stamp a source-scope label on every tool result, retrieval chunk and memory record, tag every agent memory write with the Space audience (hash, revision) from the signed decision, fold context against the decision's audience, make compaction summaries inherit labels and cut context when the audience changes, and evaluate retrieval entitlement for the whole audience. Add an owner-signed declassify action, explicit opt-in before a person's personal context is used in a shared room, a private draft with Share-to-room for sensitive answers, and an explicit per-room knowledge list.
items.whyItMatters: Thread storage is audience-bound, but persistent agent memory (including Letta) is scoped by org, user or thread only, so what an agent learned in a private room can surface in a wider one. Personal agents in shared rooms make this a data-governance risk, not a nice-to-have.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz; qm (labels, audience fold, context boundary, memory notebook); teams (review-then-share UX, explicit knowledge list)
others: grokbot (runtime labelling of outbound Slack/Gmail/Outlook sends)
qm (sharing posture: Isolated by default, Open needs owner and room opt-in, live membership re-check)

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-10-02] Agent flow control: 2 of 5 (buzz draft design, grokbot); sharing posture: 1 of 5 (qm); label propagation: 1 of 5 (teams, partial). Differentiator. [R-t1-07-08] Audience-safe disclosure 4 of 5 (table-stakes); context assembly/compaction 4 of 5 (table-stakes); memory 3 of 5 (common); per-room knowledge scope 1 of 5 (unique, Teams)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-10-02] Each agent instance is bound to one audience. Memory entries carry an audience label and a membership epoch; a read is allowed only when the target audience is a subset of the source audience, unless the owner explicitly declassifies. Outbound tool sends are classified internal, external or self and sampled for review. Sharing defaults to Isolated; Open requires an owner opt-in on the resource plus a room opt-in, re-checked against live membership at turn time. Derived content takes the maximum label of its sources. [R-t1-07-08] QM stores a scopeLabel on every transcript entry; filterHistoryForAudience keeps an entry only if all audience members are entitled; a context snapshot fingerprints scope plus sorted audience ids and when it changes throughSeq moves to the latest seq and older entries are dropped from replay; resource handles only if every member is entitled; compaction summaries record throughSeq, scope label and a tainted flag so they cannot leak to a narrower audience. Teams: if entitlement cannot be verified for all recipients the answer is a private draft to the requester with a warning and an 'Allow to send to the group' button; knowledge_resources[] requires membership in the source, removal deletes derived knowledge and re-add starts from zero. QM memory: per-scope revisioned notebook with records {id, text, sensitivity ordinary|unknown|sensitive|restricted, source scope/session}, a helper model classifies and the strictest label wins, recall filtered by audience disclosure policy, editor with compare-and-swap and restore.
