items.approach: [R-t1-10-02] Model Plane session-core: add space_ref, audience_hash and audience_revision to agent_memory (new migration), set them at write time from the decision claims, filter at retrieval with the subset rule, and treat user or org scope memory read inside a Space as personal context that needs a Control decision. letta-bridge must apply the same filter. Control user-core: add context_shares (resource, Space, owner opt-in, expiry) and a declassify decision type that is owner-signed and audited. Frontend: a panel that shows which personal context the agent may use in this room, with opt-in and declassify. Outbound: integration-corev2 tags each send by recipient domain versus org and writes it to audit. Later phase: Control defines label taxonomy, Data Plane documents and Spaces carry a label, Model computes output label as the maximum of input labels and the Application Plane stores it on the message. [R-t1-07-08] Model Plane Session Core: stamp the source scope on every tool result, retrieval chunk and memory record; filter replay by the decision audience (entry kept only if all members entitled); compaction summary inherits the label and a tainted flag; move throughSeq when the audience hash changes. Data v2 retrieval: evaluate entitlement for the whole audience (intersection) and return handles only if every member is entitled. Frontend: private 'only you can see this' draft with Share to room and a visible 'withheld because a member lacks access' state. Memory and knowledge: follow the S3.1 split (Data v2 owns authored Space/personal memory documents with revision history and explicit shared-to-personal promotion; Model owns learned memory and the resolver) and settle that ADR first because the existing memory enum lives in capability-core; add a space scope keyed by the Control space_ref, records with sensitivity and provenance, a memory tab with restore, a binding knowledge_scope referencing Data v2 collections with a deletion saga on removal. ZDR orgs get no durable memory. Never auto-copy room facts into personal memory.
dependencies: Data v2 retrieval ACL per principal and per audience
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (session-core memory, letta-bridge, compaction, labels); Data Plane v2 (retrieval entitlement); Control Plane (declassify decision)
items.risks: [R-t1-10-02] Memory becomes less useful when partitioned, so declassify must be cheap. Membership epoch changes must invalidate labels correctly. Letta semantic memory may not be partitionable without bridge work. Label taxonomy can be over-applied (everything confidential). [R-t1-07-08] Over-filtering can make answers useless: needs a clear withheld state. Cross-room leakage and ZDR conflict for memory. Must never widen an owner-plane ACL.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t1-07-08] S3.1 authored context with split ownership in docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md:1943-1952; knowledge_scope is explicitly deferred in the Application binding schema.

items.title: Room attachments and file library: paste, drop and attach through presigned Data Plane documents with Space provenance, scan and typed refusals, plus a Files view
items.summary: Let members paste, drop or attach images, audio, video and files in a room. The gateway checks the room decision and size/type policy and returns a presigned slot against a Data Plane document carrying space_ref, created-in Space, human or agent creator, mime, size and content hash; a complete step scans, hashes and thumbnails and attaches the document id to the entry. Reads are served by id under the room check, refusals are typed, and the Knowledge tab gains a Files view. Space-bound writes use a Control-signed Space decision, not the legacy unscoped chat upload.
items.whyItMatters: Attachments are table stakes in all five references, and a work room without files cannot carry real work. The /chat upload accepts only JSON text with a hard-coded ZDR class and no space_ref, so it cannot simply be reused.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (content-addressed media with metadata stripping); slack (3-step external upload plus malware scan); grokbot (typed size policy and refusal reasons); QM (SRC) for the model; Teams (REA) as the product benchmark
others: Buzz (SRC): thumbnails/blurhash and snapshot-based storage accounting
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-04] 5 of 5 sources (table-stakes) [R-t1-08-03] 4 of 5 sources; table-stakes (some evidence sits in records clustered elsewhere, per the comparator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-04] Step 1: request an upload slot (gateway checks room ACL and size/type policy) and receive a presigned URL plus file_id. Step 2: the client PUTs bytes directly to storage. Step 3: complete: scan for malware, sha256 the content, strip client metadata, generate thumbnail and blurhash, attach to the entry. Reads are by id with a room ACL check. Refusals are typed (empty, too_large, count, type) so the client can explain them. [R-t1-08-03] Direct upload to object storage keyed by sha256, then register a FileArtifact {id, owner_scope, created_in_scope (the room), created_by (human or agent), path, mime, size, sha256}. The room library lists files created in or granted to the room. Teams makes the channel a folder with one storage authority for ACL and compliance; thumbnails are generated asynchronously and quota is counted by an off-path worker.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-01-04] The room composer has no file input, paste or drop. /api/v1/chat/documents and /extract exist for Chat but Space does not use them; the Knowledge tab only lists documents that already carry space_ref, read-only. [R-t1-08-03] The Knowledge tab lists documents with space_ref read-only and the composer has no attach, upload or file code (grep finds none). The /chat upload accepts only JSON {title, content} text, hard-codes zdr_classification internal and sends no space_ref, so it neither handles binary files nor carries Space authority. The ephemeral extract route (documents.rs:14-33) stores nothing. No raw-bytes object store was found in documents-api-go (grep for presign, PutObject, minio, blob found nothing; the Ingestion-plane imports service was not searched), so retaining original files is a gap to confirm.

items.approach: [R-t1-01-04] Data Plane v2: document upload accepting space_ref and an entry link, malware scan, hashing and thumbnails. Frontend Plane gateway: routes under /api/v1/spaces/{space_ref}/attachments (slot, complete, read by id) that perform the Control ACL check and typed refusals; bytes never pass through the gateway. Session Core entries reference attachment ids in metadata, never bytes. Frontend: attach button, paste and drop in SpaceRoomComposer, preview chips with per-file progress and refusal messages. Keep one document ACL path so Space membership never grants read of an owner-plane document beyond the attachment itself. [R-t1-08-03] Data Plane documents-api owns bytes or extract plus metadata: space_ref, created_by principal (human|agent), mime, size, sha256, extraction status. Follow the already-built connector-import pattern (plan S1.5): browser sends only a spaceRef, the gateway asks Control for a Space decision, Imports Core runs extraction with a space_import_intent, and Documents API verifies the signed decision (space_import.go). Frontend: attach control in SpaceRoomComposer, Files view inside the Knowledge tab, attachments in messages as document-id pointers resolved under the viewer's own grant. Phase 1 stores the extract (Grok Bot style) and shows a download card only if bytes are retained; phase 2 adds an object store for originals, thumbnails, malware scan and quota. ZDR orgs: use only the ephemeral extract and mark the file session-only. Reuse the viewer registry from F-t1-014 (R-t1-08-02).
dependencies: Data Plane document upload accepting space_ref
Gateway presign routes with Control ACL check
F-t1-046 (R-t1-01-07) so agents can use the files
Control Space decision issuer for documents:write in shared Spaces (the plan's import issuer derives personal-Space membership and import_write_entitled is deny-by-default)
F-t1-057 (R-t1-08-04) phase 1 so a Space-attached file does not widen the uploader's ACL
items.planeOwner: Data Plane v2 (documents) with Frontend Plane (gateway presign routes, composer, Files view) and Control Plane (Space write decision)
items.risks: [R-t1-01-04] ACL widening (a room member reading owner-plane documents); ZDR retention of uploaded files; storage cost and abuse limits; malware and decompression bombs. Overlaps category 08 (room file library, C-t1-08-011/012): build one pipeline. [R-t1-08-03] The comparator estimated M assuming the chat upload could be reused; it is text-only and unscoped, so L is more honest. An attachment in a shared room must not grant access beyond the uploader's intent. Malware scanning and ZDR conflict with durable files. Binary storage may not exist yet (needs verification).

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t1-01-04] Owner plane is named as Data Plane documents with space_ref (Knowledge tab already reads documents.space_ref); no Space upload path exists in code. [R-t1-08-03] apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md:1660-1690 (S1.5 slices 2-4: Data doc/file binding to Space and signed import decisions, source-wired for connector imports). Data side only; no room upload or attachment UI is planned.

items.title: Bring agent-produced artifacts and the shared viewer registry into the Space room
items.summary: Mount the artifact panel that /chat already ships inside the Space room, with a room-level Artifacts list, and persist artifacts emitted by Space runs as shared, revisioned objects. Extract the per-kind viewers into one registry reused by the timeline, the artifacts panel and the Files view, adding lazy DOCX and XLSX preview. Add an artifact-first instruction to Space agent bindings so analyses and documents land as artifacts instead of long posts.
items.whyItMatters: This is the visible proof of the human-plus-agent hybrid: agents deliver work as inspectable objects while the shared timeline stays short. It is mostly reuse of shipped chat code, so it has high impact for moderate effort.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (SRC): a packaged rule routes standalone analyses into a canvas, backed by canvas/document read and write tools; lazy viewers for PDF, DOCX, XLSX, code and Mermaid
others: QM (SRC): validated self-contained HTML playgrounds as typed tool results, offered only to surfaces that can render them
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: artifacts in room: 2 of 5; inline viewers: 2 of 5; both differentiators
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Agent tool create_or_update_artifact {id, kind, title, content, version}; a system-prompt rule routes deliverables to it; the server validates HTML (no network, no external assets) before registering; the client shows a side panel with a revision stepper and a sandboxed iframe for HTML; the tool is withheld from surfaces without a renderer. Viewer registry keyed by mime/kind with lazy chunks (pdf worker, docx to HTML, sheet to table, per-language highlighter, Mermaid) and size thresholds that fall back to a download card.

verevonToday.gap: Shipped in /chat only: artifact panel with kind-based viewers, revision stepper, sandboxed HTML iframe, DOCX/PPTX/XLSX export. Artifacts arrive as inline SSE payloads {id, kind, title, content, version}, not as persisted objects. A grep of the Space components finds no artifact panel; the room renders Markdown only. In-browser DOCX/XLSX preview was not seen (INF, not exhaustively checked).

items.approach: Frontend Plane: render ChatArtifactPanel (or its extracted core) in the Space room and add a room-level Artifacts list; move the per-kind viewers behind a shared registry used by the Space timeline, artifacts panel and the Files view in F-t1-013 (R-t1-08-03), lazy-loading DOCX/XLSX/PDF viewers and falling back to a download card by size. Model Plane: persist artifacts emitted by Space-bound runs as thread-owned revisions in Session Core under the same shared-read decision as the turn (same id with a higher version is an update, as chat-artifacts.ts already defines), and add an artifact-first rule to Space agent bindings. Add a Promote to canvas action that writes the artifact as a canvas version (F-t1-015 (R-t1-08-01)), matching the plan's idea of promoting selected output through Data artifact APIs (S3.3). Under ZDR keep artifacts session-only and say so in the UI. Keep the existing HTML sandbox.
dependencies: Shared read of Space turns (deny-by-default per-org space_effect_policies rows per the comparator; not re-verified)
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (UI); Model Plane Session Core (persistence)
items.risks: Persisted artifacts must follow the same shared-read decision as the turn or they become a read bypass. HTML and PDF artifacts are untrusted, so keep the sandboxed iframe and CSP. Bundle size from lazy viewers. Room turns may already render charts through ChatMarkdown (INF).

items.title: Room canvas: a shared, revisioned Space document that humans and agents co-author
items.summary: Add a Canvas tab to the Space cockpit backed by a Data Plane versioned page (Markdown first, block comments and live co-edit later). Every save is an append-only version stamped with the human or agent principal and an expected-head precondition checked in the same transaction, with history, diff and restore. Agents read and write it through a Model Plane document tool under the run's delegated Space decision.
items.whyItMatters: Four of five references have a room document and Verevon has none, so agents must post plans, minutes and decisions as long chat messages and humans have no durable place to co-author with them. Head CAS is what stops an agent run from silently overwriting a human edit once both write to the same artifact.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack canvas (DOC) for the document model; Buzz (SRC) for append-only revisions with a server-side expected-head check
others: Teams notes pane and Loop pages (REA)
Grok Bot room canvases plus file locks and tombstone undelete (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: canvas: 4 of 5 sources, table-stakes; write safety (CAS/locks): 2 of 5, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Room-scoped document {doc_id, space_ref, head_revision, body}; each save is a full revision with author principal and expected_head, applied as one INSERT ... WHERE current_head = expected_head that returns a typed conflict (missing, mismatched, not superseding); the losing text stays in history; restore writes a new revision copying an old body. History panel lists revisions newest first with a diff against head. Buzz replaces the whole body under CAS, which is enough for a first version; Slack and Teams add rich blocks, block-anchored comments and CRDT co-edit. Grok Bot adds lock/renew/release with fencing tokens and tombstone undelete with typed outcomes for agent leases.

verevonToday.gap: No Space-authored document and no Canvas tab (the cockpit has six tabs: chat, work, knowledge, activity, agent, members). The Studio canvas is gateway-memory only and lost on restart. Data Plane wiki-store already has pages, append-only versions with proposed_by_user/proposed_by_agent, a diff route and a proposal/approve flow, but CreateVersion locks the page row and always advances the head (no expected-head precondition, no restore), pages are keyed by workspace_id not Space, and the gateway proxies wiki-store only for operating-map actions. The Convex planner document store keeps an opaque state blob with last-write-wins saveState and no v3 consumer.

items.approach: Data Plane: extend wiki-store-go as the canvas store (SRC: it already has versions, diff, proposals and RequireDurableWritesAllowed). Add an expected_version_id precondition to CreateVersion with a typed conflict, a restore operation that writes a new version, and a Space binding that resolves SpaceRef to the page workspace through space_retrieval_bindings and verifies a Control Space decision header the way documents-api verifies X-Space-Import-Decision (space_import.go:14-60). The adoption plan already assigns this ownership (S3.1 slice 2: Data owns revisioned Space knowledge documents with CAS, history, restore). Gateway: add /api/v1/spaces/{ref}/canvas routes. Frontend: Canvas tab in SpaceCockpit (extend SpaceTabId), Markdown editor first, history, diff and restore reusing the chat DiffView, conflict banner that shows the losing text. Application Plane: only the Space-to-canvas pointer and presence. Model Plane: a document read/write tool that writes under the run's delegated decision and stamps the agent principal; for human-authored sections route agent writes through the existing proposal/review path. Later phases: block comments, presence via Convex spacePresence, CRDT co-edit (the Convex planner state blob is a possible layer, not the system of record), and agent file leases with fencing tokens only if multi-step agent edits need them.
dependencies: Control Space decision issuer for document writes in shared Spaces (adoption plan S1.2/S1.5 describe issuers that derive personal-Space membership today)
F-t1-057 (R-t1-08-04) phase 1: edit role and Space subject in resource_grants
items.planeOwner: Data Plane (wiki-store-go versions); Frontend Plane UI; Application Plane pointer; Model Plane agent tool
items.risks: Canvas text becomes prompt content, so it must be framed as untrusted data (F-t1-032 (R-t1-08-08)). ZDR callers are rejected for every wiki mutation (authctx.go:226), so ZDR orgs get no canvas and the UI must say so. Version-per-save bloat needs debounce or coalescing. Live CRDT co-edit is a large step beyond CAS-with-reload. wiki_pages has no space_ref column, so correctness rests on the binding table.

alreadyPlanned.where: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md:1943-1948 (S3.1 slice 2: Data-owned revisioned Space knowledge documents with CAS, history, restore). Backend intent only; the S3.1-S3.6 block is still [~] and no room-visible canvas UI or agent write tool is planned.

items.title: Direct messages and group DMs on Space authority, with conversation kind deciding agent scope and history window
items.summary: Add dm and group-DM Space kinds with a fixed roster and a participant_hash that makes the same set of people always resolve to one conversation, hideable per viewer and resurfaced on new activity. Derive the agent scope from the conversation kind (a DM with my agent maps to my personal scope, group DM to a group scope, a room to the room scope) and let the person who adds a member to a group DM choose how much history that member may read.
items.whyItMatters: One-to-one and small-group chat is an immediate Teams/Slack expectation and is absent. Modelling DMs as small Spaces keeps one authority path (Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL), lets a person DM a colleague or an agent, and gives a clear rule for which memory, files and sandbox an agent may use in which conversation.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (DM identity by participant hash); qm (scope mapping by conversation kind); teams (history-sharing choice)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: DMs 4 of 5 sources (table-stakes); scope by kind 2 of 5 (differentiator); history choice 1 of 5 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: buzz: an open-DM event lists participants; the server computes participant_hash over the sorted member ids, unique per org, and returns the existing DM if one exists; cap 9 participants; hide is a per-viewer projection cleared when new activity arrives. qm: conversationScope() maps dm to personal(actor), group to group:<ref>, anything else to channel:<ref>; each thread is its own session inside the scope, and memory, files, sandbox and crons attach to the scope. Teams: adding a person to a group chat carries a history choice (none, last N days, all) and a system message narrates it.

verevonToday.gap: Space kinds are personal|room|project|case in both Control (CHECK constraint) and Convex; the create route accepts only personal and room and refuses the rest. No DM kind, route or one-to-one flow; a personal Space cannot hold other members or an agent. Audience-revision filtering exists (the right primitive) but no adder-chosen history window was found (low confidence, inferred from baseline).

items.approach: Control Plane (user-core): extend registered_spaces.space_kind CHECK with dm (and group_dm) in a migration, add participant_hash unique per org, fixed roster with no role escalation, scope derivation (dm with an agent maps to the caller's personal scope; allow an agent binding in a personal Space). Application Plane: add the kind to the Convex spaces.kind union, a per-viewer hide row cleared on new activity, and a sidebar DM section. Gateway: accept the new kinds in the create route (spaces.rs:2873) and reuse the transcript, presence, typing and read paths unchanged. Model Plane: sessions per thread carry the scope ref. History window: the member-add grant carries history_from (none | timestamp | all), enforced in the Session Core read filter (grpc.rs:5340-5360) and in retrieval; narrated by a system entry (F-t1-052 (R-t1-01-10)).
dependencies: Control Space kind registration and membership grant schema change
F-t1-052 (R-t1-01-10) system messages for narrating member and history changes
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (user-core) with Application Plane projections and Model Plane scope refs
items.risks: A DM with an agent must bind to the caller's personal scope or it leaks agent context into shared conversations. Group-DM member add needs the history window enforced in retrieval indexes too. Migration of existing personal Spaces. Hiding a DM must not remove membership.

items.title: Message lifecycle and reactions: edit and delete as revision entries (owner-of-agent retract, revisions reach the agent), emoji reactions and a per-message action toolbar
items.summary: Add edited and deleted revision entries in Session Core (never in-place overwrite), allowed for the author, the owner of the authoring agent, or a Space admin under policy, rendered with an edited marker or tombstone and written to audit; when the entry is already in model-visible history, append a message_revision entry so the agent sees the change. Add per-user emoji reactions keyed by (thread, seq) and a hover/focus toolbar (quick reactions, copy, edit, delete, pin, quote, fork); phase 2 makes reactions typed agent events and lets agents react through a capped tool.
items.whyItMatters: Reactions (5 of 5) and edit/delete (4 of 5) are among the most basic room behaviours and are absent from proto, gateway, Convex and UI. QM's revision entries and buzz's owner-of-agent retract make them safe in a room where agents read history.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (owner-of-agent authority, soft-deleted events kept in audit); qm (revision entries to the agent); buzz (reaction table and events); qm (reactions to and from agents); slack (product reference)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-05] Edit/delete 4 of 5 sources (table-stakes); revision propagation to the agent only in qm (unique) [R-t1-01-06] Reactions 5 of 5 sources (table-stakes); reactions as agent input/output 2 of 5 (differentiator); per-message action surfaces 2 of 5 recorded (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-05] An edit is a new revision event referencing the target; a delete is a tombstone event; permission is self-author, or viewer owns the authoring agent, or admin; originals stay in an append-only audit store subject to retention. Slack and Teams add admin policy flags (allow user edit / allow user delete). qm appends a message_revision system entry (action, target_seq, text) outside a turn under the session lease, and the prompt builder renders it as <message-edited> or <message-deleted>. [R-t1-01-06] reactions(target_entry, subject, emoji, created_at, removed_at) unique on (target, subject, emoji); toggle is idempotent; counts return with the timeline; a real-time event fires on change. qm: a reaction on an agent entry passes a policy gate (shouldSurfaceReaction) and becomes ambient turn input {reaction, target_seq, by}; agents emit reactions through a typed tool capped at 5 per turn; a cheap helper model can pick an acknowledgement emoji. grokbot adds explicit feedback votes (up, down, submit, revert). slack: role=toolbar per message with roving focus and a more-menu; clipboard writes text/html, text/plain and image in one item.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-01-05] No edit or message-delete RPC in Session Core (only whole-thread DeleteThread/DeleteThreads/DeleteSpaceThreads) and no Space route for it; only an owner can delete a whole thread through Chat. Therefore no revision propagation to the agent. [R-t1-01-06] No reaction or emoji anywhere in Session Core, the gateway Space routes, Convex or the Space UI (no matches under apps/Application Plane other than unrelated conversation-core consumers). The only per-post actions are Reply and Pin buttons on the post card (checked this audit); no hover toolbar, context menu or rich copy. A chat feedback route exists (chat.rs:69-72) but the Space feature does not use it.

items.approach: [R-t1-01-05] Model Plane Session Core: revision entry kind (edited, deleted, target_seq) appended with the Space decision, folded at read time under audience-revision filtering; the prompt builder renders revisions for entries already in model-visible history. Control Plane: org and Space policy flags for edit and delete (with an optional edit window), the authority check for owner-of-agent via the agent binding, and an audit event. Gateway: PATCH/DELETE routes on /api/v1/spaces/{space_ref}/threads/{thread_id}/messages/{seq}. Frontend: actions in the message toolbar (this item (R-t1-01-06)) and an edited marker or tombstone row. ZDR: replace content with a tombstone and keep no original beyond retention; send the model only a deleted marker, never the old text. [R-t1-01-06] Application Plane (Convex): spaceReactions table (space_ref, thread_id, entry_seq, subject_id, emoji, removed_at) unique per (entry, subject, emoji); gateway route toggles after the Control membership check; counts ride with the transcript read and a Convex subscription pushes changes; rows hold only an emoji, so they are content-free under ZDR. Frontend: MessageActions component (role=toolbar, roving focus) with the quick-react row, emoji picker, and the more-menu that later hosts edit, delete, pin, quote and fork. Phase 2 Model Plane: reaction-as-input event type gated by Space policy (default off; cap 5 per turn) and a react tool for agents; map thumbs up/down on agent turns to the existing chat feedback route. Defer custom emoji and :shortcode: completion to the composer work; do not add a third-party GIF proxy (data egress).
dependencies: F-t1-001 (R-t1-01-01) Space append path and stable entry seq ids
Control policy flags and audit event for edit/delete
Stable entry ids (thread_id, seq) exposed to the UI
F-t1-001 (R-t1-01-01) so humans can be reacted to as well as agents
Phase 2 needs a Model Plane reaction event type
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (Session Core revisions) with Application Plane (reactions table), Control Plane (policy and audit) and Frontend Plane (toolbar)
items.risks: [R-t1-01-05] Agent context diverges if revisions are not propagated. Compliance retention of originals conflicts with ZDR and must be an explicit per-org rule. Deleting an entry an agent already acted on does not undo its effects; show that in the tombstone. [R-t1-01-06] Reacting to content the reactor cannot read (check audience). Accidental agent wakeups and cost, so the gate defaults off. A reaction must never stand in for a Control approval of an effect. Third-party GIF providers conflict with ZDR.

items.title: Permission-checked message search: Session Core index with per-hit re-authorization and ZDR exclusion, in-room scoped search on Ctrl/Cmd+F and open-in-context
items.summary: Add a keyword index over Space thread messages in Session Core and a SearchSpaceMessages call plus gateway route; the index only proposes candidates, every hit is re-authorized against the Control room-read decision and audience revision, and ZDR or privacy-restricted turns are never indexed. In the room, Ctrl/Cmd+F opens a search with a removable scope chip (room, thread, person, global), and hits open in context through thread and entry deep links plus cursor paging of the thread list.
items.whyItMatters: There is no message, thread or room search at all; four references treat permission-aware search as table stakes, and a room people work in for months is unusable without it. The index must not ship before Session Core enforces ZDR.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz; teams
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-04-01] 4 of 5 sources; table-stakes [R-t1-04-02] 4 of 5 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-04-01] Postgres STORED generated tsvector column (simple config) on the message table with a GIN index; sensitive kinds produce a NULL tsvector so they never match; every query requires a tenant/community id. The engine reads candidates in pages of about 100 ordered by ts_rank, re-fetches each through a scoped fetcher and applies the access predicate per hit, so a page can be shorter than the limit. A prefix mode (to_tsquery with :*) serves typeahead. Teams adds suggestions, search-history and click-feedback endpoints and a query-alteration (spelling) field, which inform the API shape only. [R-t1-04-02] Teams offers channel, chat, community, thread, post and a people-centred scope (files, messages, images with a person), each discoverable from autosuggest with a shortcut hint. Slack routes the native Find command to in-app search; buzz shows a removable scope chip. Esc or backspace on the chip widens to global search; people-centred mode filters by author or participant id.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-04-01] No Space, thread or message search route or index exists. Gateway search.rs routes are web, image, video, suggest and answer (Quarry-backed) only (SRC, re-read in this step), and conversation search exists only for the support inbox. The pieces a hit needs to open in context are also missing (see this item (R-t1-04-02)). [R-t1-04-02] Only a client-side filter over room names and the selected room's thread titles and previews exists. It never searches message bodies, other rooms, one thread or a person, and Ctrl+F is not routed to it. Thread deep links (?thread_id=) are generated in activity-grammar.ts but no code under src/features/spaces reads a search param (grep in this step), and the thread list has no paging, so a hit could not be opened in context.

items.approach: [R-t1-04-01] Session Core (Model Plane): add a generated tsvector plus GIN index over message text on origin=space threads, NULL for turns stamped ZDR or privacy-restricted; add gRPC SearchSpaceMessages(space_id, query, filters{authors, since, until, is, has}, cursor) returning {thread_id, message_seq, snippet with highlights, author, ts}. Candidates are paged by rank and filtered with the same audience-revision predicate the room transcript read already uses (spaces.rs space_thread_transcript, which Session Core enforces by dropping rows newer than the decision revision). Gateway adds GET /api/v1/spaces/{ref}/search that obtains the Control read decision exactly as the transcript route does and forwards it; client-supplied scope is never trusted. Start keyword-only; evaluate stemming for Norwegian/English mixes (simple config has none). [R-t1-04-02] Frontend Plane: scope chip plus Ctrl/Cmd+F handler in SpacePage calling the this item (R-t1-04-01) gateway route with space_id (and thread_id or author filters). Keep the sidebar filter for instant title matching and fall through to server results. Make SpacePage consume ?thread_id=&seq= (scroll to and highlight the message) and add cursor paging with jump-to-message to the thread read path. Offer a fallback to the browser find bar when in-app search is unavailable.

Reuse of the Control room-read decision and audience-revision predicate (spaces.rs:2616-2736)
Non-owner reply fix if search should also cover replies by other members
Thread list cursor paging and deep-link consumption in SpacePage

items.title: Let room agents call Space actions themselves (agent self-API with run-bound grants)
items.summary: Admit a vetted subset of the typed spaces.* actions, plus new agent-oriented ones (create thread, post card, schedule follow-up, pin or rename a thread, pause self), to the model-executable set so a room agent can do what a human member can without a bespoke tool per action. Model Plane consumes the Frontend action registry as a staged-disclosure tool catalogue, Control Plane mints run-bound capability grants, and the gateway dispatcher re-checks the delegating human's ACL on every call; risky actions route to the existing in-room approval card.
items.whyItMatters: This is the core of 'agents that work like a human': today a room agent can only talk, because none of the 14 registered spaces.* actions is model-eligible. qm and buzz show the payoff (agents organise threads, schedule their own follow-ups, invite or pin) and Verevon already has the right catalogue shape (typed registry with risk level and owner plane per action), so the cost is low relative to the value.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 sources; differentiator (absent from the human-chat incumbents)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: qm serves a discoverable /v1/apis catalogue: API families with guidance text and eligibility predicates (role, feature flag). The runtime signs a capability token per durable run (claims: org, principal, session, run attempt, expiry; 48 h default) sent as x-agent-capability, and every handler re-verifies the principal's authority per call, so admin work reuses the same handlers. Buzz mirrors every action as a JSON-in/JSON-out CLI subcommand over signed events, the most ergonomic shape for shell-driven agents.

verevonToday.gap: MODEL_EXECUTABLE_ACTION_IDS holds 8 entries (tickets.create, inbox.*, chat.*, org.*) and none of the 14 spaces.* actions. The admission bar is strict by design: owner-issued durable receipt, idempotent fencing and forged-call denial proven on both sides (SRC, model-eligibility.ts header). Model Gateway's inline read lane deliberately has no write actions because it has no approval gate. The Space action catalogue endpoint is human-only with no UI consumer, and there is no run-bound grant for agent-originated Space actions. Several existing actions (add/remove member, revoke agent, request deletion) must stay human-only; the plan (S3.6) says agents may request use but never change future authority. The most agent-useful actions (create thread, schedule follow-up) are not registry actions yet (INF).

items.approach: Model Plane (capability-core / execution-core): list eligible registry actions to the agent with staged disclosure (as mcp_catalog does) and dispatch them through the governed agentic path, not the read-only inline loop. Control Plane: add a run-bound grant decision (principal, Space, run id, action allowlist, expiry) following the existing model.cron.create / model.cron.fire decision pattern. Frontend gateway dispatcher: accept the grant, re-derive the delegating human's membership from Control and audit exactly like a UI call. Admit actions one at a time under the model-eligibility.ts bar, starting with low-risk idempotent ones (update_thread_presentation, set_agent_state for itself, new create_thread and schedule actions); keep membership, role, deletion and credential-grant changes human-only and send medium/high-risk calls to the approval card via approval continuation. Optional later: a thin JSON CLI for sandboxed agent computers (buzz style) over the same dispatcher.
dependencies: Per-action admission under the model-eligibility.ts bar (owner receipt, idempotency, forged-call denial)
New agent-oriented spaces.* actions in the registry
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (catalogue and dispatch); Control Plane mints grants; Frontend Plane owns the action registry
items.risks: Prompt injection driving membership, role or visibility changes; destructive actions must stay approval-gated and audited; Space access must never widen the owner-plane ACL, so the grant must intersect with the delegating human's authority on every call.

items.title: Room-scoped agent browser: space_ref on browser runs, a live preview card that expands to an interactive view, hand-off and take-over with a control indicator
items.summary: Add a space_ref to the browser run start request and authorize it with a Control decision for the room audience, show browser steps and evidence as room cards, and let the room watch the session as a glanceable preview card that expands to an interactive modal (screen switcher, 'control: agent | you' badge, idle pause) in the AuxPane. Add a hand-off request (id plus instruction), Take control and I'm done, and bot-wall detection that hands off instead of retrying. Quarry still executes every action; the Model only proposes.
items.whyItMatters: The brief asks for agents that work like a person with their own browser. Browser runs exist and the gateway already serves live frames with human takeover, but nothing is Space-scoped, so the room cannot see, attribute or govern the agent's browsing.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm (browser model grant); grokbot (hosted browser, live takeover, bot-wall detection); Grok Bot (preview card to interactive modal, multi-screen, control owner badge)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-07-06] Agent browser 2 of 5 (differentiator); live view and take-over 1 of 5 (unique); teach by demonstration 1 of 5 (unique) [R-t1-12-08] 1 of 5 (Grok Bot); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-07-06] QM core mints a capability token {browserModel, browserAccount, aud browser-model}; the browser runner calls an OpenAI-style completions endpoint at core, so it never holds a provider key; 409 if the person's account or model changed; sign-in profiles are held as credentials and shown only in DMs. Grok Bot classifies bot-check walls from URL/title and hands off instead of retrying; LiveState carries box_handoff_request_id plus an instruction; EndHandoff trigger BUTTON|VIEWER_CLOSED|DISMISSED; the live view is an embedded noVNC page with token-to-header injection, phase reporting and pause when hidden. Grok Bot teach mode: recording START|SAVE|DISCARD, the saved recording is sent as a message with initiator TEACH_RECORDING so a skill is authored in chat. [R-t1-12-08] Computer view modes {preview, interactive}: preview is a periodic frame or low-rate VNC stream in a card; the modal is interactive VNC with a screen switcher and a control-owner badge (agent or you); an idle pause with wake and retry; a REC overlay while recording.

No hand-off request primitive and no bot-wall classification. [R-t1-12-08] Nothing is reachable from a Space and there is no per-agent computer; the takeover browser and run screenshots are reusable building blocks only.

items.approach: [R-t1-07-06] Model Plane model-gateway: add space_ref to BrowserRunStartRequest and thread it into the run's Space context (the chat/invoke path already does this via ThreadSpaceContext). Control: a browser-run decision bound to the room audience hash/revision; Model proposes browser actions and Quarry-v2 executes or rejects them under the grant (architecture rule). Show only to members entitled to read the run, never share credentials across members, and do not retain frames beyond policy.

items.title: Agent computer confinement: real network enforcement and resource caps, audience-bound egress, one SSRF-safe connector
items.summary: Finish the agent-computer boundary. First, make egress real: run processes whose policy allows domains in a network namespace whose only route is the egress proxy (today the executor only checks that a proxy variable is set), add cgroup or rlimit caps, apply the seccomp or Landlock layers that the code comments name, and require a sandbox-manager lease for every Space agent. Second, compute an effective egress allowlist per room from the audience snapshot (intersection of members' lists, union of denies), bind it into the signed decision and enforce it in Quarry and the sandbox proxy with audited allow and deny. Third, share one SSRF-safe connector for unfurls, webhooks and agent fetches.
items.whyItMatters: Grok-Bot-style agent computers are part of the Space vision, and confinement is the real security boundary under every softer control. A room-aware egress rule fits 'Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL': an agent acting for a room must not reach a destination any member's org forbids.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Sandbox confinement: 1 of 5 (grokbot); egress policy: 2 of 5 (grokbot, qm); SSRF-safe fetch: 2 of 5 (buzz, grokbot). Differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A launcher takes a declarative policy {type: readonly or workspace read-write, writable roots, network: none or proxy}; on Linux it uses bubblewrap, Landlock and seccomp plus a cgroup v2 attach per process with OOM reset, and file APIs resolve real paths and refuse anything outside the root. For rooms, audienceEgressFloor intersects every member's allowlists and unions denies, binds the result to the turn and logs decisions at the proxy. SSRF: resolve the host, require a global unicast address (reject private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, mapped and NAT64 forms), connect to the pinned IP with the original SNI, re-validate on redirects.

apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/browser_egress_proxy.rs and apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/tests/ssrf_forward_not_fetch.rs (exist; not read in depth)
verevonToday.gap: Filesystem confinement fails closed, which is good. The gaps are: domain allowlisting is advisory for any process that ignores proxy settings, there are no CPU, memory or pid caps and no syscall filter, a lease is not mandatory for Space agents, egress is not computed from the room audience, and there is no single SSRF-safe connector (unverified).

items.approach: Model Plane execution-core: for AllowDomains use a netns whose only reachable address is the egress proxy (without CAP_SYS_ADMIN this needs a design spike, so test on the production image), add rlimit or cgroup caps per spawn, and apply a seccomp profile; make a sandbox-manager lease mandatory for Space agents and release it on run end. Control Plane user-core: add effective_egress to the effect policy computed from the audience snapshot and bind it into the decision. Quarry (Ingestion Plane) and the sandbox proxy enforce it and write allow and deny events to audit. A shared Rust connector crate in Quarry (resolve, check, pin, re-validate redirects) is reused by the gateway link-preview path and execution-core web tools.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (execution-core, sandbox-manager) with Ingestion Plane (Quarry) and Control Plane (egress floor)
items.risks: Network namespace plus proxy plumbing is hard without extra capabilities. Over-restriction in large rooms needs clear refusal text. Production kernel behaviour differs from dev hosts. Keep Model proposes, Quarry executes.

alreadyPlanned.where: Partly: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/S3_2_SANDBOX_LEASE_CLOSEOUT_DESIGN_2026-09-10.md (sandbox lease) and the S6.2 matrix (SSRF) in VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md. Audience-intersection egress is not planned.

items.title: Room administration basics: change and choose member roles with an owner guard, rename, topic, archive and restore, and keep the organization room roster in sync
items.summary: Add a per-member role change and a role choice on add (viewer, editor, manager, owner) instead of the fixed editor grant, with Buzz-style pure guard functions (canGrant, canChangeRole, canLeave, last-owner rule) and table tests. Let managers rename a room and edit its topic, archive and unarchive it (read-only archive), and let owners or org admins delete it with a restore window once shared-room deletion lands on the saga (see the retention item). Run the existing syncAllOrganizationRooms on a schedule and on org membership changes so new members appear in the organization room and removed members leave it.
items.whyItMatters: Control already has viewer/editor/manager/owner roles and lifecycle states, but no route or UI changes a role, shared rooms cannot be renamed or archived, and the organization room's roster is never re-synced after provisioning. These are small, visible gaps that every chat product closes.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz
others: slack (richest role set: primary owner, owner, admin, member, two guest tiers)
qm (separate read, write, manage predicates per scope kind)
qm (agent-led onboarding recorded in the agent notebook)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-02-01] 5 of 5 sources have graded roles; 3 of 5 (buzz, slack, qm) have record-level evidence in this category; table-stakes [R-t1-02-04] 2 of 5 (buzz, teams); common [R-t1-02-06] 2 of 5 (buzz, qm); differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-02-01] Closed role enum with rank. canGrant(actor, target_role) requires actor rank >= target rank and actor >= manager; canChangeRole refuses demoting the last owner; canLeave refuses the sole owner. The role write runs in one transaction with a membership-revision check (TOCTOU-safe). Read, write and manage are separate predicates per room kind. [R-t1-02-04] room.state in {active, archived, deleted(restore_until)}. Rename and topic are metadata edits with role checks (topic by any member, name by admins in Buzz). TTL rooms: ttl_deadline = last durable event + ttl_seconds, advanced by a deferred trigger; a sweeper archives expired rooms. [R-t1-02-06] ensure_starter_rooms(org) with deterministic ids; on member join, add to default rooms and optionally trigger a welcome agent run that opens a welcome thread and closes it when introductions are done.

[R-t1-02-04] Deleting a shared room must cascade receipts across planes and honour the retention class and legal hold; ZDR orgs need immediate purge semantics rather than a restore window. items.title: Enterprise identity: stop the fake-success SCIM stub, real SCIM 2.0 with deprovisioning that suspends a person's agents, per-org SSO enforcement and domain verification; linked identities later
items.summary: First make the SCIM intake stop acknowledging requests it does not apply. Then build SCIM 2.0 Users and Groups in Control so IdP deactivation revokes sessions, removes Space memberships and suspends the agents that person owns; make SSO a per-org setting (domain verification, enforce-SSO flag, break-glass owner, domain allowlist and auto-join) with a typed session state in the UI. A later slice adds principal links so a person's sign-ins and external chat identities resolve to one principal.
items.whyItMatters: SSO and SCIM are table stakes for enterprise buyers in four references. Today SSO sits behind a global flag and the SCIM stub returns success without applying anything, so a deprovisioned employee silently keeps access and their agents keep acting: a real governance risk.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams; slack (SSO and SCIM), qm (principal links, actor gates)
others: qm (principal links: flat, evidence-recorded, reversible, no privilege creation)
teams (auth state machine, M365 group sync)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-10-04] SSO and identity federation: 4 of 5 (buzz, teams, qm, slack); table-stakes. SCIM is the usual enterprise companion. [R-t1-02-09] SSO methods 2 of 5 (common); SCIM 1 of 5 (unique here, enterprise suite feature); linked identities 2 of 5 (differentiator); allowlists 2 of 5 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-10-04] OIDC or SAML service provider with per-org IdP configuration and home-realm discovery by email domain; SCIM 2.0 /Users and /Groups endpoints drive membership and deprovisioning; principal links map several subjects to one canonical principal with recorded evidence and no privilege inheritance. [R-t1-02-09] Per-org sign-in policy {methods, default IdP, enforce SSO}; typed session auth state (up, interaction_required, licence_error, sign_in_restricted, unredeemed_invite). SCIM 2.0 /Users and /Groups per org with an org-scoped bearer token; deactivate revokes sessions and all Space memberships; group membership maps to a team. principal_links(person_id, provider, subject, evidence, created_by, revoked_at) with a cached canonicalPerson() resolver; links never carry admin rights and unlinking is immediate. Allowlist(org_id, kind email|domain, value) checked at sign-up, invite claim and agent invocation.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-10-04] SSO is behind a global flag with no per-org enforcement or domain verification. SCIM exists only as a token-managed intake that acknowledges requests without applying them, so deprovisioning silently does nothing and no provisioning reaches org membership or Space memberships. [R-t1-02-09] Passkeys, 2FA, email OTP and generic OAuth exist. Not verified: per-org SSO enforcement, domain verification and a typed auth state. SCIM and IdP group sync are absent. Principal linking exists only as an ADR.

items.approach: [R-t1-10-04] Control Plane owns identity. Add per-org IdP config, domain verification and an enforce-SSO flag in auth-core and org-core, and implement SCIM 2.0 Users and Groups in org-core: create, update and deactivate map to org membership, after which Control publishes the existing membership_changed event (Space memberships and session-core revocations already consume it) and auth-core revokes sessions. Deactivation also suspends owned agents using the suspension from F-t1-043 (R-t1-10-03). Reuse or re-home the per-org SCIM token store from integration-corev2. Immediately, make the integration-corev2 SCIM route return 501 so no IdP believes it succeeded. Group to Space mapping goes through the existing roster declaration. [R-t1-02-09] Control Plane: auth-core and org-core settings for per-org SSO policy, domain verification (DNS) and allowlist or auto-join; a SCIM service in org-core writing org membership, after which Control publishes membership_changed (Space memberships and Session Core revocations already consume it); principal_links owned by Control with OAuth proof as evidence, with integration-corev2 resolving provider subjects through Control instead of keeping its own mapping. Expose a typed session state to the gateway. Sequence: SSO and domains, then durable membership events and SCIM, then links once the Channel Plane starts.

Misconfigured domain verification can lock out an org. [R-t1-02-09] Enforcing SSO can lock owners out; keep a break-glass owner path. items.title: Client resilience: root and per-region error boundaries, lazy-chunk recovery, a boot watchdog, and a build id with stale-tab reload and contract guard
items.summary: Wrap the app in a root error boundary plus per-region boundaries (navbar, Space cockpit, side panels, run console) that show a classified failure card (render error, stale-deploy chunk failure, session expired, gateway unreachable) with Reload and Retry; reload once on a chunk-preload failure with a loop guard; add a boot watchdog. Expose a build id (Vite define plus a no-store version.json) and a minimum-client/contract version from the gateway, show a non-blocking 'new version, reload' banner, and force reload only on a contract mismatch after drafts are saved.
items.whyItMatters: The code itself states there is no Suspense or ErrorBoundary, so one render error blanks a Space that people keep open all day, and a tab open across a deploy keeps an old bundle whose lazy chunks can 404. Both are cheap to fix and immediately visible to users.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (diagnosis-specific error curtain with Restart / Repair / Open on web); grokbot (per-feature minimum client versions with a machine-readable update-required hint)
others: slack (fatal-exception and unresponsive-window dialogs with telemetry flush)
grokbot (single restore lifecycle with a 30 s stuck detector that reports the stage reached)
teams (staged nag-then-block staleness policy, DOC only)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-11-02] 3 of 5 sources (slack, teams, grokbot) = common; every native reference invests heavily here. [R-t1-11-04] 2 of 5 sources (grokbot, teams) = differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-11-02] Root boundary catches render and chunk-load failures and shows a curtain with a classified cause and actions; watchdog timers on boot stages emit "stuck at stage X" telemetry; hang detection offers wait or reload; safe-mode switches. [R-t1-11-04] Remote config {min_version, feature_min_versions, max_age_days}; API responses carry a CLIENT_UPDATE_REQUIRED hint when a stale client calls a gated feature; the UI turns the hint into a banner or forced reload.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-11-02] The createResource shim comment states the app has zero Suspense/ErrorBoundary usage, and src/index.tsx renders <App/> directly. A grep over src (excluding demo) for ErrorBoundary, Errored, Loading, unhandledrejection and vite:preloadError finds only that comment. About 30 routes are lazy() imports, and nginx answers a missing hashed .js file with 404 (try_files $uri =404), so a stale chunk after deploy has no recovery path. Only per-feature typed error states exist (for example budget_exceeded in the Space composer). [R-t1-11-04] No build id or version is exposed to the client (comparator grep for buildId, __APP_VERSION__, version.json found nothing; my grep of import.meta.env use shows only demo, captcha and gateway-url toggles). A tab open across a deploy keeps the old bundle, lazy chunks can 404, and there is no "reload" prompt. The SSE reader already supports Last-Event-ID resume, which is a natural hook for the version check.

items.approach: [R-t1-11-02] Frontend Plane: use the boundary primitive of the Solid version in use (the shim comment names Errored/Loading for Solid 2) at the root and around each shell region; failure card component with i18n copy keyed by error code (reuse shared/i18n/errors.ts) and a request id; window listener for the Vite preload-error event that reloads once (sessionStorage guard) and otherwise shows the card; boot-stage recorder posting to the existing gateway observability route (apps/gateway/src/domains/monitoring.rs). Report action uses the ids-only flow in F-t1-079 (R-t1-11-08). [R-t1-11-04] Frontend Plane: Vite build id injected at build, emitted as /version.json (Cache-Control: no-store; add an explicit nginx location, because json files currently fall through to the SPA fallback at nginx.conf:131-133 with no cache header, and give index.html no-cache too); gateway adds an X-Verevon-Client-Min header (or /api/v1/client-config) next to the existing envelope; SPA store compares on visibilitychange and SSE reconnect, shows the banner, and hard-reloads on a contract-version mismatch after the draft store flushes. An optional "What is new" entry can render once per build id from the deploy pipeline (low value, one-day follow-on).
dependencies: Persistent composer drafts (F-t1-032 (R-t1-01-08)) before any forced reload
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: [R-t1-11-02] Boundaries that swallow errors silently; always report with a request id. Auto-reload must not lose an unsent composer draft (see F-t1-032 (R-t1-01-08)). [R-t1-11-04] Forced reloads during typing lose drafts; version skew between the gateway and Space event schemas must be a deliberate contract version, not the build hash.

items.title: Multi-agent rooms: turn-taking, governed delegation, agent-to-agent messages and background child work
items.summary: Let several agents live in one room and cooperate: a room coordinator fans out per-member turn requests (nonce, deadline, parent/root ids, outcome sent|pass|skipped|timeout|cancelled), a hop limit and loop detector (shadow first), and an agent-to-agent message contract with typed delivery outcomes. A delegate must re-resolve its own authority through Control, and the whole chain renders as one collapsed unit with an openable transcript. Child sessions carry space_id and audience.
items.whyItMatters: Humans plus several agents working in the same room is the core of the Space vision and the main gap relative to Grok Bot. Verevon's Control model (agents as their own subjects) is a better base for this than any reference, but today only one agent can be addressed per message and delegation is unbuilt.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (turn protocol); qm (orchestrator spine, subagent inheritance)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Multi-agent turn-taking 2 of 5 (differentiator); agent-to-agent messaging 3 of 5 (common); subagents/swarms 2 of 5 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grok Bot coordinator fans out RequestMemberTurn{nonce, member, peers, new_messages, is_winding_down, deadline_ms, parent_request_id, root_parent_request_id}; members answer with outcome SENT|PASS|SKIPPED|TIMEOUT|CANCELLED; idempotency by nonce; hop limit via root-id depth; wind-down mode; loop detector off|shadow|on; UI shows each member's reading/typing/working phase. Agent messages: SendAgentMessage{from,to,message_id,text,reply_to} with outcomes FORBIDDEN|TARGET_NOT_FOUND|DUPLICATE, a collapsed 'messaged N agents' summary with openable transcript and a separate cost flow. QM spine: the coordinator cannot run tools, posts an early ack, delegates to child sessions (inherit caller scope+audience, durable mailbox that is data and never human authorization, tree caps, cycle checks) and is re-woken on completion.

items.approach: Follow the constraints in SPACE_AGENT_SCOPE_PLAN UI-2c: delegation is a side effect so it lives only in execution-core's governed loop, never in model-gateway's plain chat loop; the delegate gets a Control decision for its own subject in the same Space, bound to the initiating human's turn (re-resolved, never inherited). Add a room coordinator in the Model Plane driven by Application room events with bounded fan-out, depth and per-room caps, the nonce/deadline/outcome protocol above, loop detection in shadow mode first, and per-member phases for the UI. Add the execution-core to gateway (or Application) path the plan says is missing. Child sessions propagate space_id and audience; mailbox content is treated as data. Render a delegation as one collapsed card (item F-t1-004 (R-t1-07-02)). Tag agent-to-agent cost as its own flow (item F-t1-027 (R-t1-07-11)).

items.title: Typed cards and agent input requests (forms and secret drop)
items.summary: Define a small Verevon card schema (sections, buttons, select, fields, chart, link, with a required plain-text fallback) that agents emit as typed tool results and rooms render natively, with actions round-tripping as typed run signals. Build the first card type as request_input: an agent tool that pauses the run, shows a form (choices, multi-step, custom answer, dismiss) and resumes on submit, where secure fields post straight to the Control credential broker and only an opaque handle enters the run.
items.whyItMatters: Structured input makes multi-human rooms readable (who answered what) and replaces long prose with compact actionable UI. Keeping secrets out of chat is mandatory for ZDR and for agents that sign in to services for a person. Both are visible quality jumps for agent messages.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Forms and secret capture: 2 of 5 (differentiator); cards/blocks: 2 of 5 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: qm's secret drop mints a one-time URL (7-day TTL) via mint/peek/redeem with take-on-redeem; the value goes to the person's keychain with an optional grant to the conversation and the transcript records only that a secret was provided. Grok Bot's request_input tool {fields[], secure, multi_step} creates a pending widget in the thread; Respond/Submit/Dismiss resume the run with a typed message. Slack Block Kit is the best-specified card schema (server-validated, action_id/value round-trips, required top-level text); Teams Adaptive Cards add charts and dynamic search.

verevonToday.gap: Agent output renders Markdown, code and charts and there is a built-in approval card (owner-only decide, reconcile-on-error), but there is no general typed card schema with actions and no forms: agents can only ask in prose. Tool-call/plan cards and chat artifacts are absent in rooms. The credential broker for secret fields (S3.4) is planned only. The AG-UI stream accepts up to 32 caller-declared client tools (spot-check), which may carry the pause/resume round trip, but whether a client result resumes a Space run is unverified.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: card schema aligned with AG-UI generative-UI events, validated server-side in the gateway, rendered by the room timeline; start with buttons, select, fields, chart and link. Model Plane: request_input tool with a pause/resume contract that reuses approval continuation (or the AG-UI client-tool result path after verifying it resumes a Space run); card actions return as typed run signals through the gateway with a per-action authority check. Secret fields post directly to the Control credential broker (S3.4) and return an opaque handle; only the handle enters the run, transcript, logs and snapshots. Show the requesting agent's identity and destination on every form.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (request_input and resume); Frontend Plane (card schema, renderer); Control Plane (credential broker)
items.risks: Phishing-style forms driven by injected prompts; card actions are an injection path and need server-side validation plus per-action authority; secrets must never reach transcript, logs, snapshots or the model.

items.title: Agent operations: per-room and per-agent cost and budgets, admin allow/block, answer-quality surface, and room-behaviour evals
items.summary: Attribute usage to Space and agent binding by flow (chat, scheduled, agent-to-agent, browser, computer) in cost-core, add a per-Space allowance with warnings and a hard stop plus a room spend panel, and let admins allow or block agent definitions with a reason shown to users. On the answer itself add an AI label, citation chips and the thumbs-plus-reason feedback that /chat already has, a closed vocabulary of typed turn failures, and a room-behaviour eval suite that replays scripted multi-person scenarios against the gateway and Model Plane.
items.whyItMatters: Per-agent and per-room cost is table-stakes in four of five references, and it is the safeguard that makes multi-agent rooms, browsers and computers affordable to ship. Admins need to govern which agents may exist, and a room-behaviour eval is how Buzz keeps agents from becoming noisy or silent regressions.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (cost by flow and bot, hard limits); teams (AI label, citations, admin allow/block); buzz (room-behaviour evals)
others: qm (rolling-window admission check, multiplayer scenarios on real Slack)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Cost and usage attribution 4 of 5 (table-stakes); AI labelling/citations/feedback 3 of 5 (common); admin governance 2 of 5; turn resilience and typed failures 2 of 5; room-behaviour evals 2 of 5 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Buzz per-turn usage record {turn usage, cumulative, null for unknown, deltaReliable, session/turn seq}; Grok Bot series centsByFlow and centsByBotId, hard limits, prepaid top-up and usage warnings; QM admission check of rolling-window spend per person and org. Teams: a disclaimer label per agent message, citation chips that open the source, feedback {thumb, reason: not asked|inaccurate|low quality|too slow, comment}, explicit allow/block per agent app with reasons. Grok Bot: closed vocabulary of system-event kinds covering every resume path, typed result unions per tool, first-token and idle deadlines with server-paced retry. Buzz evals: task containers run the real product process tree with a roster manifest, scripted human actors, assertions on thread placement, notifications and silence plus an LLM judge, used as release regression.

items.title: Persistent per-agent computer with lifecycle UX and a governed egress boundary
items.summary: Grow the credential-free, network-less, run-scoped code_interpreter workspace into a per-(Space, agent) computer: a resource record with lifecycle states (absent, hibernated, starting, running), a durable home that survives runs, hibernate and pre-thaw on presence intent, and a room view of its files and processes with stop/kill. Route its network through Quarry with per-turn capability tokens and an audience egress floor (intersection of allowed hosts, union of denied), and add pattern-triggered process watches. Design the execute target so the user's own machine can be added later.
items.whyItMatters: An agent that works like a colleague with its own PC is the other half of the Grok Bot vision. Today the sandbox is deliberately hermetic, so agents cannot reach anything, and inline runs lose their edits, so there is no durable workplace to show in the room.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (lifecycle and cost-aware wake); qm (resource records, durable home snapshots, capability tokens plus authorising egress proxy)
others: buzz (agents as supervised local processes, pluggable computer backends)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Persistent agent computer 3 of 5 (common); lifecycle UX 1 of 5; sandbox security boundary 2 of 5 (differentiator); pluggable backends 2 of 5; own machine 2 of 5 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: QM sandbox resource record {owning scope, provider, identity, lifecycle} with an explicit default per scope ('no default -> no execution'); home snapshots via provider checkpoints plus throttled tar to object storage, a pending marker before create and never adopting a blank home over a saved one. QM egress: HMAC/Ed25519 token {aud, scopeId, actorId, members, egress, credentials, runId, runLease}; an Envoy filter calls the authz check, resolves DNS, rejects private ranges and dials the checked IP; allowed egress hosts = intersection over the audience, denied = union; backend profile egressEnforcement none|ip_port|domain with refusal of substitutes. Grok Bot: ReportClientPresence{agent, viewing, surface, intent: APP_FOREGROUND|CHAT_OPEN|COMPOSER_FOCUS|TYPING|UPLOAD_START} yields NONE|IN_FLIGHT|PRETHAW|REFUSED, calls tagged background never wake, and a pure wake|hold|follow function; pattern-triggered wake-ups use an output observer with batching and notification limits.

verevonToday.gap: No per-agent computer, no lifecycle states or hibernation, no durable home beyond run end, no room-visible computer view, no signal/kill or watches from the room, no network path for the sandbox, no per-turn capability token with an audience egress floor, no backend capability contract beyond the published profile.

items.approach: Model Plane sandbox-manager: per-(Space, agent) lease with a durable home, a resource record and lifecycle states, snapshots on run end and periodic checkpoints, and the 'no default -> no execution' rule; publish a typed backend capability profile {persistence, processSessions, egressEnforcement} and refuse unsupported routes (keep few backends). Egress: send sandbox traffic through Quarry (reuse its SSRF guards) with a per-turn capability token bound to the run lease and the Space decision audience floor, never direct internet. Frontend: Work tab computer section (state, files, processes, stop/kill) and presence intents (typing, composer focus) to pre-thaw. Add pattern-triggered watches on process output using the S4.3 Watch primitive. ZDR orgs get ephemeral homes. Keep the execute target abstract (scoped|scratch|owner-machine) so a typed exec protocol to the user's own device can be added later without redesign.

items.title: Room calls on a bought SFU with Control-authorized join and a navigation-persistent call bar, modelled as a meeting record that belongs to the Space
items.summary: Add a Call button that starts or joins the single live call of a room. Run media on a self-hostable SFU plus TURN (LiveKit OSS or equivalent) and keep Verevon code to authority and signalling: a call/meeting record in the Application Plane (state, start and end, server-derived attendees, links to AI policy, transcript and recap), a gateway route that mints a short-lived SFU join token only after a Control decision for a new space.call.join effect, a live badge with Join in the room header, start and end rows in Activity, and a Solid call store with explicit phases. Authority is inherited from the parent Space, not from a new child Space kind.
items.whyItMatters: Calls are table stakes in every human-chat reference (Teams, Slack, buzz) and the brief names Teams. They are not first because the Space definition lists huddles as a non-goal (a product decision is needed), media is a buy rather than a build, and a live badge needs the push substrate first.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack (huddles, DOC) for the product model; Grok Bot (SRC) for the client call state machine; Teams SlimCore (SRC) for lifecycle depth; Buzz (SRC): the data model; Teams (REA): the UX
others: Teams (ring members individually or all, roster-size cap; REA)
Buzz (audio-only WebSocket relay of Opus frames, O(n^2) fan-out; SRC)
Teams: live participant count and Join in the channel header, Meet now, scheduled channel meetings
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-03-01] Calls started from a room: 3 of 5 (Slack, Teams, Buzz), table-stakes. Explicit call lifecycle and reconnect: 3 of 5, common. Device enumeration and permission probing: 2 of 5 (Slack, Teams), common. [R-t1-03-05] 2 of 5 (Buzz, Teams); differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-03-01] The call is an attachment of the room: one click from any room, optional video, ends when the last person leaves. Server side: POST creates or returns the live call for the room, checks membership, and mints a short-lived SFU token (room = call id, identity = actor id, publish/subscribe grants); media flows browser to SFU over WebRTC (Opus audio, simulcast video); roster and speaking state come from the SFU and are projected to the room as a live call card with Join. Client side (Grok Bot): a pure reducer with phases connecting|live|reconnecting|ending|failed, isMuted, startedAt and a fault field, a recoverable-close policy with bounded backoff, and a call island that persists across navigation; never re-open the mic silently after relaunch (Buzz rule). Devices (Slack): enumerate with a devicechange listener, probe that a device actually opens, route output with setSinkId, and map getUserMedia failures to actionable messages. [R-t1-03-05] Buzz: a huddle is an ephemeral private child channel (ttl 3600) referenced from the parent by creator-signed started and ended events, relay-emitted joined and left events, and the last human leaving ends it, so chat, reactions and transcript inherit room authorisation and leave a persistent record in the parent. Teams: header badge with live count and Join, meetings as channel objects with companion chat.
