verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-03-01] No call, huddle, SFU or WebRTC code in the gateway, Model or Application planes and nothing under src/features/spaces. The Space doc lists huddles as a non-goal, so this is a code gap and an open product decision. Two substrate gaps shape the build: the Space has no push transport (6 s poll), so a live-call badge lags up to 6 s unless SFU webhooks feed a push path; and there are no Space notifications or human-only posts, so ring-others and a call card in the thread are blocked. [R-t1-03-05] No meeting object, no time-bounded session type and no live indicator. Threads and run status exist but nothing models a bounded live session. A literal copy of the Buzz child-channel model would mean a new SpaceRef kind registered with Control for every call, which the authority ADR does not define. A companion chat is blocked because every room post is currently an AI turn and there is no human-only post path.

items.approach: [R-t1-03-01] Application Plane (apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex, next to spacePresence.ts): a spaceCalls record {call_id, space_id, org_id, state live|ended, started_by (server-derived), started_at, ended_at, participant_count} fed by signed SFU webhooks; this is the minimal form of the meeting aggregate in this item (R-t1-03-05). Gateway (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs): POST /api/v1/spaces/{id}/calls (create or get live) and POST .../calls/{call_id}/join, which obtains a Control decision for a new space.call.join effect (same pattern as the thread create/read decisions, deny by default through per-org space_effect_policies) and then signs the SFU token with the Control subject id as identity; the browser never supplies identity. Frontend: src/features/calls with a Solid store modelled on voice-mode-state.ts, SFU web SDK, call bar mounted at shell level, Call button and live badge in SpacePage.tsx, and a shared media-devices module extracted from voice-recorder.ts (enumerateDevices, permissions.query, level-meter pre-join test, setSinkId, persisted device ids). Start/end rows go to the Space activity feed (src/features/spaces/lib/activity-grammar.ts). Self-hosted SFU for sovereign and ZDR tenants; media is relayed, not stored. [R-t1-03-05] Application Plane: a spaceMeetings record {meeting_id, space_id, kind live|uploaded|external, state, started_at, ended_at, attendees, policy_ref, artifact_refs} authorised under the parent Space decision with purpose meeting; artifacts carry space_id plus meeting_id. Prefer this sub-resource over a new child SpaceRef kind; if a child Space is wanted later it needs an ADR-0001 amendment and a cheap registration path. Frontend: live badge in the SpacePage.tsx header, meeting card in the activity feed, Meetings section in the cockpit. Server derives attendees from SFU or capture roster events, never from the client. Companion notes thread only after the messaging category delivers human-only posts.
dependencies: Product decision reversing the huddle non-goal in docs/space-defenition.md
SFU and TURN deployment (Infra Plane), self-hostable
Control effect space.call.join plus space_effect_policies rows
Push transport for Space liveness (realtime and sync category) for a sub-6 s live badge
Human-only post path (messaging category) for a companion chat
ADR-0001 amendment only if a child Space kind is chosen
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (call and meeting record); Frontend Plane (gateway token route, call UI); Control Plane (join decision); Infra Plane (SFU/TURN)
items.risks: [R-t1-03-01] Reverses a documented non-goal. Media infra cost and operations. ZDR posture must state that media is relayed but never stored unless recording (F-t1-084 (R-t1-03-09)) is enabled. Building a custom media engine would be XL, so stay on the SDK. Calls are built on a room whose human-to-human messaging path is still missing. [R-t1-03-05] Ephemeral TTL semantics must not conflict with legal hold or retention policy. Child-Space-per-call would load the Control registration saga.

items.title: Room content hardening: read authorization for attachments and transcripts, stricter CSP, anti-spoofing, link and download safety
items.summary: Four small web changes for a UI that renders other people's and agents' content. Check room membership and audience on attachment and transcript reads and render an explicit 'restricted' state instead of swallowing the 403. Tighten the CSP (Trusted Types with a sanitiser policy, narrower connect-src and img-src, report-only candidate policy with a report endpoint, subresource integrity). Keep agent-generated HTML in the sandboxed no-network iframe and approval UI in the main origin. Mark agent-sourced links and files and serve attachments with safe headers.
items.whyItMatters: An XSS or exfiltration channel in a room acts with a user's agent authority. Several cheap controls already exist; these changes close the remaining broad allowances (img-src and connect-src allow any https host) and the silent 403.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams
others: buzz (kind-level read policy; attachment ACL gap to avoid)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Strict CSP with Trusted Types: 2 of 5 (teams, slack); fine-grained read authz: 1 of 5 (buzz); trusted sensitive UI: 1 of 5 (teams); link and download safety: 1 of 5 (slack).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: CSP: default-src 'self', nonce-based script-src, require-trusted-types-for 'script' with named policies, object-src 'none', base-uri 'none', plus a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only with a stricter candidate and SRI integrity for every build chunk. Reads: a kind-level policy consulted on every read path (query, push, search) returns not-found for hidden kinds, and attachment reads check the parent message's room ACL. Links: scheme allowlist, warnings for unusual protocols, safe download headers.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/nginx.conf:70 (enforced CSP: default-src 'self', script-src 'self' plus Turnstile and Nexi, frame-ancestors 'none', object-src 'none', base-uri and form-action 'self'; but style-src 'unsafe-inline', connect-src 'self' https:, img-src allows any https host; no Trusted Types, nonce, report-only policy or SRI)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/lib/sandbox-html.ts:1-40 (agent HTML preview iframe with default-src 'none', connect-src 'none', img-src data and blob only, form-action 'none')

apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:2616-2680 and src/features/spaces/components/SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:201 (deny-by-default shared-read gate; the timeline swallows the 403 and shows a preview, per the UI baseline)
Per-room attachment ACL and Content-Disposition and nosniff headers on room downloads: not found or verified
verevonToday.gap: The server gate is right but the UI hides it; attachment authorization per room is not recorded; the CSP lets agent- or member-authored markdown trigger requests to arbitrary https hosts (images, fetch), which is a known exfiltration channel (inference); no Trusted Types or SRI.

items.approach: Frontend Plane gateway: confirm attachment fetches check room membership and audience and add not-found semantics for hidden kinds; Frontend: render a restricted state for 403. nginx.conf: add require-trusted-types-for with a DOMPurify policy, replace connect-src https: with the own API and the telemetry host, restrict img-src to own origin plus a media proxy for chat images, add a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only candidate and a gateway report endpoint, add an SRI plugin to the Vite build. Keep approval dialogs in the main origin and agent HTML only in sandbox-html iframes. Mark agent-sourced links, allow only https and mailto without a warning, and serve attachments with Content-Disposition attachment and nosniff.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (nginx, gateway, SPA)
items.risks: Third-party scripts (Turnstile, Nexi checkout) can break under Trusted Types. Remote chat-media images need a proxy. Over-tight CSP can break existing embeds, so roll out through report-only first.

items.title: Org audit trail for admins: role-gated view, Space decisions and agent invocations, SIEM export, usage ledger export
items.summary: Expose audit-core to org admins and auditors through a role-gated, cursor-paginated API and view, and an export token that streams or pulls events (metadata only). Record signed Space decisions (decision id, subject, audience revision, agent principal, privacy tier, outcome), agent invocations, approvals and moderation actions. Add per-Space and per-agent attribution and a bounded export window to the usage ledger for finance.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprises that adopt an agent workspace must answer which agent did what, on whose authority. Verevon already signs decisions, so exporting them is cheap and differentiating. The current read path also looks too broad: any authenticated org member can list the org's events.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: slack
others: qm (source-level mechanics: recordOnce idempotency, audited admin reads, spend ledger and bounded export)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: SIEM-grade audit: 2 of 5 (slack DOC, qm SRC); spend export: 1 of 5 (qm). Differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Append-only table keyed by org and sequence with a unique idempotency key; fire-and-forget record() and exactly-once recordOnce(key); a read API filters by scope, action and time with cursor pagination; an org-admin token streams JSON events (actor, action, entity, context, details, app) to a SIEM; message bodies are never logged; each export is itself audited. Spend: a ledger by day, scope, origin and model with a bounded, token-authenticated export.

evidence: apps/Control Plane/audit-core/internal/api/api.go:106-115 (GET and POST /v1/audit, /v1/usage and GET /v1/usage/summary, service-authenticated only)
apps/Control Plane/audit-core/internal/api/api.go:197-222 (filters org_id, since, until, event, user_id, limit default 100; no cursor)

apps/Control Plane/audit-core/internal/store/schema.sql:11-33 and :45-66 (audit_events with plane, event, subject, resource_id, outcome, details, event_id, payload_hash; usage_events with tokens and cost_cents) and migrations/003_logical_control_audit_idempotency.sql

apps/Control Plane/audit-core/internal/api/service_auth.go:205-213 and :268-273 (scope audit:read:self; HMAC delegation with replay nonce binds the org; the signed X-User-Role is carried but the list handler does not consult it)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/audit.rs:30-112 (session-gated proxy of /v1/audit for the Trust Center; no admin check in the handler)
apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/spaces/decision.go (no audit emission seen; signed Space decisions are not recorded in audit-core)
verevonToday.gap: The audit and usage pipes exist, but there is no admin-scoped audit view or export, no cursor, no Space, agent or decision-id dimension, and decisions are not recorded. The read handler appears to rely on org binding alone, so a normal member could read all org events (needs a trace through audit-core to confirm).

items.approach: audit-core: add cursor pagination, filters for plane, subject, resource_id, outcome and decision_id, require an admin or auditor role from the signed delegation (self-scope for ordinary members), and per-org export tokens with audited exports. Control user-core: emit space.decision.issued and space.decision.denied events (metadata only). Model Plane: session-core audit_publisher already records tool actions with data category and zdr; add agent-invocation and approval events. cost-core and session-core add space_ref and agent principal to usage metadata. Gateway: /api/v1/admin/audit and an export route. Frontend: an admin Audit view filterable by Space, agent and decision id. Under ZDR carry metadata only. First step in W1: trace the audit-core read handler; if a normal member can read all org events, fix that as a bug before building the admin view.
dependencies: Control decision ids on every effect
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (audit-core) with Frontend Plane gateway
items.risks: An export is a mass exfiltration path, so reads must be audited and scoped. Event volume. The tool_action consumer in the Trust Center must keep working when the read path is role-gated.

items.title: Composer for real work: rich text, persistent drafts, queue and steer while a turn runs, attachments and paste chips, scheduled send, and ref-based context chips with a pre-send preview
items.summary: Replace the plain textarea with a rich-text composer that emits markdown plus mention refs, render human posts through the same ChatMarkdown as agent output, keep per-room and per-thread drafts across navigation and failed sends, wire the existing queue and steer backend into the Space composer, and add attachments (including folder drop), long-paste chips, model presets and scheduled send. Add 'Ask the agent about this' from canvas, list, file, artifact and Work/Knowledge/Activity selections: the selection travels as a typed reference chip, the exact payload is shown before sending, and the Model Plane frames it as quoted, capped, untrusted data.
items.whyItMatters: The composer is where people and agents meet; today it is a disabled-while-sending textarea whose text is lost on navigation, and human posts render as plain text while agent posts get full markdown. Buzz's context hand-off shows how to give an agent context without copying content into the transcript.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (Tiptap chat editor, send journal and delivery states); buzz (revisioned drafts, markdown toolbar); qm (queue chips and steer); QM for a human+agent composer; Slack for the human messaging set; Buzz for selection-to-context; Buzz (SRC, highest-quality evidence in this category): context block capped at 100 items and 16,000 characters, control characters collapsed, values JSON-quoted, a fixed treat-as-data notice, and a byte-identical payload preview before signing
others: Buzz (selectable list groups, count menu, discuss action, capped context block builder opening an agent chat or channel)
QM (SRC) app bar with select, marker, draw and capture posting snapshots via postMessage
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-08] Rich composer 4 of 5 and drafts 4 of 5 (table-stakes); scheduled send 3 of 5 (common); queue/steer and reliable send 1 of 5 each (unique) [R-t1-12-05] composer 2 of 5 (Slack, QM; common, likely under-counted since attachments are industry-standard, INF); selection-to-context 1 of 5 (Buzz; unique) [R-t1-08-08] in-page context: 1 of 5, unique; annotate: 2 of 5, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-08] grokbot: Tiptap/ProseMirror with a restricted schema (paragraph, lists, code, link, mention chip) serialised to markdown on send, Shift+Enter as a user setting, dir=auto per paragraph. buzz: draft keyed by (room, thread) holding text, mentions, attachment refs and a revision; clearing writes an empty tombstone with a higher revision so late async completions cannot resurrect it. grokbot send pipeline: client nonce, local journal, server dedupes by message id, bubble confirms on transcript echo, typed delivery ACCEPTED|DUPLICATE|REFUSED and an UNKNOWN_DURABILITY state. qm: editable queue chips while a run streams and a steer promotion through a durable RunSignal. Scheduled send fires through the normal send path with the author's authority rechecked at fire time. [R-t1-12-05] Composer state {text, attachments[], chips[], loadout}; a paste handler turns text over N characters into a chip atom labelled from its first line; loadout presets upserted with cap 8; a slash token parser opens a command menu from a registry; scheduled send writes a job owned by the message plane. Buzz: buildContext(selection) produces a quoted, capped block of object refs and the action opens an agent chat or new channel with the block pre-attached as visible chips. [R-t1-08-08] buildContextBlock(selection) produces JSON-quoted values with caps; the prompt adds a fixed instruction that quoted values are data; the UI renders the exact string to be appended and the user confirms. Annotate: a bar script inside the sandboxed frame captures the selection (DOM path plus box) and an annotated screenshot and posts it to the parent with origin checks; the parent attaches it to the composer as typed context.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:597-772 (two-row textarea, model picker, skill chips, reply banner, ZDR refusals surfaced)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceWorkPanel.tsx:106-192 and components/SpaceKnowledgePanel.tsx:82-243 (read-only lists, no selection)
verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-01-08] The composer is a plain textarea (rows=2) disabled while a send is in flight; human turns render as a plain paragraph while agent turns use ChatMarkdown; draft text is a component-local signal lost on navigation or failure. The gateway accepts an idempotency_key for the append decision (generated per request when absent) but no client-stable key was found in the chat client, and Session Core dedupe by key was not verified. Queue/steer backend exists (invocation queue route and re-minted append decision per queued message) but only /chat uses it. No human scheduled send (agent crons only). [R-t1-12-05] No attachments, formatting, emoji, slash commands, clips, scheduled send, presets or paste chips, and no multi-select or "ask an agent about these" action. Every send is an AI invocation. [R-t1-08-08] Model Plane already applies injection defense and a treat-as-data notice to untrusted retrieved and tool content, but it was not verified that room artifacts or selected context pass through it. The Space composer has no context chip, no pre-send payload preview and no annotate feedback (grep of the spaces components finds none). The comparator left this status unknown.

items.approach: [R-t1-01-08] Frontend Plane: Tiptap core (ProseMirror) wrapped for Solid with a restricted schema, emitting markdown plus mentions[] (F-t1-007 (R-t1-01-02)); render human turns with ChatMarkdown. Drafts: localStorage keyed (spaceRef, threadId) inside try/catch with revision tombstones, cleared on logout and honoring ZDR; restore on failed send. Send: client UUID idempotency_key passed to the gateway and bound into the Control decision digest (the append decision already takes one), Session Core dedupes on it, UI shows pending, failed (retry restores draft) and sent. Queue/steer: wire queueInvocationInput into SpaceRoomComposer so a message typed during a run becomes an editable queued chip showing its author, and promote to steer for an authorized member. Last phase: scheduled send through a Control schedule primitive that rechecks authority at fire time. Build one composer with category 12 (C-t1-12-009). [R-t1-12-05] Frontend Plane: composer state with chips that hold refs (documentId, runRef, threadRef) resolved by Data/Model planes at use time; attachments go through Data Plane documents with Space-bound ACL (never widened) and respect ZDR; slash menu reads human-eligible entries from shared/actions/action-registry.ts. Each append still needs a Control thread:append decision bound to the final bytes. Scheduled send needs an owner (Model Plane session or an Application Plane scheduler) and is deferred. Selection mode lands on the three read-only lists once chips exist. [R-t1-08-08] Frontend Plane: add Ask agent about this on canvas, list and file views producing a typed context chip with a byte-exact preview; for HTML artifacts add a selection overlay in the sandboxed viewer with origin-checked postMessage. Model Plane: render attached context as quoted untrusted blocks with caps, reusing the moderation injection_defense path, and bound what is attached by the viewer's own grants. Under ZDR drop screenshots from the payload.
dependencies: F-t1-001 (R-t1-01-01) shared append so non-owners can queue and steer
Session Core dedupe by idempotency key
F-t1-014 (R-t1-08-02) HTML artifacts for the annotate phase
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (composer) with Model Plane (untrusted-context framing, dedupe) and Control Plane (scheduled send)
items.risks: [R-t1-01-08] Editor bundle size and ProseMirror-in-Solid integration. Digest-bound decisions must include the nonce to stay replay-safe. Steer by a non-owner needs the shared-append authority. Drafts in browser storage must be clearable under ZDR. Authority can drift between schedule time and fire time. [R-t1-12-05] Copying content into prompts would bypass owner ACL and ZDR, so pass refs. Content-bound append decisions complicate drafts and scheduled send. ZDR content must not reach external preview or embedding services. Attachments are table stakes in practice (INF): promote to priority if the category 01 human-only path lands first. [R-t1-08-08] Context bloat and screenshots may contain data the agent should not see under ZDR. postMessage origin validation. The annotate phase is polish and can slip.

items.title: SPA realtime client layer: client-supplied idempotency key, send states with in-place optimistic row, normalized store with version guards, offline vs service-down banner
items.summary: Make the composer generate an idempotency_key per send and reuse it on retry (a new key only when the content changes), expose queued, sending, accepted and failed states, and key the timeline row by that key until the canonical id arrives from the stream, reconciling in place. Replace per-component fetches with a Solid store keyed by entity id that stream frames and fetches patch with version guards (a write supersedes an older in-flight read). Add a connectivity service that probes a no-auth gateway health route to tell offline from service-down and shows a banner with the last-fresh time.
items.whyItMatters: The gateway generates its own idempotency key when the composer omits one, so a client retry after a timeout creates a second append and a second billed AI turn. A store that push frames can patch is needed to apply the stream cleanly, and the room should explain unreachable states instead of showing stale data. These are small, cheap changes with direct cost and trust payoff.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (send journal with stages queued, prepared, dispatching, accepted-awaiting-echo; resource state machine with stale-while-revalidate and write-supersedes-read guards); Slack for connectivity states
others: Buzz (content-addressed event ids with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; optimistic-<uuid> row swapped on success keeping the render key)
QM (idempotency keys and 5-minute replay window at every ingress)
Teams (central data layer with normalized cache; DOC/SRC)
Slack (online, slackDown, offline via unauthenticated api.test probe; sleep and wake forwarded)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 3 of 5 for idempotent sends (common); 2 of 5 for a normalized data layer; 3 of 5 for connectivity awareness (common); optimistic in-place insert 1 of 5
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Client generates a send id on Enter and persists it with the draft; server insert is ON CONFLICT (tenant, send_id) DO NOTHING and returns was_inserted; the client marks accepted only when the echo with the same send id arrives. Resource<T> = {state: loading, ready, failed(prev), empty, unavailable, value, version}. Probe a cheap no-auth health endpoint on connection errors, listen to online/offline, visibilitychange and page freeze/resume, and resync on resume.

verevonToday.gap: SRC verified: spaces.rs required_or_generated invents an idempotency_key when the client omits it, and no idempotency reference appears in the Space composer or lib files. Control append decisions already bind the key and payload digest, so only the client key is missing; whether Session Core dedupes on it was not verified (grpc.rs:2598 derives an idempotency hash for the message event). The timeline updates only on the next poll, data fetches are per component, and there is no offline vs service-down banner or last-fresh label.

items.approach: Composer (SpaceRoomComposer.tsx): generate the key per send, store it with the pending exchange, send it in the append body so spaces.rs passes it into the Control thread:append decision; confirm Session Core dedupes on (thread, key) and returns the existing turn, otherwise add it in append_message_in_tx. Keep approvals and pins deliberately non-optimistic. Store: createStore keyed by entity id with version guards and explicit resource states, keeping the existing gap-not-empty rendering as the unavailable state. Connectivity: small service using the existing gateway unauthenticated /health route (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/main.rs:91, rate-limit exempt) as the probe plus online/offline, visibilitychange and freeze/resume hooks feeding the watchdog of F-t1-003 (R-t1-09-01) and a room banner. Coordinate with F-t1-032 (R-t1-01-08) (composer states and queueing).
dependencies: Session Core dedupe on idempotency key (verify)
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Content-bound decisions: a retry with edited content must get a new key. Store refactor churn across SpacePage components. Gateway health probe must stay unauthenticated and content-free.

items.title: Scalable room timeline: server-computed windows with exact cursors and reply summaries, virtualised rows with scroll anchoring, jump-to-latest and history paging
items.summary: Add a Session Core query and gateway route that returns windows of top-level threads with reply count, last reply time and participants kept at write time, a keyset cursor on server seq and id and a limit+1 has_more probe. Window the SpaceRoomTimeline rows with a pure, tested anchoring policy (hold the anchor on prepend, auto-scroll on append only while pinned to the bottom, otherwise show Jump to latest), page older turns on scroll, support jump to thread or date, and keep aria-setsize/posinset.
items.whyItMatters: Every 6 s poll reloads the full thread list and then fetches each transcript (N+1); with push and streaming the view will jump. Buzz's cursor windows and anchoring policy are the tested pattern.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Buzz (NIP-CW timeline windows: top_level, include_summaries, composite until + before_id cursor, thread_metadata computed at ingest); Buzz (written, tested anchoring policy on a patched virtual list, mobile IME handling)
others: Grok Bot (FLIP animation for rows shifting under late content, epoch-keyed layout cache)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-09-07] 1 of 5; unique [R-t1-12-06] 2 of 5 (Buzz, Grok Bot); differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-09-07] Maintain thread_metadata (reply_count, last_reply_at, participants) at write time; page with WHERE (created_at, id) < (until, before_id) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT n+1 and return summaries inline; reject client timestamps beyond a skew bound or order by server seq instead so keyset order is replica-safe. [R-t1-12-06] Virtual list with measured row heights; anchoring state {pinnedToBottom, anchorRowId, anchorOffset}: on prepend preserve anchor offset, on append scroll only if pinned, show Jump-to-latest when not pinned and new rows arrive; ResizeObserver plus FLIP animates siblings when a row grows, disabled under reduced motion.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:134-416 (plain <ol>; MAX_TURNS_PER_POST = 30 at line 50; no scrollTop or scrollIntoView use anywhere in features/spaces)
verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-09-07] The full thread list loads on every poll with no paging, no jump-to-date and no reply summaries, each post fetches its own transcript (N+1), and deep links with thread_id are ignored. [R-t1-12-06] No virtualisation, no scroll anchoring and no paging: the full thread list loads on every 6 s poll, so the view will jump once realtime or streaming lands.

items.approach: [R-t1-09-07] Session Core (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core): add a Space timeline-window query over threads with origin=space, with reply summaries stored at append time; expose through model-gateway and a gateway route GET /api/v1/spaces/{id}/timeline?before=&limit=. Order by server seq from F-t1-003 (R-t1-09-03) rather than client timestamps. Summaries and participant lists are filtered by per-thread read decisions. SPA: virtualised list in SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx fed by the store of F-t1-033 (R-t1-09-06); fetch bodies lazily per visible post. [R-t1-12-06] Frontend Plane: a windowing layer for the timeline with a standalone anchoring-policy module and lifecycle tests, plus a turn-paged history call from Model Plane through the gateway. Because the app is on Solid 2.0 RC with no virtual-list dependency, first confirm that @tanstack/solid-virtual works on Solid 2, otherwise implement windowing with IntersectionObserver and measured heights.
dependencies: Session Core query support for thread summaries
Turn-based history paging API in Model Plane
Push realtime (category 09) is the consumer that makes this necessary
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (Session Core windows) with Frontend Plane (gateway route, virtualised timeline)
items.risks: [R-t1-09-07] Summaries must respect per-thread read decisions and not leak participants of threads the reader cannot see. Backfilling reply summaries for existing threads needs a resumable job. [R-t1-12-06] Virtualisation breaks find-in-page and screen-reader reading order unless handled; Solid 2 RC compatibility of third-party list libraries; unmeasured rows cause scroll jumps.

items.title: Attention outside the open tab: installable PWA, content-free Web Push with service-worker Open/Reply, in-tab toasts, tab-title and app badge
items.summary: Add a web app manifest, a versioned service worker (build-id-keyed shell cache, reconnecting page, push and notificationclick handlers) and an install affordance. Add Web Push (VAPID) subscriptions per device in notification-core where the push payload is only an opaque wake plus a notification id; the service worker fetches the notification through the gateway and renders it, honouring hide-preview, with Open and Reply only (an approval opens the approval view, never approves from a toast). In the tab, add one toast store fed by the attention stream, a tab-title and favicon count and navigator.setAppBadge from the unread map with a monotonic projection, and optional per-signal sounds.
items.whyItMatters: There is no manifest, service worker or push, so an agent that finishes or needs approval while the tab is closed cannot reach anyone. Buzz's content-free wake push is the reference pattern that fits ZDR; the native desktop shell (5 of 5 references) can come later on top of this.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm (installable single web build with phone mode) for the PWA surface; slack for the aggregated unread state behind tray and badge; Buzz (content-free wake push); Slack for toasts with inline reply and action buttons; Teams (in-app toast panel and banners); Grok Bot for the badge projection; Slack for sounds
others: buzz (native mobile apps, badges, running agents in tray)
grokbot (monotonic unread projection feeding the badge)
Slack (grouped toasts, reply input, content-free logs)
Teams (wake-for-calls path, dismissal and suppression reasons)
Grok Bot (permission state reported to the server, active-device routing)
Slack (HTML toast window, 13-14 named sounds, tray and overlay cues)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-11-01] Installable PWA 2 of 5 sources (qm, buzz) = differentiator; unread badge/tray state 3 of 5 (buzz, slack, teams) = common. Presence outside the open tab is treated as table stakes by every native client. [R-t1-05-05] 4 of 5 sources across push, native toasts and permission handling; common [R-t1-05-08] 4 of 5 sources; toasts common, badge and sounds table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-11-01] One web build with a shared breakpoint constant for CSS and JS and a visualViewport listener to keep the composer above the keyboard (qm); web manifest plus service worker for app shell and Web Push; Badging API fed by an aggregated unread count; Slack derives a three-state icon (rest/unread/highlight) plus a count tooltip from the same aggregate. [R-t1-05-05] Buzz: the device registers an encrypted, expiring (at most 30 days), installation-scoped lease with self-only filters; after read-authorization checks the server queues a wake; a blind gateway sends a constant payload; the client wakes, fetches pending items through the authenticated API, verifies and renders locally, so neither the push provider nor the gateway sees content. Slack builds a ToastGeneric toast from the normalised payload with grouped header, avatar, reply input and action buttons; the reply dispatches with channel, thread and trace ids and logs only non-content fields. Grok Bot reports {platform, os_permission, can_ask_again, in_app_enabled} per device so the server skips denied devices; Slack throttles macOS re-prompts (3 per session, 10 minutes apart). On the web the equivalent is showNotification with actions plus a notificationclick handler. [R-t1-05-08] Teams draws its own toast panel (corner, compact or comfortable density, grouped collections, in-place update) and a separate web-layer banner system, distinguishing in-context banners from OS toasts. Grok Bot computes the badge from the same roster as the sidebar, skips muted or hidden items, and rejects stale snapshots by epoch and sequence so the number never moves backwards. Slack stores a sound id per event type and plays it in the web layer when visible, otherwise passes it to the OS notification.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-11-01] Responsive workroom layout and dark theme ship, but index.html links no manifest, the title is the static string "verevonv3", and a source grep (src, public, vite.config.ts) finds no service worker, Push API or setAppBadge use outside the demo guard. Unread counts exist only as navbar badges polled on a timer. Cannot be installed and cannot notify when the tab is closed (SRC; also stated in the dated parity audit, DOC). [R-t1-05-05] A Novu adapter exists but is disabled by default, and provider-side ZDR is not proven. The delivery worker marks any ZDR request failed with zdr_async_delivery_unavailable, so ZDR orgs get no push. There is no service worker, Notification API use or PushManager in the web app (INF from grep, low risk) and no permission or device-state reporting. No OS or browser notifications exist at all. [R-t1-05-08] A grep of verevonv3 src found toast code only in ticket bulk actions and global.css, no notification sounds (the only audio code is voice read-aloud), and no Badging API use or title count. A shared notice component under another name could exist outside these greps, so status rests on negative searches (INF).

items.approach: [R-t1-11-01] Frontend Plane (verevonv3): add public/manifest.webmanifest plus icons and link it in index.html; hand-rolled or vite-plugin-pwa service worker that precaches the shell keyed by the build id from F-t1-024 (R-t1-11-04) and never caches /api, Space transcripts or media (ZDR); serve the worker script and index.html with no-cache (nginx.conf:102-105 gives every .js file a one-year immutable header, so sw.js needs its own location, and the CSP comment at nginx.conf:69 assumes no workers, so check worker-src/manifest-src); push handler and Open/Reply actions exactly as specified in this item (R-t1-05-05) (subscription storage and fan-out stay in Application Plane notification-core, payload carries ids only); title "(n) Verevon" and setAppBadge from the same unread map as this item (R-t1-05-08), skipping muted rooms; manifest protocol_handlers (web+verevon) and share_target route through the resolver from F-t1-039 (R-t1-11-03) and the share target from F-t1-070 (R-t1-06-12). Native tray with a running-agent list is deferred to F-t1-073 (R-t1-11-09). [R-t1-05-05] Application Plane (notification-core): store Web Push subscriptions per device with the permission state; enqueue a wake through the S4.4 ledger (F-t1-060 (R-t1-05-10)); lift the ZDR refusal only for the wake class whose payload is constant and content-free. Gateway: a scoped, short-lived token for the service worker's fetch of /notifications/{id}. Frontend Plane: register a service worker; render with Open and Reply actions; Reply posts to the right thread without opening the app; approvals never act from the toast. Active-device suppression: reuse the gateway's presence calls to keep a renewable activity lease (store only the current lease, no log) and default to sending when unsure; this is the device-routing half of the cross-device cluster. Use Novu only for non-ZDR orgs, if at all. [R-t1-05-08] Frontend Plane: a notification store in a shared module consuming the F-t1-009 (R-t1-05-02) stream and F-t1-008 (R-t1-05-01) signals, rendered by a toast stack (max N, timeout, pause on hover, in-place update for agent progress). Compute the title and favicon badge and setAppBadge from the same unread map as the sidebar, applying updates only on newer sequence numbers. Sounds via Web Audio when the tab is visible, with settings in the F-t1-008 (R-t1-05-04) preferences. Keep scope to agent-attention, not Slack-level polish.
dependencies: F-t1-039 (R-t1-11-03) (route resolver for protocol and share handlers)
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (manifest, service worker, toasts, badge) with Application Plane (push subscriptions and fan-out in notification-core)
items.risks: [R-t1-11-01] Stale service-worker caches pin users to an old bundle (pair with F-t1-024 (R-t1-11-04)), and the current nginx rules would cache sw.js for a year unless exempted; iOS web push works only for installed PWAs; payloads and cached responses must never carry message text from ZDR Spaces; badge counts must respect per-Space mute. [R-t1-05-05] Session-less service-worker fetch needs a narrowly scoped token; iOS web push limits; any third-party push provider needs ZDR proof even for a constant payload; approving effectful actions out of context; preview text leaking ZDR content into the OS notification centre; browsers block repeated permission prompts permanently. [R-t1-05-08] Toast spam from agents (rate limits must apply); badge drifting from the sidebar if computed separately; the Space definition lists 'notification polish' as a non-goal (docs/space-defenition.md:352-353), so keep this minimal; native tray and OS focus cues wait for a desktop shell.

items.title: Room automations: create schedules, watches, calendar and event triggers from the room, with fire outcomes, recipient consent, goals and run traces
items.summary: The backend already re-authorizes every schedule fire through Control; finish the product around it. Expose schedule create, pause and test-run in the Work tab through spaces.* actions (also agent-callable), finish the Watch primitive so process output and external events wake the room, add a calendar-event trigger beside cron (prep before a followed meeting, follow-up after) on the existing calendar read action plus approval-gated event creation, and show a fire log with an outcome vocabulary (ok, silent, deferred, failed, refused), stored recipient acceptance, skip-with-note when a member left, pause while nobody reads, optional goal runs with a verifier, and run traces with cancel, steer and retry. Let agents draft automations as triggers for a human to approve rather than cloning a no-code builder.
items.whyItMatters: Scheduled and event-triggered agent work is table stakes among the agent references (4 of 5) and workflow automation in Teams, Slack and buzz; creation lives in Settings today and the Work tab is read-only.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm; qm (fire keys, outcomes, loops with gates, runAs and recipient rules, goals governor); grokbot (routine panel, pause-while-away); teams (reports with reviewers); Grok Bot (SRC, medium): calendar as an agent trigger source plus approval-gated scheduling and prep packs
others: Teams (REA): native calendar and Outlook add-in
Slack and QM: integrations or an agent skill only
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-06-06] Workflow automation: 3 of 5 (table-stakes); crons, loops and watches: qm only (unique) [R-t1-07-10] Scheduled/event-triggered work 4 of 5 (table-stakes); per-fire reauthorization and consent 2 of 5 (differentiator); goals with verifier 1 of 5 (unique); reviewed reports 1 of 5 (unique) [R-t1-03-08] 4 of 5 (Teams native; Grok Bot, Slack and QM via integration or agent skill); table-stakes only in the integration-level sense.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-06-06] qm crons support timezone, one-shot and sub-day intervals, destinations, runAs modes, a fire log and shared-scope editing; deterministic fire keys and slot claims through a job queue. Loops add a playbook, ledger, ship gates and a governor that quarantines on consecutive failures (shadow run before arming). Watches turn background process output into new turns. Slack Workflow Builder adds broad triggers and steps, run history and AI-drafted workflows; buzz's YAML engine with step traces is the best open implementation. [R-t1-07-10] QM: deterministic fireKey per (cron, scheduled time), a thread per fire, outcomes running|ok|silent|deferred|failed|refused, a stranded-fire sweep, webhook ingest acked after durable store, Loop items with gates auto|hold; runAs owner|scopeFloor|scopeShared with membership skip notes at fire time, audience built from the current members and recipient acceptance stored. Grok Bot pauses routines whose output is unread and asks on return. QM goals: GoalRecord{objective, floor, capTokens, governor} with a governor every 3 rounds or 30 min returning continue|complete|step_back|pause. Teams reports: schedule {once|daily|weekly|monthly, approvers}, draft -> reviewers edit/approve -> share to room. [R-t1-03-08] OAuth calendar connector reads events; triggers {event or series, offset} start agent runs; a schedule_meeting tool produces an approval card "Schedule this meeting?" and then a provider action; repeat model {frequency, interval, days_of_week, month_day, weekday_of_month, time, timezone}.

apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/cron/sweeper.go:148-152 (fire key = next fire time, idempotency key = schedule id + fire key)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/orchestrator-core/cmd/activities/scheduled_run_authorizer.go:17-60 (execution intent bound to template digest, fresh Control authority per run)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/watch/watch.go:1-40 (Watch: a standing intent bound to one resource, one Space, one member's authority, cursor-based)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:421-590 (Control-decided schedule creation inside a personal Space)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceWorkPanel.tsx:171-189 (Work tab lists schedules and their run threads)

apps/Ingestion Plane/integration-corev2/internal/actions/calendar_read.go:1-60 and service.go:208,294 (SRC: read-only calendar.events for Outlook via Graph and Google, Europe/Oslo windows, paging token; its header says live proof against a provider is still pending)

Baseline (SRC): agent cron schedules exist and are filtered by space_ref in the gateway Space work projection
verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-06-06] Space schedules exist with a Control create decision bound to a template digest and a separate fire decision per tick, but creation lives in Settings and the Work tab is read-only. The watch surface is mounted in capability-core but its routes require a user principal (humanCaller rejects service identities: a watch belongs to a person), and watches are not exposed to rooms (S4.3). Background processes are listed but do not wake the room; there are no message/reaction/join triggers, no loops, ledger or governor, no run trace in the room, no cancel/steer/retry (S4.5) and no destinations beyond the room (S4.4). There is no per-agent personal home; the Work tab and Activity cover review. [R-t1-07-10] Per-fire reauthorization, fire keys and a Watch primitive are shipped (SRC). Missing or unconfirmed: create/pause/test-run from the room UI, an outcome vocabulary and silence sentinel visible to people, stored recipient consent, pause-while-unread, event triggers wired from Watch to runs, goal governor, scheduled reports with reviewers. [R-t1-03-08] The comparator recorded this as absent, but the read side exists: an agent can already list calendar events through integration-corev2. Missing: any write operation (create or update event), a calendar-event trigger beside cron, a prep-pack run template, a Space surface for upcoming meetings, and live verification of the read action. Writing needs extra OAuth scope and a reconnect.

items.approach: [R-t1-06-06] Frontend Plane: schedule create/edit in the Work tab via spaces.* actions with a Control decision per create and per fire. Model Plane capability-core: finish S4.3 (process-output adapter first, one adapter per PR) so a watch can be created under the delegating person on behalf of an agent run and wake the room; add Space triggers beside schedules (webhook per F-t1-047 (R-t1-06-03), room events later). Frontend Work cockpit (S4.5): run trace per automation, per-agent lens filtered to the viewer's delegations, cancel/steer/retry. Let agents draft automations for human approval; expose approval steps only once suspend/persist/resume is one tested path. Add loops with a human ship gate and a cost governor last. [R-t1-07-10] Frontend: create/pause/test-run in the Work tab by extending the existing Control-decided create path (spaces.rs inject_personal_schedule_create_context) from personal Spaces to room Spaces. Model Plane capability-core: a fire-log outcome enum and silence sentinel, recipient acceptance stored per schedule, skip with a note when a member is gone (audience from current members at fire time), pause schedules whose output stays unread and ask on return, and Watch events as triggers that reuse the same per-fire reauthorization with turn_origin=automation. Optional goal record {objective, token cap, governor every N rounds: continue|complete|step_back|pause} with an independent verifier. Reports: a schedule whose output is an approval card for reviewers and then a share-to-room step (builds on item F-t1-010 (R-t1-07-05)). [R-t1-03-08] Model Plane (capability-core schedules and watches): new trigger kind calendar_event {connection, event or series, offset} implemented first as a poller over windowed calendar.events reads, no webhook dependency; the run executes in the Space with the room agent. integration-corev2: add calendar.create_event as is_write behind the existing effect-bound authorization (payload digest, idempotency key); Frontend: approval card "Schedule this meeting?" in the room and an Upcoming meetings read-only section in the Work tab. Prep pack uses Space thread history plus Data Plane retrieval under the Space decision. Meeting links found in events are offered to F-t1-066 (R-t1-03-04) with consent.

items.title: Space tool cockpit and reliable tool connections: per-room MCP enablement, per-binding allowlist, credential mode and scoped consent, health states and person-bound sign-in links
items.summary: Let a Space manager enable org-approved MCP servers for a room, set a per-binding tool allowlist and choose per-user or shared credentials, with plain-language consent cards bound to the exact Space, agent and tool, by extending the Model Gateway MCP registry (plan items S3.4 and S3.6). Make tool use fail visibly and recover: a per-server health state machine with reconnect and backoff, separate idle and total call budgets, a typed result union with recovery hints (needs_auth, retry_after, fresh schema), a room-visible 'needs sign-in' card, and person-bound OAuth consent links whose callback verifies the signer.
items.whyItMatters: An MCP registry with shared or per-user credentials is table stakes among the agent references (Grok Bot, buzz, QM). Verevon's registry, OAuth 2.1 and argument validation are good, but nothing is scoped to a Space, so room agents either get no tools or org-wide tools.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm; grokbot
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-06-02] MCP registry: 3 of 5 (table-stakes among agent products); container-scoped consent: Teams only (unique) [R-t1-06-08] MCP runtime policy: Grok Bot only (unique); connected apps by consent link: 2 of 5 (grokbot, qm; differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-06-02] qm's server record carries credentialScope shared|per_user (resolved by the runtime from the initiating principal's keychain, never from tool arguments), a toolAllowlist and a readOnly flag; tools reach the model filtered by allowlist and binding policy. Grok Bot adds per-tool permissions and the richest config schema. Teams RSC stores consent per (app, container) by a container owner, uses about 106 plain-language permission strings with _Chat/_Group/_User scope, and intersects token scope with the caller's ACL. [R-t1-06-08] Grok Bot routes URL servers through a backend executor and stdio servers through the box, caches discovery 24 h with background refresh, reconnects fast and periodically with 10 s health probes, bounds calls at 2 min idle and 60 min total, and returns a union success|error|rejected|permission_denied|tool_not_found|server_not_found with typed McpError {needs_auth, retry_after_ms, recovery{fresh_input_schema, available_tools}}. qm stores a consent link {principal, toolkit, return URL, expiry}, completes auth only for the signed-in principal, and checks owner, active status and tool version before every call, never retrying an uncertain execution and excluding arguments from audit.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-06-02] Model Gateway registers, lists, deletes and shares MCP servers (Private/Shared/Org scope, optional allowlist at connect, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, one auto-detecting connect route). A grep of spaces.rs and src/features/spaces finds no MCP reference: no per-room enablement, no per-binding tool allowlist, no per-user versus shared credential choice, no consent card. Owner agent-action grants exist but only tickets.create is correlated to receipts; per-conversation grants are a stub; the credential broker (S3.4) is planned only. [R-t1-06-08] Spot-check (SRC): Model Gateway validates arguments against the tool schema before the call (equal to Grok Bot's repair), caches tenant MCP discovery with 6 s discovery and 10 s HTTP timeouts, and runs OAuth 2.1 with a server-side callback, which avoids the loopback problem. Not found: reconnect/backoff and health probing, idle versus total call budgets (10 s is short for long tools), typed recovery hints surfaced to the model, per-message MCP config, sandbox-resident stdio servers. integration-corev2 has an org-level OAuth catalogue (Microsoft, Slack, Google, Notion, GitHub, Shopify, Stripe, LinkedIn and more) with PKCE and read actions; missing for Spaces are consent links minted from a room for a given person, per-call owner/status/version evidence and Space credential grants (S3.4).

items.approach: [R-t1-06-02] Model Plane (model-gateway / capability-core): add space_ref enablement and a per-binding tool allowlist to the MCP server rows, and resolve credentialScope (shared versus requesting principal) at call time from the requester. Control Plane: generalise owner-grant decisions to (principal or agent, action or tool id, Space ref, expiry, once/session/standing), keep grant mutation on human-only APIs as S3.6 requires, and reuse existing secret stores (S3.4 says do not add a QM-style keychain). Frontend Agent tab: list org-activated servers, enable per room, show health and last use with a revoke action, and render a Teams-style consent card in the room the first time an agent needs a tool. Never grant more than the org activated or the server owner shared. Phase 1 (enablement, allowlist, credential scope) is M; consent cards and the cockpit view are the rest. [R-t1-06-08] Model Plane model-gateway: per-server health state machine with backoff, separate idle and total timeouts per tool, a typed error union with recovery hints returned to the model, and honouring Retry-After. Frontend: a 'needs sign-in' card in the room linking to the existing server-side OAuth flow, plus health shown in the Space cockpit (this item (R-t1-06-02)). Ingestion Plane integration-corev2: person-bound consent links with a callback that checks the signed-in principal, per-call checks of owner, status and version, no retry when an outcome is uncertain, arguments excluded from audit. Control Plane grants tie a connection to a Space binding. Stdio MCP servers run only inside the Space sandbox once S3.2 lands. The Model proposes provider actions and Ingestion executes them after the authority check.
dependencies: S3.4 Space credential grants and broker
S3.6 cockpit projection of MCP/plugin state
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (MCP registry and runtime); Control Plane (grants); Ingestion Plane (connector consent); Frontend Plane (Agent-tab cockpit)
items.risks: [R-t1-06-02] A shared credential lets any room member act as its owner (needs an explicit warning and a read-only default); consent fatigue and grant sprawl without expiry; a private MCP server must not be widened by Space linkage. [R-t1-06-08] Retry storms against third-party servers (respect Retry-After); wrong-person binding via forwarded links; over-broad OAuth scopes; non-idempotent calls retried after an uncertain outcome.

items.title: Agents and AI answers over room history under the asker's authority: search_space_history and open_space_entry tools, cited answers over messages and Space knowledge
items.summary: Give room agents search_space_history and open_space_entry tools on a new capability, backed by the Session Core index, each call running under the Control decision of the human who triggered the turn (never an agent-wide grant), with a rule that stops an agent quoting member-private results into the shared room. On top, let a question in Space search produce a generated answer with linked citations (entry deep links and documents) composed from Data Plane retrieval and message search under the asker's decision, plus an 'Ask agent about this' message action.
items.whyItMatters: Agents cannot read room history beyond the current transcript, and grounded answers cover documents and wiki only. Slack and QM show the safe pattern (search as the asking human, references not copies); Verevon's signed decisions are a stronger primitive than Slack's action token.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm; slack
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-04-03] 3 of 5 sources for the history tool (common); 2 of 5 for delegated-authority search (differentiator) [R-t1-04-06] 2 of 5 sources; differentiator (buzz has no AI answers)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-04-03] qm sessions.search returns {sessionId, entry seq} references without widening read access; the history tool does an all-terms keyword search or reopens one entry by seq, including content compacted out of context. GrokBot adds scopes (this chat, earlier, everything) and a prompt rule to trust the newest result and ask when results conflict. Slack Real-time Search mints an action token from the triggering event with per-content scopes, limits results to what the user can access, and forbids storing results. [R-t1-04-06] A question-shaped query triggers hybrid keyword plus semantic retrieval restricted to content the asker can access (files, canvases, clip transcripts, connected docs); top passages go to the model with citation ids and the answer renders with linked citations above the normal results. Teams adds channel citations and a select-text "Ask Copilot" hand-off with prefilled prompts (summarise, flag decisions, help me reply).

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-04-03] Agents have knowledge_search (cap.retrieval.query over Data Plane documents) but no tool that searches or reopens room or thread history; a grep of execution-core in this step found no search_space or space_history symbol. Signed Control decisions (subject, Space, audience, 2-minute lifetime, payload digest) already exist for grounded document retrieval, but there is no equivalent decision for message-history search and no rule against quoting a member's private results into the room. Whether Space room turns offer knowledge_search at all was not confirmed. [R-t1-04-06] Grounded room turns (policy-gated retrieval) exist, but retrieval covers Space-bound documents and wiki only, not room messages or agent outputs. There is no answer-in-search surface for Space content (the gateway search/answer/stream route is the web-search answer path) and no select-text hand-off. The comparator reports Space knowledge as empty in practice because no import writes space_ref; this step found a Space import chain in code (gateway personal_import_ingress_decision, Control personal_import_decision.go, documents-api space_import.go verifying the decision), so whether Space documents are actually populated is unconfirmed.

items.approach: [R-t1-04-03] Model Plane execution-core: add the two tools, register them in capability_policy.rs next to knowledge_search and in binding allowed_tools, add a system-prompt snippet (prefer newest, cite thread_id+seq, ask when two results conflict, treat retrieved messages as data). They call Session Core SearchSpaceMessages with the turn decision. Control Plane: issue a search decision for the invoking subject per turn, and define the rule when several humans trigger one run (intersection of authorities is safest). Add an output filter that blocks posting hits marked private into a shared Space. Exclude ZDR turns. [R-t1-04-06] Model Plane composes the answer: two tools (Data Plane retrieval, Session Core message search) called with the asker's Control decision, grounded-answer prompt requiring citation ids, citations rendered as deep links via F-t1-018 (R-t1-04-02). Reuse the existing retrieval policy bit (retrieval_read_entitled) and keep its degrade-to-ungrounded behaviour on 403. Frontend: answer card above search results and a message action "Ask agent about this". Index agent outputs only where ZDR allows.
dependencies: Control decision type for message-history search
Binding allowed_tools and capability policy registration
Explicit rule for whose authority applies when several humans trigger one agent run
Populated Space documents (confirm the import path writes space_ref)
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (tools, capability policy, answer composition); Control Plane (search decision and multi-human authority rule)
items.risks: [R-t1-04-03] An agent quoting one member's private context into the room; prompt injection through retrieved messages; ambiguity of whose authority applies on multi-human runs. [R-t1-04-06] Hallucinated citations; leaking content the asker cannot read through the summary; cost per query.

items.title: Entry references and permalinks: one entity router for message, thread and run links, deep links honoured, Space-role pins, visibility-preserving fork, quote and forward
items.summary: Introduce one reference to a room entry (space_ref, thread_id, seq) that the server resolves under the viewer's audience revision, and one SPA route table of (entity, action) pairs with /spaces/:id/m/:entry and /spaces/:id/runs/:run; notification clicks, push actions, agent-posted links and protocol/share handlers all call it, and message links page back until the target is loaded. Build pins by Space role (lifted above the timeline, capped, pinnable by an agent), a Session Core fork that copies only what the forking viewer can see, quoted replies with tombstones, and forward with a decision per destination.
items.whyItMatters: Deep links are table stakes in four references. Activity already emits ?thread_id links that SpacePage ignores, pins are author-only flags that are not lifted, and fork is an open S1.7 checkbox; one router avoids every surface inventing its own link handling.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (entity link chips and deep links); qm (visibility-preserving fork, capped surface-neutral pins); slack and teams (header shelf, quote with tombstone, forward); teams (toast clicks, deep links and lifecycle events normalised into one (entity, action) command) with qm (?seq= pages older history until the target message is loaded and highlights it)
others: slack (maps the team in a link to a workspace the user belongs to; holds links until the web app is ready)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-11] Pins 3 of 5 (common); deep links, fork, quoted replies and forward each 2 of 5 (differentiators) [R-t1-11-03] 4 of 5 sources (slack, grokbot, qm, teams) = table-stakes.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-11] Deep link: URL scheme /spaces/{ref}/t/{thread}/e/{seq}; the router opens the exact entry; known hosts render as chips; external crawlers get minimal metadata. Pins: room_pins(room, entry_seq or note, pinned_by, at) capped (409 pin_limit), room editor and above, shown in the header and info pane. Fork: fork(thread, upto_seq) reads the viewer-folded transcript (or the intersection across members under a roster lock), appends copies to a fresh thread and records forkedFrom and forkBoundarySeq. Quote: the message carries quoted_message_id plus a server-resolved snapshot; on render it re-resolves and shows a tombstone or a cannot-verify marker. Forward: a new entry with a forwarded_from chip and size and count validation; access to the source is rechecked. [R-t1-11-03] Route table of entity types x actions; resolver checks membership before navigating and fails closed; message links load the transcript window around the target id then scroll and highlight; notifications reuse the exact same command object.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-01-11] Activity rows link to ?thread_id=...#chat but SpacePage never reads thread_id, so deep links land on the room only. Pin is a thread-level flag that only the post's author can set, and the timeline re-sorts chronologically so pins are flagged, not lifted; no pinned section, bookmark shelf or agent pin (room-wide pin by non-authors is a known open item in the page audit). Reply targets a thread, not a quoted entry. No forward. Fork is listed as open work in S1.7 and has no code. [R-t1-11-03] Space plus tab is linkable (/spaces/:spaceId with hash tabs, replaceState on tab change). Chat has a validated /chat?thread_id= deep link that resolves through the owner-bound transcript route (fail-closed parser; a good pattern to copy). No message/entry permalink, agent-run link inside a Space or shared command router exists (grep for permalink, messageId=, ?message= finds nothing); notifications carry a free-form href string rather than a typed route.

items.approach: [R-t1-01-11] Frontend: SpacePage reads thread and entry params and scrolls to the entry; entry chips; a minimal, ZDR-aware metadata endpoint for external unfurls that never reveals private titles. Application Plane: room_pins (Space-role authorization, not thread owner; cap with a typed refusal) plus an agent tool to pin; fix the timeline ordering so pinned posts are lifted. Model Plane Session Core: fork RPC built on the existing audience-revision filtering (grpc.rs:5340-5360), copying only rows the forking viewer, or all current members, can see and recording forked_from and boundary_seq; entry field quoted_entry_seq resolved reader-side with a tombstone; forward creates a new entry with provenance and carries no source-room retrieval grants. Every resolution checks the viewer's audience revision first. [R-t1-11-03] Frontend Plane: a typed route builder/reader module (modelled on chat-thread-deep-link.ts) used by the Solid router, notifications, push and agent-posted links; add the two Space routes in App.tsx. Server side comes from this item (R-t1-01-11) (stable (space_ref, thread_id, seq) reference resolved under the viewer audience revision) and an Application Plane read-around-entry call; the resolver never widens an owner-plane ACL, and unfurls expose no titles before the ACL check. Notification payloads should carry entity refs, not hrefs.
dependencies: Control decision per destination Space for forward

items.risks: [R-t1-01-11] A pin, quote or snapshot must not reveal entries outside a viewer's audience (do not store denormalized quote text). Copying content on fork under ZDR; intersection correctness across members. Forward across Spaces is the riskiest for the authority model, so do it last or leave it. [R-t1-11-03] Links must not leak titles or previews to non-members; ZDR Spaces must not keep resolvable entry ids beyond retention; never execute actions from a link without user confirmation.

items.title: Per-thread serialized, leased agent run queue and member-safe mid-run steering for multi-member rooms
items.summary: Verify first, then build: write a test where two members post to the same thread while a turn is running, and confirm what Session Core and execution-core do. Then add a per-thread run claim (at most one running run per thread, lease with heartbeat, reaper that requeues or parks after repeated crashes) and a tool ledger keyed by (run, attempt, call index) so replays do not repeat side effects. Extend the existing mid-run queued input from the Chat path to Space turns so another member's message becomes a steer or a follow-up at the next tool-round boundary, with stop still aborting.
items.whyItMatters: In a room several people and agents can talk to the same thread at once, so concurrent turns, lost steering and duplicated effects are real correctness risks, not edge cases. QM shows the pattern for serialization and crash recovery; Verevon already has model-classified steering for single-user Chat that is not yet wired into Spaces.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (unique one-running-per-session index, SKIP LOCKED claim, lease heartbeat at ttl/3, abort after 3 lost beats, reaper with crash-loop parking, ToolLedger; routeWake returning engage, steer or drop with a durable RunSignalStore)
others: Grok Bot (Temporal-based durable harness as an alternative)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 for a durable per-conversation run queue (differentiator); 1 of 5 for mid-run steering (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: runs table (session_id, status, lease_token, lease_expires_at); claim = UPDATE ... WHERE id = (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) guarded by a unique partial index on (session_id) WHERE status = running; worker heartbeats; reaper requeues expired leases and parks after N crashes; effectful tool calls go through once(runId, attempt, callIndex) which returns the cached result on replay. Incoming message for a thread with a running run is classified engage, steer or drop; steer is appended to a signal store read at step boundaries; unconsumed steers start a follow-up run.

verevonToday.gap: SRC verified for steering: model-gateway has mid-run queued input delivered at a tool-round boundary, where the model classifies redirect versus follow-up, keyed by request_id and bound to the tenant and user, in-memory and single-replica (its own note says multi-replica needs a NATS subject keyed by request id). It is wired into the Chat page and controller but no reference was found in src/features/spaces. Stop is shipped in the Space composer. Per-thread run serialization, leases and a reaper in Session Core or execution-core were not found by grep (only FOR UPDATE row locks on threads and runs), so concurrent-turn behaviour is unknown.

items.approach: Model Plane. (1) Characterise current behaviour with a two-member concurrency test. (2) Session Core / execution-core: per-thread run claim with lease, heartbeat and reaper, plus a tool ledger keyed by Quarry execution receipts for effectful actions. (3) Steering: promote queued_input from request-id to run-id keyed signals stored durably or routed over a NATS subject to the replica holding the stream; gateway route for Space steer gated by a fresh Control append decision per message so each steer is attributed and audited; extend SpaceRoomComposer so a member can send while a turn runs (queued, steer) instead of being locked. Coordinate with F-t1-032 (R-t1-01-08) which plans queue-and-steer in the composer.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Queueing changes perceived latency in busy rooms and needs steering to feel right. Steer text needs its own append decision and audit, and a policy for who may steer another member's turn (queued_input is bound to the requesting user today). Do not widen owner-plane ACLs through the steer path.

items.title: One command layer on the typed action registry: Cmd/Ctrl+K palette and quick switcher, platform slash commands, shortcut sheet, then a unified 'To:' picker
items.summary: Wrap the typed ActionDescriptor registry plus navigation commands in one command registry {id, title, hotkey, when, run} with a single key handler, Ctrl/Cmd+1-9 Space switching and a '?' shortcut sheet. Rebuild Cmd/Ctrl+K as a palette with fuzzy match over rooms, threads, agents, people and human-eligible actions (web search becomes a palette mode). Add a platform section to the '/' picker (invite, mute, pin, schedule, summarise, pause agent) executed through the same dispatcher and answered ephemerally, then message actions that hand a message to a room agent. Once DMs and a directory exist, add a 'To:' field that finds or creates agents, people and groups.
items.whyItMatters: Cmd/Ctrl+K opens web search today and '/' lists skills only. Verevon's typed action registry, shared by human clicks and model-initiated actions, is a base no reference has: one vocabulary for people and agents.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm; grokbot (every shell action is a registered command with id and hotkey, consumed by one hotkey layer and a mod+K palette); Slack for the keyboard model (switcher, unread navigation, All-unreads, F6 section cycling); Grok Bot for hold-to-reveal hints and the "To:" picker; teams
others: teams (user-assignable shortcuts, slash menu as palette)
qm (hold Cmd to reveal 1-9 session shortcuts)
Teams and Buzz almost certainly ship quick switchers (INF; no records)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-04-04] 3 of 5 sources; common [R-t1-11-05] 4 of 5 sources (buzz, grokbot, teams, qm) = table-stakes; palette itself in 2 of 5. [R-t1-12-07] switcher 2 of 5 in records (Slack, Grok Bot; common, under-counted); "To:" picker 1 of 5 (Grok Bot; unique) [R-t1-06-05] Slash commands: 3 of 5 (table-stakes); message actions and unfurl: Teams only (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-04-04] A global hotkey opens an overlay; input is debounced 150 ms and ignored under 2 characters; two parallel requests (conversation entries, resources) render as groups ordered by recency; Enter navigates or executes. Commands come from a typed registry {id, title, hotkey, run, when} so the palette and the shortcuts share one source (GrokBot has 17 command ids with hotkeys). [R-t1-11-05] Command registry {id, label, hotkey, when, run}; one keydown handler resolves hotkeys (capture phase for globals); a palette fuzzy-searches commands and entities (Spaces, people, agents); custom bindings stored per user. [R-t1-12-07] A global keydown router with scope (app, room, composer) and conflict rules; a palette component with fuzzy match over a combined directory; unread navigation iterates the cross-room unread list; hold-to-reveal arms a ~500 ms timer on modifier keydown, cancelled by other modifiers, keyup or blur, then shows numeric badges bound to Ctrl+1..9. Picker: a recipient token input over agents, team agents and people, free text offers "Create <name> agent", more than one recipient creates a group conversation. [R-t1-06-05] A command registry {name, description, args schema, owner platform|app, visibility}; composer autosuggest merges built-ins, app commands and recents (Teams has the richest built-in set); Slack defines the invocation contract (trigger_id, response_url, ephemeral versus in-channel response). Teams message actions are a context-menu entry posting the message to the app; unfurling registers a domain and the app returns an expandable card preview on paste.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/UI_UX_AUDIT_2026-09-29.md:71 (the CTRL+K overlay lacks a focus trap, focus return and arrow/Enter keys)

apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/lib/use-chat-shortcuts.ts:11 and apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceCockpit.tsx:170-179 (composer keys and tablist arrows only)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/actions/ActionCommand.tsx:1-40 (typed action registry that can feed the palette)
verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-04-04] Cmd/Ctrl+K opens the top web search (CoreNavbar.tsx:122, use-chat-shortcuts.ts:11). ActionCommand is a per-button component, not a palette, and there is no jump-to-room, agent or thread overlay. [R-t1-11-05] Basic keys exist (roving tablist focus, picker arrows, Enter to send), and Cmd/Ctrl+K plus "/" open web search with Escape closing overlays. There is no Space quick switcher, no command registry or palette, no shortcut help sheet and no custom bindings. items.approach: [R-t1-04-04] Frontend Plane Solid overlay bound to Cmd/Ctrl+K. Sources: the Space list, the room roster, the org agent registry (installations), recent threads, and action-registry commands (14 spaces.* actions) filtered by the viewer's permissions and the same model-eligibility and human-only rules. Add a command shape {id, title, hotkey, when} to the registry so shortcuts and palette share one source. Message hits join when F-t1-018 (R-t1-04-01) ships. [R-t1-11-05] Frontend Plane: a registry module that adapts shared/actions descriptors (id, label, risk, requiresApproval, zod schemas) and navigation commands; replace the ad-hoc keydown handlers in CoreNavbar.tsx and the Space cockpit with the one layer; execution of any action goes through the existing ActionCommand preview/approval path so authority stays in the owning plane (approval-required actions never run straight from the palette). Move web search into the palette as a provider (coordinate with this item (R-t1-04-04)) and share Ctrl/Cmd+1-9 org switching with F-t1-055 (R-t1-02-12). [R-t1-12-07] Frontend Plane. Phase 1 (S): extend the existing overlay shell into a palette fed by the rooms/threads/agents lists and human-eligible registry actions, fixing its keyboard model (trap, restore, listbox with arrows and Enter) per the UI/UX audit, and rebind Cmd/Ctrl+K with web search as a mode. Phase 2 (M): the "To:" picker over the Control roster (people) and Application agent bindings; creation still runs the two-step Application -> Control lifecycle and renders as pending, with born-narrow agent policy unchanged. [R-t1-06-05] Frontend Plane: populate a command section from the action registry (each action already has a zod schema and risk level), reuse the shared keyboard picker used by @ and /, execute via the existing dispatcher so audit and authority are identical, and render ephemeral results locally. Keep the structured skill_ids contract for skills. Message actions and unfurl follow F-t1-026 (R-t1-06-04) cards; unfurl fetches through Quarry honouring egress and ZDR.
