items.title: Read state, presence and personal follow-ups: per-thread read frontier, mark unread, global presence and agent availability, saved items, reminders and snooze
items.summary: Extend the room-level read marker into a per-thread server-side read frontier with mark-unread, a first-unread divider and jump-to-first-unread, and opt-in read receipts that degrade in large rooms. Add global presence and status (online, away, do-not-disturb, custom text with expiry) and agent availability derived from run state. Add saved items and a reminder primitive {owner, not_before, sealed target ref, note} with presets, firing into the Home Reminders slice; snooze reuses it and humans can ask an agent to 'ping me at 9 if X is still open'. Store references only so ZDR rooms stay content-free.
items.whyItMatters: Per-thread read state is table stakes in four references and reminders in three; Verevon has a good durable room-level marker but nothing finer, and no reminders outside support tickets.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (server-side read frontier with manual-unread overrides); teams (optimistic mark-read and richest availability model); Buzz (privacy-preserving design); Teams for shared room reminders
others: Teams (reminders visible to all room members)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-09] Read state 4 of 5 sources (table-stakes); presence 3 of 5 (common); saved items and reminders 2 of 5; urgent re-notify 1 of 5 (unique) [R-t1-05-09] 3 of 5 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-09] read_frontier(subject, room, thread, last_read_seq) lives server-side; unread is every entry with seq above the frontier; manual unread moves the frontier back; the client marks optimistically and batches network calls (about 3 per 8 s); receipts are cut off above about 20 participants. Presence is a lease: a heartbeat every 60 s sets a key with a 180 s TTL, OS idle moves to away, a manual status carries text, emoji, expiry and availability, and DND suppresses notifications. Saved items carry a due date and a reminder scheduler; Urgent messages re-notify every N minutes for M minutes until read. [R-t1-05-09] Buzz encrypts the reminder target and note to the author and leaves only a not_before time public, so the server can schedule without knowing what it is about; due reminders surface under Needs action and can wake agents. The reminder id is at least 128 bits of randomness and status is pending, done or cancelled. Teams adds shared room reminders where anyone can delete for all.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-01-09] Room-level lastReadAt marker only (durable and cross-device, which is good); no per-thread frontier, no jump-to-first-unread, no mark-unread, no receipts. Presence is room-scoped online/typing/offline with a 30 s TTL and polling; no global status, away, DND, custom status, or agent working/waiting states. No saved items or reminders in Space. Whether notification-core supports priority re-notify was not verified. [R-t1-05-09] No Space or message reminders. Greps found snooze only for support tickets (InboxPage snoozed_until), ticket follow-up in conversation-core, and the org-deletion reminder notification; nothing in src/features/spaces, capability-core or convex-core. capability-core already has Space-scoped schedules with Control decisions that could host the due-time trigger.

items.approach: [R-t1-01-09] Application Plane (Convex): add a per-thread last_read_seq to spaceReadMarkers (schema.ts:845); gateway read route (spaces.rs:1894-1916) takes thread and seq; client marks optimistically and batches; Frontend adds the divider and jump. Presence: a global per-subject presence lease and status table (content-free rows, own-row writes only, kept from the current design), agent availability projected from Model Plane run state; DND honored by notification-core. Later phase: per-user saved_items (access rechecked on read) with reminders through Control schedules; an escalation policy in notification-core for approval-wait entries. Coordinate with category 05 (C-t1-05-007, 013, 019), category 07 (C-t1-07-017) and category 09 (C-t1-09-014) so one presence and unread model is built. [R-t1-05-09] Application Plane: store reminders with refs only; fire due items via the capability-core scheduler or a notification-core delayed job; due items enter the inbox Reminders slice (F-t1-009 (R-t1-05-03)) and respect DND (F-t1-059 (R-t1-05-06)). Frontend Plane: a reminder menu on messages and threads, snooze on inbox items. Add an agent-callable action in the registry so an agent can create a reminder for its owner within explicit grants.
dependencies: F-t1-001 (R-t1-01-01) shared threads (per-thread unread needs them)
Model Plane run-state feed for agent availability
capability-core scheduler or notification-core delayed job
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (convex-core read state, presence, reminders) with Model Plane (run-state feed)
items.risks: [R-t1-01-09] Read receipts and presence reveal behavior, so make receipts opt-in and keep presence content-free. Saved references must re-check access when read. Notification fatigue from urgent re-notify. [R-t1-05-09] Shared room reminders need an owner and delete rule; agent-created reminders need a cap so they cannot be used to spam a person.

items.title: Room moderation: report, queue, tombstones, user block, and timeout or ban that also stops the person's agents
items.summary: Add a Report action on every room message (human or agent-authored), a private moderation queue for owners and managers, and signed moderation actions (dismiss, delete with a visible tombstone, timeout, remove, ban) that notify the reporter and the author. Add a per-user block list. Control refuses to issue decisions for a suspended member and for agents owned by a suspended member, and the suspension event drops live subscriptions and in-flight runs.
items.whyItMatters: Rooms that mix humans and agents need a way to remove harmful or leaked content, including agent output, and to stop a misbehaving participant. Without it Spaces cannot be opened to larger teams or guests. Because personal agents act like humans, a ban that does not cascade to the person's agents becomes a bypass.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz
others: teams (best end-user side: report concern, block, chat-request expiry)
slack and teams moderation controls exist in the products but were not recorded in this category
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Moderation workflow: 2 of 5 (buzz, teams); ban cascade to owned agents: 1 of 5 (buzz). Differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A reports table (target, reporter hidden from the author, reason, status open/processing/resolved/dismissed/escalated) feeds an admin queue grouped by target. Actions are signed commands that write a tombstone visible in the room and notify everyone affected. A per-user block list filters delivery. The ban verdict is checked at authentication for the principal and for its owner (agent to owner link), fails closed on error, and audits which principal matched; a timeout is a write-deny until expires_at and a ban disconnects all sessions.

evidence: apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/schema.ts:546-716 (Space tables; lifecycle has a suspended state for the Space only; no report, block, tombstone or member-sanction table; a grep for report, tombstone, moderat, ban, mute found none for Spaces)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces and apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs (grep for report/moderation/tombstone found no Space moderation route or UI)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/moderation.rs:1-20 (injection and PII handling for model-bound content only)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/migrations/0032_space_membership_revocations.sql (session-core already consumes Control membership_revoked events, the hook a suspension cascade can reuse)
verevonToday.gap: No way to report or remove a message, no per-member timeout or ban, no block list, and nothing that ties an agent's right to act to its owner's standing in the Space.

items.approach: Application Plane convex-core: tables for reports, blocks and sanctions plus a tombstone message kind that replaces content and triggers purge in search and notification payloads; gateway routes under /api/v1/spaces/{space_ref}/reports and /sanctions gated by room role. Control user-core: a moderation decision class (signed, bound to subject, Space and audience revision) and suspended_until on space_memberships; decision issuance refuses a suspended subject and any agent whose owner is suspended (needs the agent to owner link from category 02); publish the sanction as a membership event so gateway, Convex and session-core drop subscriptions and runs. Frontend: Report on the message menu (agent messages included), admin queue in Space settings, tombstone rendering, Block in the member menu. Record every action in audit-core as metadata only.
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (reports, tombstones, blocks) with Control Plane (signed moderation decision, suspension)
items.risks: Removal must propagate to search and graph indexes and notification payloads. Reporter privacy. A fail-closed ban check must alert instead of silently locking people out on a transient error. Under ZDR a report can store only a reference and hash, not content.

items.title: Credential custody and outward actions: secrets broker, per-person connectors, draft-first sends, bounded cross-room reach
items.summary: Give room agents the ability to use credentials without ever seeing them: a broker in the Ingestion Plane that attaches secrets server-side with host/method/path pinning, https only and no redirects, a one-time secret-drop form that bypasses chat and the model, and Control grants (once|session|standing) bound to the Space audience. On top of that: per-person connector accounts for room agents, draft-first outbound messages where the human stays the sender, bounded cross-room posts under the initiating human's membership, and classification of gateway actions as human-only or agent-callable with a parity test.
items.whyItMatters: A computer or browser without credentials cannot do real work, and with raw credentials it is a leak risk. Verevon has already decided the design (reuse Control grants and existing connector stores, broker server-side) but none of it is built, so agents cannot yet act on behalf of a person in mail, calendar or SaaS tools from a room.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm (broker, secret drop, cross-person asks, reach, route classification); grokbot (shared plugin with per-person OAuth, vault UX, draft cards)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Secrets custody 3 of 5 (common); connectors/plugins for room agents 3 of 5 (common); agent operates product via same API 3 of 5 (common); draft-first outbound 2 of 5 (differentiator); cross-room reach 1 of 5 (unique); credential asks 1 of 5 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: QM broker: the sandbox sends {credential slug, method, url}; the broker checks capability claims, host, method and decoded path prefix, uses redirect:manual, caps responses at 5 MB and writes an audit receipt; secret drop is a platform-styled one-time form with a random drop id, peek/redeem once and 7-day expiry; KeychainAsk/Grant {mode once|standing, audienceScopeId, expiry, revokedAt}. Grok Bot plugin {mcp_config, skills, variable_names, connector_type USER|TEAM} with per-person OAuth accounts and install modes OPTIONAL|DEFAULT|REQUIRED. Drafts: Draft {from,to,cc,subject,body} or {workspace,target,thread,body}, SendDraft/DiscardDraft, setting always|needs-approval|disabled. QM reach: resolveReachTarget(recipient|channel|participants) -> not_a_member|identity_unverified|ambiguous|group_too_large with at most 5 cross-conversation posts per turn. QM route table: agentApiMatches() gates paths per capability token and a parity test pins which routes an agent token can call.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md:1979-1986,2000-2006 (S3.4 credential grants and broker, S3.6 MCP/plugin/connector cockpit: planned, not built)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:4483-4573 (bindings carry only an allowed_tools filter)

apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/actions/dispatchers.rs:5427-5482 (typed spaces.* actions already shared by the UI and the AI/JSON path; some actions marked human-only, e.g. dispatchers.rs:632)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/mcp.rs:1-30 (MCP server registry with user/org scope and sharing; not linked to Spaces)
verevonToday.gap: No Space credential grants, no broker (sandbox is credential-free), no secret-drop form, no per-room connectors or per-person connector accounts for a room agent, no skill management at binding level, no draft object, no agent-initiated DM or cross-room post route, and no route-level human-only versus agent-callable classification or parity test beyond individual dispatchers.

items.approach: Control and integration-corev2 keep credentials (reuse existing OAuth/MCP/plugin/connector stores, no new keychain, per S3.4). Ingestion Plane: a broker that executes {credential slug, method, url} with host/method/path-prefix pinning, https only, redirect:manual, response cap and a usage receipt without secret material, reusing Quarry SSRF guards; the Model only proposes. Control: grant records once|session|standing bound to Space, actor/run, purpose and expiry, rechecked at use and at every scheduled fire; a one-time secret-drop form in the Frontend that never enters chat or logs. Connectors: bindings reference connectors and the Model Plane uses the invoking person's own account (a shared account would break the owner-plane ACL rule). Application Plane: a Draft object (agent setting always|needs-approval|disabled) sent by integration-corev2 on approval so the human remains the sender. Gateway: agent posts to another Space through a Control decision for the target Space with the initiating human as actor, typed refusals and a per-turn cap; classify gateway actions in domains/actions as human-only or agent-callable and add a parity test.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (broker, integration-corev2); Control Plane (grants); Application Plane (drafts); Frontend Plane (secret drop, route classification)
items.risks: The broker can become an SSRF vector; standing grants outliving membership (recheck at use); spam from cross-room posts (caps and audit); privilege escalation if route classification is wrong (pin it with a test).

alreadyPlanned.where: S3.4 Space credential grants and broker and S3.6 Space MCP/plugin/connector cockpit in docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md.

items.title: Agent runtime guardrails for shared rooms: member-text screening, shell command policy, room approvals, secret masking, DLP
items.summary: Extend the existing screening and policy code to what other people put into a room. (a) Add a trust class for non-owner room messages and attachments to execution-core provenance and show shadow-screening agreement stats to admins. (b) Parse shell commands into a syntax tree before capability policy, with an org floor (deny, approve) and typed reason codes. (c) Route elevated-risk browser actions into the room's approval card with decision ids. (d) Mask every injected credential value (raw, URL-encoded, base64 variants) in tool output before it reaches the model or the room. (e) Apply pii_filter and secret masking to agent-authored room messages before append, and optionally to human messages as DLP.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Tag every content chunk with provenance (owner, member, external, tool), screen external chunks with deterministic markers plus a classifier under a deadline, quarantine on enforce, and keep verdicts without payloads so a candidate rubric can be replayed. Value-based masking precomputes needles for every injected secret (raw, URI-encoded, base64, base64url, ignoring very short ones) and masks stdout, stderr and errors; pattern redaction covers bearer, JWT, sk-, AWS keys, PEM and DSN userinfo.

items.title: Files become agent input and room knowledge: per-turn re-authorized attachments as model input, extraction with summaries and typed refusals, and agent-proposed pinned knowledge
items.summary: When a room turn is built, resolve attachment references newest-first under caps, re-authorize each against the invoking member's current ACL, pass it natively to providers with file input or as extracted text with explicit truncation notices, label it untrusted, and store only references in the transcript. After an upload, extract, summarise and index it into the Space retrieval binding with typed refusals (too large, unsupported, policy); later let an agent propose a distilled summary or decision that a human approves before it is pinned, reusing the wiki propose-and-review flow.
items.whyItMatters: Uploading a file is useless to an agent room unless the agent can read it safely. QM's per-turn re-authorization and Slack's files-as-knowledge show how to do it without copying bytes into history.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm (per-turn authorization and provider route table); grokbot (pre-upload and pre-captioning); Slack (DOC) for auto-summary, retention and source-stays-in-provider; Grok Bot (SRC) for extract-only storage and typed refusals
others: Buzz (DOC, planned only): agent proposes durable knowledge, human approves and pins it
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-07] 2 of 5 sources (differentiator); pre-caption 1 of 5 (unique) [R-t1-08-07] files as knowledge: 2 of 5, differentiator; crystallization: 1 of 5, unique and unbuilt in Buzz
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-07] qm: at turn build, list attachments in scope newest-first (up to 10 documents, 8 MB), authorize each against current ACL, dedupe by sha256, extract in a worker with heap and time caps, choose native file input or a text fallback per provider from a route table, emit notices for skipped or truncated files, wrap content as untrusted data, and store only references in the tape. grokbot: a pre-upload manager keyed to the staged path and scoped to agent and session holds an upload and a background image caption, releases on send and deletes on discard. [R-t1-08-07] On upload completion enqueue extraction (text, tables) and an LLM summary; store extract and summary linked to the file id; index into the Space retrieval binding; return a refusal enum synchronously; a retention job deletes or tombstones per org setting. Crystallization: a proposal {summary, sources[]} awaits human approval and is written to the room canvas or knowledge store on approval.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-01-07] A room has no attachment path, so nothing reaches the model; the Chat documents and extract routes exist but are not reused in Space. [R-t1-08-07] Knowledge reaches room agents through the read-only Space retrieval binding and nobody can add knowledge from inside the room. There is no auto-summary, no typed upload refusal and no Space-level retention. The propose-then-approve mechanism exists in Data Plane (wiki_proposals with submit and review routes, scope wiki.approve) and in the Knowledge page Operating Map accept/reject UI, but nothing offers it in a room (INF: reuse, not verified end to end).

items.approach: [R-t1-01-07] Model Plane (session-core prompt builder): gather attachment refs from entries in scope, ask the Data Plane documents/retrieval API (no cross-plane DB reads) to authorize each ref for the invoking subject on every turn, then pick native file input or extracted text from a per-provider route table; Data Plane owns extraction with heap/time limits (the Chat extract route is the starting point); emit notices for skipped or truncated files; wrap as untrusted data; persist references only. Optional later: pre-caption staged files, with delete-on-discard and a ZDR consent rule. [R-t1-08-07] Data Plane: on room upload (F-t1-013 (R-t1-08-03)) run extraction and index into the Space retrieval binding; a Model Plane job writes the summary back as a Data Plane field computed only within viewer-authorized scope; add a typed refusal enum to the upload response. For crystallization, reuse wiki-store SubmitProposal and ReviewProposal: a room agent submits a proposal against the canvas page or a knowledge page, Application holds the approval item, a human with wiki.approve accepts, and the result becomes a new version with source_refs provenance. Frontend: summary card on the file and a proposal review surface patterned on the Operating Map review. Under ZDR keep only a session extract.
dependencies: Data Plane extraction API with size and time limits
Per-provider file-input route table in the Model Plane
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (prompt builder, provider routing) with Data Plane v2 (extraction, indexing, proposals)
items.risks: [R-t1-01-07] Prompt injection through document text (always label untrusted). Cost of native file inputs. Pre-captioning unsent files raises consent and ZDR questions and must delete on discard. Overlaps category 08 (uploaded files as shared agent knowledge, C-t1-08-012). [R-t1-08-07] Summaries can leak content to members without the document grant, so compute and show them only within viewer-authorized scope. Crystallization is DOC-only in the reference (planned, not built in Buzz).

items.title: Webhooks that wake room agents (Space-bound inbound endpoints)
items.summary: Let a Space manager create a secret webhook endpoint bound to a room and an agent. Ingestion Plane verifies the provider or HMAC signature, dedups the delivery, filters by JSON path and caps the payload; Model Plane capability-core then receives a wake envelope on the same trigger path schedules use, with the payload wrapped as untrusted data, and Control Plane decides every fire under the endpoint owner's authority.
items.whyItMatters: It turns room agents from chat-only into event-driven coworkers: a GitHub PR, a Stripe dispute or a monitoring alert starts work in the room. The agent-centric references that have it (qm, buzz) treat it as the way agents are triggered by the outside world, and it reuses the schedule fire path Verevon already governs. The same unattended-turn plumbing also unblocks per-agent email (F-t1-075 (R-t1-06-10)).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 sources; differentiator (webhook triggers also appear in Slack/Teams workflow builders)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: qm's WebhookReceiver.deliver(id, headers, rawBody) runs a per-provider verifier (github, slack, stripe, linear, generic HMAC) with constant-time compare, handles provider handshakes, derives a delivery id for dedup, filters events by JSON path (e.g. action in [opened]), caps the payload at 16,000 chars in a wake envelope, wraps it as untrusted content and dispatches it like a cron fire under the endpoint owner's authority. The secret is shown once; each endpoint has an event log. Buzz adds outbound calls with SSRF protection.

verevonToday.gap: The baseline recorded 'absent' after searching only the Spaces router and Convex schema; this pass found more (SRC). integration-corev2 already receives org-level provider webhooks at /api/v1/webhooks/:provider (signature check, normalise, tenant resolution, stored with a duplicate flag, published as verevon.ingestion.integration.webhook_received on NATS), and the only consumer found is conversation-core's inbox. Missing for Spaces: per-room secret endpoints (the route only accepts providers in the fixed catalogue), generic HMAC and GitHub/Stripe/Linear-style verifiers with path filters and a payload cap, a consumer that turns the event into a Control-decided capability-core fire bound to space_ref, and any UI. bridge-core's outbound webhook adapter (durable, retrying) is not wired to Spaces.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane integration-corev2: add a space-webhook route family (endpoint id in the path) backed by an endpoint record owned by Control (secret shown once, space_ref, agent binding, filter, size cap, owner), reuse the existing verify, normalise, dedup and store path, and publish a wake event carrying only a reference (as webhook_received does, with the stored payload fetched by id). Model Plane capability-core: consume the event as a trigger variant beside schedules, obtain a Control fire decision per delivery (owner authority, privacy/ZDR claims), then start an unattended turn through the Space scheduled-run machinery with the payload wrapped as untrusted content. Frontend: endpoint management and a delivery log in the Agent or Work tab; results post into the room. ZDR rooms keep payloads out of retention. Outbound calls (agent or workflow calling external URLs) can reuse bridge-core's webhook adapter once its SSRF/egress controls are confirmed (INF).
dependencies: Control endpoint record and per-delivery fire-decision contract
Unattended no-live-user turn for Space scheduled runs (capability-core PrepareScheduledRunThread)
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (receive and verify); Model Plane capability-core (trigger); Control Plane (endpoint record, fire decision)
items.risks: Prompt injection through payloads (bound and wrap as untrusted); webhook secret leakage; flood and cost control; ZDR rooms must not retain payloads; at-least-once delivery means replays need idempotent fire keys.

items.title: Meeting intelligence with consent: long-form transcription and an authority-scoped recap saved as a Space document, under a deny-by-default per-meeting AI policy
items.summary: Build the meeting-intelligence MVP from uploaded recordings first, then live calls: long-form speech-to-text with speaker labels and timestamps in the Model Plane, transcript segments stored as Data Plane knowledge units (not room posts), and a recap (decisions, action items with owners, chapters, citations to segments) written back as an editable Space document. Gate it with a Control-owned per-meeting policy {ai_access off|transcript_only|full, privacy_mode, ephemeral or retained answers, managers, locked fields} checked before any ASR, agent or recap reads audio or transcript, announced to all participants, default-off when externals are present.
items.whyItMatters: Transcript and AI recap are table stakes in Teams, Slack and buzz, and the meeting-intelligence design (a meeting as a source type on existing retrieval, wiki and ZDR rails) is architecturally sound but has no code. Teams' consent controls must ship with it, not after.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Teams (REA): recap with notes, tasks, topics, chapters, speaker timeline, citations back to the recording and visibility derived from transcript access; Teams (REA): visible AI on/off, privacy mode that blocks Copilot and all agents, ephemeral versus retained answers by org policy, only selected people can change AI settings, admin-locked options shown as locked
others: Slack (DOC): notes become a canvas in the huddle
Buzz (SRC): transcript segments are ordinary chat messages in the meeting channel
Slack (DOC): announce to all when AI notes start, default off with external guests
Grok Bot (SRC, medium): per-meeting or blanket consent card for the agent and an admin visibility setting (MANAGERS or EVERYONE)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-03-02] 3 of 5 (Buzz, Slack, Teams); table-stakes. Citations, attendance report and content-bin report are Teams-only. [R-t1-03-03] 2 of 5 (Teams, Slack) for AI policy, differentiator; Grok Bot adds consent for agent attendance; admin-locked indicator is Teams-only.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-03-02] Audio to streaming or batch ASR with diarisation produces segments {speaker, t_start, t_end, text}; on meeting end a reasoning pass produces the recap with citations to segments; the recap is saved as an editable document or canvas in the room; action items become tasks only after human approval; recap visibility equals transcript visibility (no transcript access, no AI summary); attendance comes from roster events. [R-t1-03-03] Policy evaluated server-side before any agent or ASR reads meeting content. Enabling AI emits a system message to participants and a badge. Externals present means default off. Ephemeral answers are stored with a meeting-scoped TTL. Fields locked by an admin render as locked with the owner of the lock.

Shared-Space deletion: owner or manager approval decisions, write fence at the Application Plane, receipts from all planes, legal hold outranks everything. items.title: Typed timeline entries: server-signed system messages, a card registry with a safe fallback, link previews through Quarry, and pointer embeds for artifacts
items.summary: Give Session Core entries a content_type plus payload, render by type through a card registry with a neutral unsupported-update fallback, and let the server emit typed system entries from Control and Application events (member added or removed, agent bound or paused, rename, history window). Add link previews fetched by Quarry with SSRF guards and stored as a snapshot so recipients never contact the third-party site, provider link cards classified in the browser, and an embed block that stores only {kind, id} for a canvas, list, record or file and renders it under the viewer's own grant with a request-access stub.
items.whyItMatters: Teams has 87+ typed system notices including agent added or removed, and buzz signs notices so clients cannot forge them; Verevon shows membership and binding changes only in a separate Activity tab. Pointer embeds keep artifacts under their own ACL instead of copying content into messages.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (typed previews with unknown and retired fallback cards); teams (87+ typed system notices incl. agent added or removed); buzz (relay-signed notices, sender-side link snapshots); Teams Loop (REA) for pointer embeds with their own ACL and a sharing warning; Grok Bot (SRC) for provider link-card classification
others: Slack typed cloud pickers as hardened child windows (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-10] Typed content 2 of 5 and system messages 2 of 5 (differentiators); link previews 3 of 5 (common) [R-t1-08-10] pointer embeds: 1 of 5, unique; provider cards and pickers: 2 of 5, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-10] Entry {content_type enum, payload oneof}; the preview projection is typed; the client renders a fallback card for unknown types and logs once per type. System entries {type, actor, subject, details} are emitted by the server from authority events and are never client-authored (buzz signs them with the relay key). Link preview: the sender side fetches under SSRF guards (private-IP block, redirect cap, 256 KB page and 2 MB image caps, per-host cooldown), extracts OG metadata, re-hosts a sanitized image and stores a signed snapshot with the message; recipients never contact the third-party site. Slack lets apps enrich unfurls. [R-t1-08-10] Message body contains an embed {artifact_kind, artifact_id}; the renderer fetches the artifact under the viewer's grant and subscribes to live updates; a viewer without access sees a request-access stub; pasting elsewhere reuses the same id; the share dialog warns when posting to an audience wider than the artifact ACL. Link cards use host-pattern to provider and path-pattern to kind tables and never fetch content.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-01-10] AppendMessageRequest carries role (user, assistant, system, tool), content and a metadata struct but no content_type; room posts render as markdown or plain text. Membership, grants and receipts appear in the separate Activity tab, not in the room timeline (checked in features/spaces: no member-added or agent-bound timeline rows). No link previews. Baseline had no record for typed content or system entries, so a final check of Session Core message conventions is still needed. [R-t1-08-10] Room posts cannot embed any artifact (chat artifacts are inline SSE payloads, not pointers to an independently authorized object). No link previews or provider cards in rooms; the baseline recorded attachments and link previews as absent in the room, and the integration-core provider actions are not offered as a picker (not re-verified).

items.approach: [R-t1-01-10] Model Plane proto: add content_type and a payload oneof (or a namespaced metadata.kind as an interim to avoid a breaking migration); existing rows default to text. Application Plane: project Control membership and binding events and Space lifecycle events into typed system entries appended under a server-only decision (clients cannot author them). Frontend: card registry (text, system notice, approval card, receipt, file, link preview, unknown fallback). Ingestion Plane: a Quarry fetch-preview endpoint (private-IP block, redirect cap, 256 KB and 2 MB caps, OG extract, re-hosted sanitized image) called by the gateway at send; snapshot stored on the entry; integration-corev2 providers can later supply richer unfurls. ZDR orgs may disable previews. Coordinate with category 12 (C-t1-12-012 typed transcript rows) and category 06 (C-t1-06-027 unfurling). [R-t1-08-10] Frontend Plane: an embed block type in room messages rendering canvas, list, record and file cards by id through the gateway under the viewer's decision; a pure client-side URL classifier for provider cards; pickers later through Ingestion integration-corev2 OAuth grants that never widen the owner ACL. Application Plane live updates reuse the existing realtime projection. Adopt the embed format inside the canvas and lists work, not as a separate product.
dependencies: Control and Application event feeds for membership and agent binding
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (entry schema) with Application Plane (system projection), Ingestion Plane (Quarry preview) and Frontend Plane (card registry)
items.risks: [R-t1-01-10] Schema migration of existing turns. Event-to-timeline consistency. SSRF and tracking-pixel leakage in previews; preview snapshots under ZDR; titles of private pages leaking through external unfurls. A decision card must not be confused with a Control approval of an effect. [R-t1-08-10] N+1 fetches on long timelines. A request-access stub must not leak titles or metadata to unauthorized viewers. Server-side unfurl would leak URLs, so keep classification client-side.

items.title: Guests and link invitations with mandatory expiry
items.summary: Introduce a guest principal type with memberships only in explicitly granted rooms, no directory or roster access and no agent invocation by default, invited through room-scoped invitations with a required expiry. Extend invitations with shareable links or codes (TTL, max uses, optional admin approval, stored terms acceptance) and a combined invite-to-org-and-room flow.
items.whyItMatters: Teams, Slack, QM and Buzz all support external collaborators; Verevon rosters only active org members, so a customer or contractor cannot be pulled into one room. Org invitations exist but cannot target a room or be shared as a link.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (guest tiers), buzz (invite codes), qm (mandatory guest expiry)
others: slack (single- vs multi-channel guests, admin approval queue)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: guests 4 of 5 (table-stakes); link invitations 2 of 5 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: principal.type in {internal, guest}. Guests get memberships only in granted rooms, cannot browse the directory, create rooms or see the roster, and by default cannot invoke agents; invitations require expires_at and expiry removes memberships through the normal membership-change path. Invite code = base64(org, room?, role, expires_at, max_uses, nonce) + HMAC; claim verifies HMAC and expiry, counts uses, records terms acceptance, then creates the membership through the normal Control path; claim is rate-limited (10 per minute in Buzz).

evidence: apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/spaceMembershipSync.ts:34-48 (rosters only from active org members)
apps/Control Plane/auth-core/src/auth/auth.ts:942-960 (org email invitations, 48 h, verified email, rate-limited accept)
apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/spaceMembers.ts:60-73 (a room grant requires existing org membership by design)
verevonToday.gap: Org email invitations exist, but there are no guests, no room-scoped invitations, no link or code invites with max uses, no approval queue, and no stored terms acceptance.

items.approach: Control Plane (auth-core, org-core, user-core): guest principal type, room-scoped guest invitation with mandatory expiry, and link invites with TTL, max uses and an optional room target and role; per-org approval policy. Agent turns in rooms with guests use the room audience in the Control decision so org-only knowledge is not retrieved. Guest seats flow to billing-core. Frontend: invite dialog on the room with a link option.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane
items.risks: Agent answers in a guest room can leak org knowledge; guest seat billing; ZDR and residency apply to guest data too; link invites leak easily, so keep a short TTL, max uses and admin revoke.

items.title: Teams and sub-groups with source-tracked membership; mentionable groups
items.summary: Add a team concept to Control (owners, members, visibility) where a team grant expands into room memberships tagged with their source, so removing someone from a team removes only team-derived grants. Later add team-level mentions (server-side expansion at send) once Space notifications exist.
items.whyItMatters: Teams are the core of the Teams half of the vision: orgs organise people into teams with their rooms. Today there is no team concept, only flat org membership and per-room lists. Teams are also the prerequisite for SCIM group sync, team-level agent context and group-based agent access.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams
others: qm (team contributes read-only resources to a turn only under a membership rule)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: teams 2 of 5 (teams, qm), mentionable groups 2 of 5 (teams, slack); common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: team(id, org_id, name, visibility), team_members(team_id, principal, role owner|member), team_rooms(team_id, room_id). Joining a team grants membership in its standard rooms; private rooms keep their own roster. Mentions: the server expands @tag into the member list at send and fans out through the notification service with per-recipient permission checks. QM teamsForTurn includes a team layer only if the actor is on the team AND the room is configured for it.

evidence: apps/Application Plane/conversation-core/conversation-core-go/internal/http/server.go:92 (ticket teams are support routing only)
apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/schema.ts:556-562 (comment anticipates team rooms as kind room, but no team table)
verevonToday.gap: No team or sub-group concept, no source tracking on memberships, no group mentions; Space events produce no notifications, so group mentions have nothing to ride on.

items.approach: Control Plane (org-core and user-core): teams as a membership source; a team grant expands into space_memberships rows tagged with source, and removal only clears that source. Application Plane: team directory projection and, later, tag definitions; notification-core allowlist extended for mention events. Team resources reach agents only through owner-plane grants, never widened by team membership. Agents in a mentionable group must be opt-in.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane
items.risks: Team-derived plus manual membership needs source tracking or removing someone from a team will wrongly remove a manual grant. Broadcast mentions to agents can trigger many paid model turns.

items.title: Personal sidebar organisation: stars, custom sections, per-group sort, hide, mute, drag-and-drop, computed system sections and cross-org badges
items.summary: Give each user a synced sidebar preference document (stars, custom sections, per-group sort, hidden refs, mute) edited with drag-and-drop and a batch mode, plus computed system sections over the same summaries (Agent runs, Waiting for approval, Unread, Muted) that can be toggled off, and a rate-limited stale-room suggestion. Add a per-org attention summary so the workspace switcher shows cross-org badges, with keyboard switching. Ship layout changes behind a flag with a switch-back.
items.whyItMatters: Sidebar organisation is table stakes in four references and becomes necessary as soon as directory, DMs and team rooms add more conversations per person; today the groups are fixed and unread is browser-local.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (sections), slack (workspace rail); Buzz (sort per group, synced sections and stars, dnd-kit sorting, More-unread pill); Teams for computed system sections and switch-back
others: Grok Bot (hide from sidebar, batch move/hide/delete for agents)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-02-12] sections 2 of 5 (teams, slack; common); account and workspace switching 4 of 5 (table-stakes, partly present) [R-t1-12-04] organisation 4 of 5 (Buzz, Grok Bot, QM, Slack; table-stakes); system sections and view modes 1 of 5 (Teams; unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-02-12] user_sidebar(user_id, org_id, sections[{id, name, emoji, sort, filter, items[]}], muted[], favorites[]) with keyboard-accessible drag between sections; stale suggestion = rooms with no visit in N days, excluding dont_suggest entries, rate-limited to once per day. Switcher: client keeps a list of {account, tenant, session}, one cheap unread badge per tenant from a per-tenant summary endpoint, Ctrl/Cmd+1..9 and next/previous, per-tenant sign-out clears only that tenant's local data. [R-t1-12-04] Per-user blob {stars:[ref], sections:[{id,name,refs[]}], sort:{group -> alpha|recent|priority}, hidden:[ref]} stored server-side and synced; groups render in fixed order, then user sections; sortable lists with a keyboard sensor; an IntersectionObserver on unread rows outside the viewport drives a "More unread" pill; selection mode with shift-range and bulk actions. Teams: system folders RECENT/MUTED/MEETING_CHATS as computed views toggled in settings, and a switch-back modal that preserves custom sections.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/core/components/sidebar/CoreSidebarSpacesPanel.tsx:104-232 (fixed groups plus a text filter)
apps/Control Plane/auth-core/src/auth/auth.ts:835-837 and :942-948 (multiSession up to 10, organizationLimit 5)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/core/components/sidebar/CoreSidebarSpacesPanel.tsx:104-232 and 281-321 (org room pinned first, thread pinned/unread/working dots, filter box)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/lib/space-unread.ts (unread mirrors Application Plane read markers, but only for the open room)
verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-02-12] No sections, favorites, ordering or mute; the switcher has no cross-org unread badges, keyboard switching or tenant marker. Unread is browser-local even within one org (UI baseline), so a badge has nothing server-side to read. [R-t1-12-04] No user stars, custom sections, sort modes, drag-and-drop, hide or bulk actions, no filters or system sections, and unread dots exist only for the room open in this browser.

items.approach: [R-t1-02-12] Application Plane: per-user sidebar preferences and visit timestamps, plus a server-side unread and attention projection per org and member. Frontend: sections with drag ordering and mute in CoreSidebarSpacesPanel; badges and Ctrl+1..9 in the WorkspaceSwitcher. Each org's badge must come from that org's own projection (no cross-plane joins). [R-t1-12-04] Application Plane owns a per-user preference document (refs only, no room names, so retention and ZDR are not touched) read and written through typed gateway actions. Frontend Plane renders groups and computed sections from the conversation summaries, with the drag-and-drop and selection mode. Priority sort waits on the salience model already used by the Activity grammar. Note: package.json has no drag-and-drop or virtualisation library and runs Solid 2.0 RC, so check compatibility of solid-dnd or build keyboard-first sorting on existing primitives.
dependencies: Room discovery (F-t1-048 (R-t1-02-02)) for more rooms per user
Run and approval state present in conversation summaries (for system sections)
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (preferences) with Frontend Plane (sidebar UI)
items.risks: [R-t1-02-12] Section names are user content; ZDR orgs may require that they are not logged. [R-t1-12-04] Low authority risk, since preferences are per user and touch no Space ACL. Solid 2 RC library compatibility. Too many default sections clutters the list.

items.title: Agent task tracker: Needs-input state, per-task threads and unread in the Work tab
items.summary: Give each agent task a visible state (working, needs input, done) with a note, a task-scoped thread beside the room and per-task unread, and project it into the Space Work tab and the activity inbox. Extend the capability-core task registry with a space_ref, a thread_ref and a needs_input state, keeping agent-owned tasks distinct from human-owned list items but linkable.
items.whyItMatters: A human should see exactly which agent task is waiting for them, which is the Grok Bot behaviour the vision asks for. Verevon already shows runs awaiting approval, but nothing says an agent is blocked on a question or lets a person answer in a task thread.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 5 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Task {id, title, state: working|needs_input|done, note, created_at, done_at, seen_done_at}; each task has a sub-thread id; a message sent with task_id routes to the agent about that task; a panel shows unread replies and done-but-unseen tasks, and the tasks panel is asynchronous.

verevonToday.gap: Per-thread orchestration todos exist, and /v1/tasks proxies the capability-core task registry (org-scoped, status filter, create, patch, cancel) with states created, assigned, blocked and completed and an assignee, but types.go has no space or thread field (the handler may store more). The Work tab lists runs and shows awaiting_approval as a critical needs-a-human state. There is no free-form Needs-input state, no per-task thread or unread, and no room-level task list.

items.approach: Model Plane capability-core owns task state: add space_ref, thread_ref and a needs_input substate to the task registry and pass space_ref through the /v1/tasks proxy as the cron list already does. Application Plane projects task state into the Space Work tab and the activity inbox. Frontend renders task threads beside the room and per-task unread, and reuses the Activity grammar so a waiting task reads the same in Work and Activity. Messages posted in a task thread route to the task session.
dependencies: Adoption plan S4.5 unified Work cockpit
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Overlap with Lists (F-t1-058 (R-t1-08-06)); keep agent-owned tasks separate from human-owned list items and link them by ref. The task registry semantics (types.go describes a seeded catalog) need confirming.

items.title: Artifact sharing: edit role, Space-as-subject grants, general access and access requests
items.summary: Extend the single resource_grants authority in Control Plane user-core with an edit role, a Space subject type (evaluated as the Space decision intersected with the resource grant), a general-access setting that defaults off per org, and an access-request flow with a human-only approve action. Extend ShareDialog to cover canvases, files and artifacts, not just documents. Phase 1 (edit role plus Space subject) must land together with the canvas and file library.
items.whyItMatters: Every artifact type in a room needs its own grants so sharing into a Space never widens the owner ACL, and the access-request loop routes the decision through a human owner. Without an edit role other members cannot co-author the canvas.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (SRC): Google-Docs-style dialog with request access and approve or decline from chat after an owner/manager check
others: Slack canvas sharing (DOC): view/edit grants independent of conversation membership, mentions notify only people with access
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 5 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grant rows {resource, subject (user|group|space), role (view|edit), granted_by}; a general_access enum on the resource; request_access creates a pending item delivered to the owner; the decide endpoint verifies the decider manages the resource's home scope, then grants (never downgrading an existing higher role) or sends a deduplicated decline notice; mentions inside an artifact notify only subjects with access.

verevonToday.gap: Shares are view-only and user-only: create_share hard-codes role view and subject_type user (shares.rs:114-115), the list and revoke routes are keyed to documents, and the only other surface is a shared-with-me list. There is no edit role, no group or Space subject, no general access, no access-request or approval flow, and no sharing for non-document artifacts.

items.approach: Control Plane user-core: add role edit, subject_type space (grant effective only when the current Space decision also allows, per the ADR intersection rule at SPACE_AUTHORITY_ADR_2026-08-13.md:64-70), a general_access field defaulting to restricted, and an access_requests table whose approve action is human-only and not model-eligible. Gateway shares.rs: generalize routes from documents/{id}/shares to resource_type and resource_id. Frontend: extend ShareDialog and deliver requests through the activity inbox (category 05). Keep resource_grants as the only grant store.
dependencies: Resource types for canvas and file artifacts (F-t1-015 (R-t1-08-01), F-t1-013 (R-t1-08-03))
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (user-core)
items.risks: A Space-subject grant must not become an ACL-widening path. Link access conflicts with ZDR and data residency, so keep it off by default per org. Hidden dependency: F-t1-015 (R-t1-08-01) and F-t1-013 (R-t1-08-03) cannot safely ship without phase 1.

items.title: Typed room records and Lists: one revisioned work-object substrate with a table view, assignees and item threads
items.summary: Build a generic Space record primitive (stable id, namespaced type, body, prev-revision CAS, idempotent resubmit) in the Application Plane, then ship Lists on top of it: typed columns, a table view first (board later), assignees, saved views and an item thread. Agents create and update records through a Model Plane tool that proposes, with authority-bearing fields staying human-only.
items.whyItMatters: Slack and Teams both give rooms lists, and a list is the natural place to assign work to humans and agents and see status, which is the core of humans and agents cooperating on work. One substrate avoids building tasks, decisions and checklists separately and keeps edits out of chat unread counts.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack Lists (DOC) for the user model; Buzz NIP-AR (SRC) for the record substrate
others: Teams Lists, Planner and Wiki tabs (REA)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: lists: 3 of 5, common; typed-record substrate: 1 of 5, unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Record = full snapshot {id (stable UUID), home_space, type (namespaced), title, body JSON, op (create|update|move|delete|restore), prev revision, optional root thread}; tables heads(id to head) and revisions; head advance is an atomic CAS on prev; resubmitting an accepted revision is idempotent; revisions never count toward unread or notifications; read access equals the room decision. A list is a record collection with a column schema {name, type: text|select|people|date|checkbox}; views store filter, sort, group and an optional default flag; assignment emits an activity item to the assignee; add message to list copies a message ref into an item.

verevonToday.gap: No Space-scoped record type, list or board. Planner documents in Convex are keyed by a legacy workspaceId (an ADR resource-local partition) and orchestration todos are per thread. Tickets are a separate route unlinked from Spaces. Humans cannot edit tasks in the room and there are no assignees, views or item threads.

items.approach: Application Plane (Convex) owns space_records and space_record_revisions keyed by spaceRef with a registered schema per record type and prev-CAS; Control read and write decisions gate every query and mutation. Do not create another generic project authority (ADR row 84 treats the Convex projects table as a migration candidate), so records hang off the Space aggregate. Frontend: Lists tab in SpaceCockpit, table view first, board later. Model Plane: list read and update tools calling the Application API under the run's delegated decision. Assignment events feed the planned activity inbox; allow linking a ticket ref into a list item.
items.planeOwner: Application Plane
items.risks: Scope creep toward a full Planner; ship one table view and a few field types first. Generic schemas drift, so keep a registry of record types shared by UI and agent tools.

items.title: Do not disturb, quiet-hours schedules and urgent break-through, visible to agents
items.summary: Add a per-user attention state {dnd_until, schedules [{days, start, end, tz}], vip subjects} to notification-core and gate the router on it: while in DND, non-critical signals from non-VIP actors are stored for the inbox only and do not go to push or the OS, then flush when DND ends. Agents classify approval requests by urgency in capability-core, with a per-agent daily cap and an owner-configurable limit on critical break-through. Expose a coarse 'can I interrupt now' answer to agents, not the schedule itself.
items.whyItMatters: Agents work around the clock. Without DND they will page humans at night, and push (F-t1-035 (R-t1-05-05)) should not ship before this gate. It also helps the agents: one that can check whether a human is interruptible can defer a non-urgent ask instead of blocking a run.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack (manual pause, schedule, admin default hours, VIP and urgent break-through); Teams for urgent messages and meeting auto-DND
others: Teams (priority contacts, urgent messages, auto-DND in meetings)
Buzz (explicitly has none; spec defers DND)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Slack combines a manual pause, a recurring schedule, admin default hours, a VIP override and a once-a-day 'notify anyway' urgent break-through (DOC). Teams adds urgent messages and priority contacts that pass DND and automatic DND in meetings (REA). Router rule: if the user is in DND, the signal is not critical and the actor is not VIP, store it in the inbox only and do not deliver to OS or push; queued items flush when DND ends; urgent break-through is rate-limited per sender.

verevonToday.gap: No DND, quiet hours or schedule exists in Spaces or notification-core (channels.go holds only org-level event-by-channel configuration). Quiet hours are named as part of S4.4, whose current source state is the delivery attempt state machine and a disabled-by-default worker.

items.approach: Application Plane (notification-core): attention-state table and a router gate placed after the F-t1-008 (R-t1-05-04) preference checks. Model Plane (capability-core): add an urgency class to approval and agent-awaiting signals, plus a per-agent daily critical cap. Frontend Plane: DND toggle, schedule editor and VIP list in Settings. Expose DND to agents only through a narrow 'interruptible now' read so the schedule itself is not disclosed to every room member's agents.
items.planeOwner: Application Plane
items.risks: Urgent-flag abuse by agents (cap per agent per day, owner-configurable); disclosing a user's schedule to agents or room members; queued items must flush once and in order.

alreadyPlanned.where: S4.4 quiet hours: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md (execution tracker, line 226) and the baseline note 'Quiet hours are planned in S4.4'

items.title: Finish the S4.4 delivery ledger and add a content-free missed-activity digest
items.summary: Generalise notification-core's lease-based delivery-attempt ledger into the S4.4 Space delivery ledger: idempotency keys, max-age expiry, bounded retries, and delivery errors reported back to the agent run that produced the message. Then add an email channel and a per-user digest (hourly or daily) that auto-pauses after inactivity and, for ZDR orgs, carries counts and links only.
items.whyItMatters: The ledger is the foundation for push, email digests, scheduled agent output and the future Channel Plane without losing or duplicating messages. The digest pulls absent humans back when agents are blocked on them, cutting approval latency.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (delivery outbox and morning digest)
others: Buzz (content-free mention outbox bridged by an operator)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Outbox: 2 of 5 sources, differentiator; digest: 2 of 5, common

items.title: 'Catch me up' recap of what I missed, scoped to my own read access
items.summary: Add a 'Catch me up' entry point on the room header and the inbox. It runs a Model Plane recap turn over the unread messages and runs since the user's last read marker, prioritising items that mention the user or need action, with scopes unread, last 7 days or a custom range, and offers mark-as-read on completion. The scope is computed from the viewer's own access, ZDR is propagated, and the result is ephemeral for ZDR orgs.
items.whyItMatters: The highest-value AI feature for a returning user in an agent-heavy room: what did the agents do while I was away, and what needs me. Verevon owns its Model Plane and already puts agents in rooms, so this is an agent turn rather than a new subsystem, and it is the sort of attention feature Slack and Teams only bolt on.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Teams (cross-thread prioritised recap)
others: Slack (unread-only, last 7 days or custom range, plus a recurring-summary workflow step)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Teams does a holistic, cross-thread recap prioritised by relevance, with read-aloud, and marks chats read when the recap is dismissed (REA). Slack offers unread-only, last-7-days and custom-range scopes and a workflow step for recurring summaries (DOC). Collect unread content since last_read for the requested scope (only content the viewer can access), summarise with a model, prioritise mentions and action items, offer mark-as-read.

verevonToday.gap: Only a 'Meeting Scribe' agent template that summarises the text conversation when it is mentioned. There is no 'catch me up' entry point, no unread-scoped or cross-room recap and no link to read markers.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: 'Catch me up' action in the room header and the inbox, registered in the action registry. Model Plane: a recap run invoked with the viewer's own read scope (never a wider room scope), zdr=true propagated, token and cost limits through the existing cost plane. Use the unread map and read markers from F-t1-009 (R-t1-05-02) to pick the window; optionally mark-as-read on completion. Output is not persisted for ZDR orgs.
dependencies: F-t1-009 (R-t1-05-02) read markers and unread map
Model Plane run with viewer-scoped access
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (recap run); Frontend Plane (entry point)
items.risks: Summaries quoting content the viewer cannot see if the scope is computed from the room rather than the viewer; cost on large rooms; stale recap if new messages arrive mid-run.

items.title: Governed Space skills and plugin bundles (ecosystem-compatible manifests)
items.summary: Give skills a Space scope and a review lifecycle (draft, reviewed, published, archived, with review invalidated by any edit and signed manifests), and let the org plugin registry accept Claude-style and Cursor-style marketplace manifests with git-sha pinning and a variables schema, fanning components out to the skill store, MCP registry and hook runner. A Space manager can then enable an org-activated plugin or publish a room skill, never beyond what the org allows.
items.whyItMatters: A team can curate room-specific know-how ('how we run incident review') safely, which is how agents get better in a shared room, and reading existing plugin ecosystems gives Verevon agents many capabilities for little effort. It extends two existing assets (the / skill picker and the admin-activated plugin packs).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Governed skills: 2 of 5 (differentiator); plugin bundles: 2 of 5 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: qm's SkillStore runs draft->reviewed->published->archived with HMAC-signed manifests verified on resolve, visibleFor(principal, scope) filtering, supporting files materialised only for speakers who can see the skill, and git skill packs pinned to a ref with visible ineligibility reasons. Grok Bot reads both .cursor-plugin and .claude-plugin marketplace.json, pins git sources to a 40-hex sha, declares a variables JSON-schema (writeOnly marks secrets) and registers each component (commands, agents, skills, rules, hooks, mcpServers) with its subsystem; buzz persona packs are a simpler variant.

Governed Space skills are plan item S3.5.

items.title: Duplex voice for agents: a voice front that delegates to the Space agent, then agents as attributed participants in room calls
items.summary: Phase A (M, no SFU needed): inside a Space, a user holds a realtime voice conversation with an agent. A fast voice persona talks and its only tools delegate: send_task hands real work to the existing agent run in the Space (still behind approval gates) and a history search covers Space threads and past voice sessions; each agent gets voice, speed and language settings. Phase B (L, after F-t1-029 (R-t1-03-01)): a server-side participant per invited agent hears the call through STT, answers with an attributed audio track, and stops when a human starts talking.
items.whyItMatters: This is the defining hybrid moment of the Space vision: humans and agents in the same voice room, and a personal agent that can be tasked hands-free. The front and worker split avoids a second agent brain, and doing it server-side is better than Buzz, whose agent voice runs on the owner desktop.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (SRC) for the voice-front and worker split; Buzz (SRC) for agents as audio participants with floor control
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 5 each (Grok Bot, Buzz); unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grok Bot: realtime session (session.update, input_audio_buffer.append, response.create/cancel) with voice tools send_task(constraints), recall_text_messages and search_conversations{query, scope this-chat|earlier|everything, from, to, if_missing}; worker results come back as async updates the persona announces; one active voice chat per user and ending needs confirmation; the refusal text for send_task tells the model not to drop prohibitions or approval requirements; per-agent voice_id, voice_speed, voice_language. Buzz: agent audio publisher authenticates as the agent and shows in the roster; VAD with about 300 ms silence flush; any human speech cancels agent TTS (barge-in); agent speaks only when addressed.

items.approach: Model Plane: a realtime voice session type whose only tools are send_task (calls the existing agent run API in the Space so approval gates and Control decisions still apply) and search_conversations (Space threads read under the read decision); add voice_id, voice_speed and voice_language to the agent profile in the registry behind SpaceCreateAgentDialog. Frontend: upgrade VoiceModeDialog into a duplex call island that can mount in SpaceRoomComposer and reuse the call store from F-t1-029 (R-t1-03-01). Phase B: a Model Plane SFU participant per invited agent subscribing to room audio, streaming to /v1/ai/realtime, publishing an agent track under the agent identity, label shown in the roster; floor policy cancels agent playback on any human speech (response.cancel) and the agent speaks only when explicitly invited to the call or addressed, consistent with the explicit-invocation rule. Enforce F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-03) before the agent hears the room.
dependencies: Agent run API and approval gates
Agents in personal Spaces (agents-in-the-room category) for personal-agent voice
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: ZDR attestation for realtime providers (the route already fails closed). Cost per minute. Agents talking over humans; always label agent voices. Delegated actions must still hit in-room approval gates and must carry the constraints of the spoken request.

items.title: Screen sharing in calls with a sharing indicator, sensitive-surface redaction, and the same cue for agents acting in a room
items.summary: Publish a getDisplayMedia track to the call as a second SFU track, show a persistent "you are sharing" bar with Stop, and switch the app into a redacted mode while sharing so approval cards, secrets and token-like fields are masked (a web page cannot exclude its own windows from capture). Reuse the border and indicator design for the agent run live view and the Quarry browser view so humans see when an agent is acting.
items.whyItMatters: Screen share is the main reason people start work calls, and it is cheap once an SFU exists. The agent-acting cue gives one consistent trust signal for the Model proposes, Quarry executes browser model, where the baseline shows agent work is opaque inside the room.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack (SRC): a native border overlay follows the shared window and the picker excludes the app own sensitive windows
others: Teams (SRC): deeper capture pipeline, annotation and single-controller remote control
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 (Slack, Teams); common.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Picker with thumbnails clamped to 480 px that filters excluded windows; an overlay with border width and colour that tracks the window bounds; share published as its own track. Web equivalent: navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia, an in-app sharing bar, and a redact-sensitive-surfaces mode.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/DashboardComposer.tsx:1915-1950 (SRC: addScreenshotFile uses getDisplayMedia for a single frame, not a stream)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/remote_support.rs:1-12 (SRC: RustDesk config only; sessions run browser to hbbs/hbbr and bypass the gateway, no durable record)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:497,559-560 (SRC: browser control mode with human_takeover)
verevonToday.gap: No human screen share in Spaces. Adjacent pieces only: a one-frame screenshot capture in the dashboard composer, RustDesk remote-support config that is not a Space feature and leaves no audit record, and agent live-view and human-takeover controls that are not reachable from a Space.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: after F-t1-029 (R-t1-03-01), add getDisplayMedia publishing to the call store with a sharing state; a sharing banner; a global redact mode that masks SpaceApprovalPanel content, secrets and credential-like inputs while sharing; extract the border and indicator component and mount it on the agent run live view and, once Space-scoped browser runs exist, on the Quarry browser view in the room. No annotation or remote control in the first cut. Keep RustDesk remote support separate and add a durable session record there later if it is ever surfaced in Spaces.
dependencies: Space-scoped agent browser view (agents-in-the-room category) for the agent cue
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Leaking approval cards or secrets during a share, since the web cannot exclude its own windows. Browser support for display capture constraints varies.

items.title: Search operators with Verevon-native filters, typed result tabs and recent-search history
items.summary: Port buzz's operator parser (from:, in:, with:, is:, has:, before:/after:/on:, quoted phrases, exclusion, trailing *) as a pure TS module, add Verevon-specific operators (agent:, has:approval, has:run, has:artifact, is:thread), and render results in tabs (threads, agents, runs, approvals, artifacts, documents) with counts. The gateway fans out to owner-plane APIs in parallel and returns {hits, counts, failed[], limited[]}; recent searches stay in browser storage per viewer.
items.whyItMatters: Power users and agents (which can emit structured filters directly) get precise recall, and one search covers Verevon objects that Slack and Teams do not have. Agent- and run-aware operators would be a differentiator no reference has. The failed[]/limited[] contract keeps an empty result distinguishable from a gap.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: slack (grammar, DOC) with buzz parser (SRC) and teams result domains (REA)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: operators 3 of 5 (table-stakes); result domains 3 of 5 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: buzz parseSearchOperators splits on whitespace, recognises an operator only at token start, leaves malformed values (e.g. invalid dates) in the free text, resolves names to ids at the call site and converts dates to since/until with an exclusive "before"; filters {authors[], spaces[], since, until, is[], has[]} go to the server as SQL predicates before ranking. Teams fans one query out to per-domain resolvers (messages, files by type, meetings, people, channels, settings), returns hit types and per-domain counts, and renders tabs with type-specific facets and date presets. qm SearchBackend registry returns failed[] and limited[] arrays.

verevonToday.gap: No message search, so no operators, tabs, filters or history. The Knowledge tab lists documents and wiki read-only without search or filters, though it already reports per-section gaps. Verevon-native objects (threads, agents, runs, approvals, artifacts) are not searchable.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: pure TS parser module plus Solid search view with tabs; name resolution against the Space roster and org members. Share the filter struct with the agent history tool (F-t1-038 (R-t1-04-03)) so humans and agents use one grammar. Gateway BFF composes per-domain calls to owner planes (Session Core messages, Data Plane documents, Application Plane activity/run projections) in parallel with a per-backend timeout, each with its own Control decision, no cross-plane DB join. Keep search history in browser storage first, since server-side query history may be forbidden under ZDR.
dependencies: Owner-plane search endpoints for runs, approvals and artifacts (not confirmed to exist)
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (parser, UI, gateway fan-out); owner planes expose per-domain search
items.risks: Name resolution must not reveal people the viewer cannot see; date timezone ambiguity; gateway fan-out must not drift into a cross-plane DB join; slowest backend sets latency; scores from different backends are not comparable.

items.title: Room header and pulse rail extras: live counts, pinned posts first, user-pinned resource tabs and a budget meter; PWA share target and MCP apps later
items.summary: Keep the six cockpit tabs as default, add header counts (open approvals, running work, documents) from existing projections, show pinned posts first, and allow user-pinnable extra tabs (link, document, later canvas) stored as Space metadata with view-only grants controlling access. Add a usage meter once per-Space cost attribution and non-zero token counts exist. Later add a PWA share target so a file or text can be sent to a room agent from anywhere, and render MCP UI resources in a sandboxed iframe whose tool calls go through the Model Gateway authority path.
items.whyItMatters: QM's scope page and Slack's tabs make a room's resources one click away; useful polish once canvas, cost and PWA exist.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (scope-centred page and top-bar tool buttons with 60 s cached counts); Slack for user-added tabs and bookmarks; Grok Bot for the usage meter; teams
others: Slack (Pins tab auto-created on first pin, bookmark folders)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-12-09] header shelf 2 of 5 (Slack, QM; differentiator); usage meter 1 of 5 (Grok Bot; unique) [R-t1-06-12] Each capability appears in 1 of 5 sources (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-12-09] Scope model {personal|project|channel|group} drives contextMeta(scope) panels with manage actions; the top bar shows breadcrumb plus tool buttons whose counts are cached per scope for 60 s, and opening a tool keeps the session scope. Slack lists tabs per conversation with "show by default". Grok Bot: usage policy {thresholds:[75,90]} feeding a meter component and a limit-hit state with upgrade or credit options. [R-t1-06-12] Teams stores a tab as (app id, content URL, entity id, scope) on the conversation and renders it in an iframe with per-viewer access checks; its package registers protocols and a share target, and share-from-web carries a compose note and verifies the active account. Grok Bot renders MCP app resources in a sandboxed frame whose tool calls pass a host bridge and the normal permission checks (feature-gated).

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceCockpit.tsx:61-110 and components/SpacePage.tsx:408-486 (six fixed tabs, no counts)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:4890-4925 (space_actions echoes the org catalog only)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:541-567 and lib/activity-grammar.ts:694-730 (budget_exceeded rendered as a refusal linking to the spend ceiling)
verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-12-09] No user-added tabs or bookmarks, no counts in the header, pins not shown first, no room-level view of skills, connectors or memory (S3.x), and no proactive meter or per-room spend (token counts are 0 from Session Core, so a meter would mislead). [R-t1-06-12] The cockpit has six fixed tabs (Chat, Work, Knowledge, Activity, Agent, Members) and no pinned or custom tabs. There is no share target or protocol handler and no native shell. No MCP UI resource handling was found in model-gateway (a grep for ui:// and MCP app terms returned nothing this pass), but the MCP app renderer status in the Frontend was not checked.

items.approach: [R-t1-12-09] Frontend Plane: header counts from existing Work, Activity and Knowledge projections, with unknown rendered as unknown; a user-pinnable tab type stored as Space metadata in Application Plane (link and document first, canvas after category 08); pinned posts first. The meter is last: Model Plane cost service publishes per-org and per-Space usage summaries and Session Core must return real token counts before the pulse rail shows a meter. [R-t1-06-12] Frontend Plane: allow pinning Knowledge documents and vetted internal links as extra cockpit tabs, restricting embeds to internal resources first (clickjacking). Add a PWA share target and deep links building on the existing in-app deep links (baseline v-space-ui-043). MCP apps after F-t1-026 (R-t1-06-04): sandboxed iframe with a postMessage bridge that forwards tool calls only through the Model Gateway authority path.
dependencies: Per-Space cost attribution in Model Plane and non-zero token counts from Session Core (meter only)
F-t1-037 (R-t1-06-02) Space tool cockpit (for MCP apps)
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (meter data from Model Plane)
items.risks: [R-t1-12-09] Tab sprawl; counts and meter must show unknown, never zero, when a projection is unavailable; the meter must not expose another member's spend. [R-t1-06-12] Arbitrary-site embedding (clickjacking); sandbox escape and data exfiltration from MCP app frames; share-target account mismatch.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t1-12-09] apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/SPACE_PAGE_AUDIT_2026-09-06.md section 17 (The later tier, about lines 1595-1625) records per-room spend as blocked, and S3.x covers room skills/connectors/memory panels (about lines 253-257).

items.title: Shareable, versioned agent templates with an export policy, and an internal catalogue of org agents and skills
items.summary: Replace the three hard-coded agent templates with user-published templates (immutable versions, active-version pointer, org or team visibility, share link, an export policy that never copies credentials, memory or grants; import re-runs roster confirmation), and build an internal 'agents in this org' catalogue as a read model over the agent registry with admin approval before listing. Defer public third-party marketplace listings.
items.whyItMatters: Grok Bot shows templates and a catalogue make good agents spread inside an org; it matters after personal agents exist.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-06-09] 2 of 5 sources; differentiator [R-t1-04-11] 1 of 5 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-06-09] Grok Bot templates have CRUD with visibility (PUBLIC|TEAM), an active version, an export policy, chat-link import and creator attribution; a template record {share_id, active_version, visibility, owner_type, blob_object_key} points at immutable version blobs, and the export policy strips secrets, memory and connections. Buzz persona packs and snapshots are a file-based variant. [R-t1-04-11] Listing objects with a status workflow (PENDING_REVIEW, LISTED, DELISTED) and a review queue, plugin lifecycle states, a browse API with category, featured and sort, per-team popularity counts, and install creating an org-scoped installation subject to admin policy. Slack and Teams app directories are INF only (not evidenced in this category).

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-06-09] Agent creation offers three hard-coded templates; there are no user-published templates, versions, share links or export policy. Personal per-user agents are absent (baseline v-space-backend-070: Control refuses personal membership replacement), so the 'copy a colleague's personal agent' flow needs that first. Whether Application Plane agent definitions are versioned was not verified. [R-t1-04-11] No marketplace or app directory for Spaces. The org-wide agent registry answers presence, not discovery of new agents, and MCP/plugins are configured org-wide in Settings only.

items.approach: [R-t1-06-09] Application Plane: agent definitions gain immutable versions and a template record (visibility, active version, share id). Control Plane governs visibility (org or team) and the export policy, which never copies credentials, memory, grants or connector references. Import re-runs roster confirmation and binding policy. Frontend: publish and import actions in the Create Agent dialog and the Agent tab. [R-t1-04-11] Start internal: a read model over existing agent definitions and skills with listing status and admin approval (Control Plane owns policy, Application Plane projects the list), browse route in the gateway, directory tab in the Frontend. Defer third-party listings until plugin/MCP governance exists.
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (definitions, versions, catalogue read model) with Control Plane (visibility, export policy)
items.risks: [R-t1-06-09] Leaking instructions or connector references through a template; imported templates carrying prompt-injection payloads; import must not inherit the author's grants.
