[R-t1-04-11] Third-party plugins bypassing ZDR or the rule that the Model proposes and Quarry executes browser actions.

items.title: Scoped agent context and promotion path: team layer, setup manifests, publish to team, service accounts
items.summary: Extend ResolvedSpaceContext with a team layer (included only when the actor is on the team and the room is configured for it), add explicit scope-to-scope grants that stay with the resource-owning plane, and add scoped setup manifests (org, team, user) for agent computers. Once personal agents exist, add a publish-to-team flow with a step-by-step carry-over proposal (never secrets) and agent-owned service credentials scoped per binding.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon already has the stricter half (decisions bound to audience and owner-plane ACL, authored instruction hierarchy). The missing half is how agents and their computers are configured at team level and promoted from a person's own agent to a team's, which GrokBot's vision of personal agents needs.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm (scope layering), grokbot (publish, manifests, service accounts)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: each 1 of 5 (qm or grokbot only); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: QM resolve(actor, scope, audience) mounts org (read-only), each applicable team (read-only) and the active scope (read-write) and composes instructions, policies and granted handles; handlesForAudience returns only what every participant is entitled to. GrokBot: PublishToTeam builds a carry-over proposal (skills, plugins, memories, automations) the owner confirms item by item and never copies personal chats; setup_manifest(scope_kind USER|TEAM|ORGANIZATION) merged org, then team, then user at sandbox creation; team agents act through service-account credentials.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:3720-3888 and :4231-4398 (authored instruction hierarchy: platform, org, Space, user persona, agent persona)
apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/spaces/repository.go:670-673 (personal Space membership immutable, so no personal agents)
no setup-manifest code found by name search in the Model Plane (comparator check)
verevonToday.gap: No team layer, no cross-scope grants, no setup manifests (status unknown), no publish flow because personal agents cannot exist yet, and provider-level agent service accounts are unverified.

items.approach: Phase A (after teams): add a team layer to ResolvedSpaceContext; resource grants live with the owner plane (Data Plane for files, Model Plane for skills) and are referenced by Control, never in a central table. Phase B (Model Plane sandboxes): setup manifests per org, then team and user, restricted to an allowlisted package registry. Phase C (after personal agents and agent access list): publish-to-team in the Model Plane with a Control publish decision; service credentials in integration-corev2 scoped per room binding, with the team copy re-requesting owner-plane grants.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (agent definitions, sandboxes) with Control Plane decisions
items.risks: A central grants table would be cross-plane DB access. Carrying credentials would break agents not sharing credentials; memory carry-over can leak personal data. Packages in manifests are a supply-chain risk. Single-source, partly medium-confidence evidence.

items.title: Tauri desktop shell around the gateway origin: narrow bridge, system-browser sign-in, protocol links, signed updater
items.summary: After the PWA, build a Tauri 2 shell that loads the existing gateway origin with a locked CSP and no local tokens, exposes a versioned, schema-validated bridge of at most about 15 capability commands (notify, badge, open-external, deep-link, window state, updater status), and signs users in through the system browser with a single-use PKCE handoff that mints the same HttpOnly BFF session in an isolated webview profile. Register a native verevon:// protocol with single-instance forwarding and a cold-start queue feeding the F-t1-039 (R-t1-11-03) router, and ship signed MSIX/MSI/DMG installers with a gateway-served updater manifest that installs only when no agent run is streaming and no draft is unsent.
items.whyItMatters: All five references ship a native shell, and it is the only route to tray presence, OS protocol links from mail and Office, and global hotkeys. Verevon can capture most value with the PWA first, but enterprise rollout (IT-managed installers, "chat with" links) eventually needs this.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (thin native shell around a web UI with a versioned RPC over capability modules); buzz (Tauri 2, Rust-owned state) is the closest stack fit
others: slack (one URL grammar on every OS, should-i-update server decision, Joi-validated bridge channels)
qm (PKCE desktop handoff, locked-down minimal Electron shell)
grokbot (never install while an agent is working)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Shell 5 of 5, protocol handler 5 of 5, bridge 4 of 5, updater 4 of 5, signed packaging 4 of 5 = table-stakes; system-browser sign-in 3 of 5 = common.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Shell loads the remote web app in a system WebView; renderer sandboxed with a narrow typed bridge (single envelope, per-capability schemas, sender-origin check, validation-failure telemetry); native side owns badge, notifications, deep links, updates. Tauri 2 plugins: single-instance, deep-link, window-state, updater, notification. PKCE: app creates verifier and state, opens /auth/desktop?challenge, the portal returns a sealed two-minute code through the protocol link, the app redeems it with the verifier for a session cookie. Updater: idle, checking, staging, ready; apply on idle; block while runs or uploads are active; candidate-commit CI with signed canary then promote.

verevonToday.gap: Web SPA only: no Electron, Tauri or MSIX package, no tray, native notifications, protocol handler, bridge, updater or desktop sign-in (SRC plus a dated internal audit, DOC, which calls Windows presence greenfield). Only HTTPS routes exist; the BFF cookie session is the right target for the handoff.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: new desktop workspace in verevonv3 (Tauri 2, Rust to match the gateway stack) with a capability ACL file and a shared TS/Rust bridge schema in packages/; native protocol and single-instance handling that parse into the same route table as F-t1-039 (R-t1-11-03) with an allowlist of commands. Control Plane identity plus the gateway: /auth/desktop PKCE endpoint minting a sealed single-use short-TTL code bound to challenge, state and audience. Gateway: updater manifest per org and channel (stable/beta) with rollback and update-required hints from F-t1-024 (R-t1-11-04). CI: Tauri bundler for MSIX/MSI and DMG using a candidate-commit release pattern and held signing certificates. No local agent runtime and no offline message store: agent execution stays server-side under "Model proposes, Quarry executes", which keeps audit and ZDR intact.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (sign-in handoff: Control Plane)
items.risks: Code-signing and notarisation custody and cost; a second client to test; bridge sprawl enlarges the attack surface (Slack has 122 channels, Teams about 545 methods), so keep it minimal; link parsing is an injection surface; a broken update channel strands users, so rollback is mandatory; no local caching of Space content that would break ZDR.

items.title: Provenance footer on relayed and automated messages and notifications; optional system voice
items.summary: Carry {sender_agent, on_behalf_of, trigger: reply, cron or relay, schedule_ref} on posts and notification payloads, and render a footer such as 'sent for @person' or the schedule name with a link back to the schedule settings. As an optional second phase, give platform notices (policy changes, new Space features) one system sender identity with a per-user cap and opt-out.
items.whyItMatters: It prevents confusion about who an automated message speaks for and fits Verevon's authority model, where owner effect receipts and authorising grants are already recorded. In a room full of agents and scheduled runs, a user needs to know whether a ping came from a person, an agent acting for a person, or a cron.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (provenance); Grok Bot for system-voice announcements
others: Slack (Slackbot as single voice for notices and reminders)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Provenance: 1 of 5 sources, unique; system voice: 2 of 5, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: QM sets a relaySender field when attributeAs differs from the sender, renders a footer, and records the trigger in delivery provenance. Grok Bot delivers changelog items through the bot with relevance guidance, delivery windows, eligibility gates, a minimum client version and a maximum number of offers; the agent decides whether to mention them in a relevant conversation.

verevonToday.gap: The room Activity feed already shows owner effect receipts and the grants that authorised them, but a grep of src/features/spaces and spaces.rs found no on-behalf-of, relay-sender or trigger fields on posts or notifications (INF). Whether schedule-run posts in conversation-core carry an attribution field was not checked, and no system sender identity for platform notices was found.

items.approach: Application Plane: add on_behalf_of and trigger to the post model and to the F-t1-008 (R-t1-05-01) notification payload; reuse the grants and receipts already in Activity as the source. Frontend Plane: render the provenance footer on timeline posts, inbox items and toasts. Phase 2 (Model Plane plus Control): an announcement store the user's agent can consult, gated by Control eligibility and capped per user, only after the footer ships.
dependencies: Schedule-run post attribution check in conversation-core
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (provenance); Model Plane and Control (system voice, phase 2)
items.risks: System-voice announcements can feel like ads inside an agent, so cap and allow opt-out; attribution fields must come from the server, never from the browser.

items.title: Agent external channels: per-agent email first, then Slack and Teams apps
items.summary: Phase 1: finish the mail-task pipeline into a per-agent address. Inbound mail is verified and deduped in Ingestion Plane, then wakes the agent as an untrusted unattended turn; outbound send is an approval-gated integration action. Phase 2 (after the durable delivery ledger and a real Channel Plane): publish an agent into Slack or Teams as its own app with an install-state machine, external messages entering under the installing user's authority.
items.whyItMatters: Gives personal agents a human-like identity and an async intake, and meets users where they already chat, a strong adoption lever for Teams-heavy companies. The email front half is already built, and the unblocking steps are documented in code, so phase 1 is a finishing job rather than a new system.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Slack/Teams agent apps: 2 of 5 (grokbot, qm; differentiator); per-agent email: Grok Bot only (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grok Bot creates a Slack app per bot through the manifest API (scopes for mentions, DMs, files, reactions, interactivity), installs it through OAuth with a typed outcome INSTALLED|PENDING_ADMIN_APPROVAL|WORKSPACE_REQUIRED|INSUFFICIENT_SCOPES|INSTALL_CONFLICT|RATELIMITED, and uses a per-tenant package for Teams. Outbound channels are typed addresses (email, Slack, Teams, SMS). Email: a dedicated domain per bot, mail only wakes the bot through a user routine, sending is approval-gated, and admins get sending windows, suppression lists and stats. qm's single-app manifest with an Agents pin is the simpler alternative.

verevonToday.gap: Mail-to-task is a self-forward flow (Postmark inbound): Ingestion and the gateway verify, rate-limit and dedup, then the gateway always returns 503 mail_task_pipeline_not_configured, because no unattended (no-live-user) turn exists outside Space scheduled runs. The thread-preparation seam (a mail_task_thread_bridge client for model-gateway's prepare-thread route over session-core PrepareUserOwnedThread) is built but deliberately unwired (SRC; module docs dated 2026-09-28, may be newer in code). No per-agent address and no send. Slack/Teams: a delivery-target field exists on bindings (stub, internal mutation only) and agent cards display targets; there is no adapter or install flow, the Slack/Teams mirror is planned (S5.1 ADR adopted, S5.3 blocked behind S4.4 and S4.3) and Channel Plane is docs-only.

items.approach: Phase 1 (Ingestion Plane plus Model Plane): reuse the mailtask verify, dedup and resolver path; wire the existing thread bridge (Auth Core service principal for the gateway, model-gateway internal route) and, sharing the unattended-turn plumbing with F-t1-047 (R-t1-06-03), post the synthesized first turn as untrusted input under the owner's authority; add a per-agent address claim; outbound send is a Model-proposed, room-approved integration action with suppression and rate windows. Phase 2: stand up Channel Plane only after S4.4 durable delivery, one adapter per platform, per-agent app identity, an install-state machine modelled on Grok Bot's outcome enum, a Control-owned external-identity link graph (never match on email alone, per the S5.1 ADR), and blocked delivery for ZDR Spaces because content leaves the boundary.
dependencies: Auth Core service principal for model-gateway
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (inbound email); Application Plane (delivery targets and mapping); Control Plane (identity links); Channel Plane (future adapters)
items.risks: Spam and phishing reaching agents (prompt injection through mail bodies); deliverability; ZDR violations when content leaves the boundary; platform review and admin-approval friction; identity mapping between external users and Verevon principals.

alreadyPlanned.where: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md (S5.1 ADR adopted, S5.3 first external adapter); apps/Channel Plane/docs/vision.md (docs-only). Per-agent email is not in the plan.

items.title: Public developer API with scoped tokens and rate limits (events, external bots and a curated catalogue later)
items.summary: Phase 1: publish an OpenAPI description generated from the typed action registry and serve it with org-issued, scoped, revocable API tokens minted by Control Plane (scope = action ids plus an optional Space allowlist, never wider than the issuing user's ACL), per-token token-bucket limits with Retry-After, and generated TS and Rust clients. Later phases, only on customer demand: signed event subscriptions from Application Plane outboxes, external bot identities as a binding kind, and a curated catalogue of skills, plugins, MCP servers and templates with admin approval instead of a Teams-style third-party store.
items.whyItMatters: Lets customers, CI and partner agents automate Spaces without screen-scraping, and one typed contract also feeds the agent self-API (F-t1-019 (R-t1-06-01)). It is table stakes in Teams, Slack and buzz, but it is not visible to most users at launch, so it follows the in-room work.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Public API: 3 of 5 (table-stakes); event subscriptions: Slack only (DOC); external bots: 2 of 5; app store: 2 of 5 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Teams Graph is the broadest parity surface (teams, channels, chats, messages, tabs, installed apps) over the same handlers as first-party clients, with OAuth2 app and user tokens, scopes and SDKs in several languages. Slack contributes the clearest rate-limit contract (tiered per-app token buckets, per-channel pacing of about 1 message/s, 429 with Retry-After) and the Events API (signed envelopes, 3 s ack, retries at 0/1/5 min, event_id dedup, auto-disable on repeated failure, Socket Mode). Buzz adds a signed-request HTTP bridge so scripts need no WebSocket.

verevonToday.gap: A typed internal action registry (14 spaces.* actions with zod schemas), a registry/dispatcher parity guard and an AG-UI stream exist, but Space routes sit behind a same-origin BFF session layer. No published API description, no third-party or app tokens with scopes, no rate-limit tiers, no SDK, no event subscriptions, no external bot identities and no app directory were found (baseline records; API-key/PAT auth and an OpenAPI export still to be searched for in the gateway).

items.approach: Frontend Plane gateway: generate and publish OpenAPI from the action registry; Control Plane issues and revokes scoped tokens; per-token rate limits with Retry-After; all writes keep flowing through the existing action dispatcher so audit and authority checks match the UI; generate TS and Rust clients. Phase 2 (Application Plane): publish Space events from the transactional outboxes to a per-app subscription table, with signed deliveries, retry, dead-letter and privacy-tier filtering so ZDR content is never emitted. Phase 3: an 'external agent' binding kind with Control roster confirmation and block/allow controls. Phase 4: extend the org plugin registry into a curated catalogue with admin approval and plain-language capability text.
dependencies: Control Plane token issuance and revocation
Action registry as single source of truth
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (API surface); Control Plane (tokens); Application Plane (events, bindings)
items.risks: Token leakage widening access; API drift from the UI; ZDR content leaving through the API or subscriptions; supply-chain and review burden for any third-party catalogue.

items.title: Compliance export, custodian legal hold, information barriers and audited admin break-glass
items.summary: Create a compliance principal in Control whose org-wide read is granted only by signed, audited decisions: export of room messages, agent turns with provenance and attachments by reference (by custodian, Space, time or keyword); custodian-level legal hold that pins items from retention and keeps originals on edit or delete; later, pairwise information barriers applied at membership and delivery. Add admin break-glass for agent computers and transcripts (hibernate, snapshot, kill, read with a reason), each audited and notified to the affected user, and never usable to impersonate an agent.
items.whyItMatters: Regulated buyers (finance, public sector, Nordic municipalities) cannot adopt a room product that holds agent output without hold and export. Operating personal agents with their own computers also needs a way to stop or inspect a stuck or abusive agent without widening anyone's ACL.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams
others: slack (Discovery API: read-only export apps versus read-write DLP apps)
grokbot (41 team-scoped admin RPCs including break-glass delete)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: eDiscovery, hold and barriers: 2 of 5 (teams, slack; DOC); admin break-glass: 2 of 5 (grokbot, qm SRC). Differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A compliance principal with org-wide read scope queries an export API by custodian, space, time and keyword; a hold pins items so retention sweepers skip them and edits or deletes keep originals in a hidden store; information barriers are pairwise segment-deny rules evaluated at membership add and message delivery. Break-glass uses a separate admin RPC namespace authorised by the admin role, every content read writes an audit row, destructive actions require a reason, and impersonation shows a persistent banner and is excluded from the agent tool surface.

evidence: apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/spaces/deletion_authorization.go and migrations 022 and 023 (legal holds and operator audit exist, as a blocker inside the personal Space deletion saga)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/sandbox-manager/internal/server/server.go:84-340 (lease, snapshot, workspace and process-registry RPCs only; no admin hibernate, kill or transcript-read RPC)
No compliance search, room export, custodian hold, communication-compliance scan or information barrier code found in the audited paths
verevonToday.gap: Legal hold exists only inside the personal Space deletion saga. There is no compliance principal, export, custodian hold, barrier or admin break-glass for agent computers.

items.approach: Control Plane: a compliance principal and a signed compliance decision (reason, scope, expiry) reusing decision.go, and custodian holds generalised from the deletion-saga hold. Application Plane: a server-to-server export of room projections gated by that decision. Data Plane: search over rooms. Model Plane sandbox-manager: admin RPCs for hibernate, snapshot and kill, honoured only with a signed break-glass decision; admin reads of Space content go through the shared-read gate with an audited override and an in-room notice. Information barriers later as Control membership rules. Do not impersonate agent authority.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane with Application Plane, Data Plane and Model Plane (sandbox-manager)
items.risks: ZDR rooms have nothing to export, which must be stated. Export is a mass exfiltration path and must be heavily audited. EU consent and works-council rules for reading people's agent transcripts; the affected user must be notified.

items.title: Perceived-latency observability: W3C traceparent on every send and stream, and performance budgets under simulated agent load
items.summary: Add a traceparent header and client timestamps (Enter pressed, composed) to Space sends and stream subscriptions, propagate them through the gateway into Control and Model Plane calls, and emit named client events for enter-to-ack, ack-to-first-frame, missing rows and resyncs. Add a Playwright performance project that floods a room with simulated agent output and asserts typing and scroll latency budgets using the Event Timing API.
items.whyItMatters: An agent-first room is only usable if typing stays fast while agents stream, and today nobody measures it. Three references trace sends end to end; only Buzz and Grok Bot test latency under agent load, which makes a budget in CI a real differentiator for Verevon.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (traceparent plus enter_epoch_ms and composed_at_ms on every send, 114 named perceived-quality events); Buzz (Playwright typing and scroll budgets under simulated agent load)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 3 of 5; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Client adds a W3C traceparent to send requests and stream subscriptions; the gateway propagates it; the client emits spans for enter to ack and ack to first frame; a perf CI project measures Event Timing under agent-typing floods with explicit budgets.

verevonToday.gap: SRC (grep in this step): server-side turn timing phases and first-token time are surfaced in chat-client.ts, but no traceparent appears in the SPA source or gateway source and no client perceived-latency events or agent-load performance budget were found.

items.approach: SPA shared http layer (src/shared/api) adds traceparent and enter_epoch_ms to sends and stream opens; gateway middleware propagates and forwards to user-core and model-gateway (the gateway already has an observability.rs metrics middleware to extend); client emits a small set of named timing events; add a Playwright perf project with a simulated agent flood fed through the room stream once F-t1-003 (R-t1-09-01) exists. Telemetry carries ids and timings only, never content.
dependencies: F-t1-003 (R-t1-09-01) for stream timing and agent-flood fixture
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Telemetry must not carry content (ZDR). Perf budgets need a stable CI environment to avoid flakiness.

items.title: Ids-only "report this" flow and hardened error-code registry
items.summary: Add a Report dialog in the Space, the run console and the error card that sends only ids (Space, run, thread, request ids, build id, error code, client error class) and an optional free-text note to a Support Plane ticket through the gateway, with no message bodies or screenshots by default. Extend the error catalogue with domain and retryable fields and add a gateway test that every emitted error code has a catalogue entry.
items.whyItMatters: Agent-heavy collaboration produces hard-to-reproduce problems. Ids-only reports let support reconstruct a run without private content and fit Zero-Data-Retention; retryable flags let the UI and agents decide between retry and ask-the-user.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: slack (self-service diagnostics kit, rotating logs with zipped upload, installation id) and teams (report-a-problem with screenshots and chunked upload); grokbot for the coded error registry
others: grokbot (108 coded errors grouped by domain with retryable flags and the raising location)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Report/diagnostics 2 of 5 (differentiator); coded registry 1 of 5 (unique).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: One action bundles recent request and trace ids, state and error code into a support upload; registry {code: {name, domain, retryable, summary, payload}} that UI, telemetry and retry logic all key on.

verevonToday.gap: The gateway returns {code, message} on every error and the client maps roughly 100 codes to Norwegian and English copy plus a ZDR refusal catalogue; errors.ts itself says it is not a claim that every gateway code is covered. There is no retryable flag, domain grouping or coverage test. No user-facing report-a-problem flow was found by name (the grep hits are report-artifact listings); request-id handling exists in several gateway domains. Whether Support Plane exposes an intake endpoint for such tickets was not checked.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: report dialog component reused by the error card (F-t1-024 (R-t1-11-02)), Space and run console, posting through a new gateway route to Support Plane; extend ERROR_COPY entries with domain and retryable and surface "retry" only when retryable. Gateway: a test that enumerates envelope error call sites against the catalogue and exposes the request id header consistently. Default to ids only; any content upload requires explicit consent and is refused for ZDR Spaces.
dependencies: Request id propagation in the gateway
items.planeOwner: Support Plane (client dialog and error catalogue: Frontend Plane)
items.risks: Uploading content from ZDR Spaces (default to ids only); catalogue drift without the coverage test.

items.title: ZDR-safe client persistence: Space drafts, per-user Space state synced across devices, cache hygiene, and an optional intent-only offline queue
items.summary: Stage it by risk. First persist non-content and low-risk state: Space composer drafts for non-ZDR organizations (reusing the existing client-storage helpers and sign-out purge) and per-user Space state (mutes, sidebar sections, per-thread read markers) stored server-side with last-writer-wins by updated_at. Later and only if wanted, add a head-page cache for non-ZDR orgs with a schema version and wipe, and an offline queue that stores user intent (text, room, idempotency key) and re-mints its Control decision at replay, with expiry and per-conversation ordering. Disable all content persistence for ZDR organizations.
items.whyItMatters: Most desktop references keep a local replica and sync per-user state across devices, but Verevon deliberately does not cache content in the browser because Zero-Data-Retention must propagate. Push plus paging gives most of the speed benefit, so the useful part now is losing no drafts and syncing state that is not content, without breaking ZDR.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Buzz (bounded, versioned paint-accelerator cache always replaced by authoritative data; per-field last-writer-wins preference registers); Teams for the offline queue (ordered resolvers, 48 h expiry, 10 cross-session retries); Slack for sign-out cleanup
others: Grok Bot (named local replicas, transcript write-ahead journal)
QM (server key/value UI-state API with LWW and future-skew clamp; deliberately no local cache)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 5 for a local replica (table-stakes in desktop clients); 2 of 5 each for offline queue, cache hygiene and cross-device per-user state
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Per (user, server) scope: last N room head pages, roster, selection and drafts hydrated before subscribing and replaced on the first authoritative page; schema version with wipe on mismatch; size caps. Server store keyed (user, key) with value up to 64 KB and updated_at, writes rejected if older than stored, client clocks clamped. Offline actions persisted with idempotency key, ordering key and expiry, replayed in order, stopping a conversation queue on hard failure.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: room read markers are server-side (cross-device) and preferences proxy to user-core. A shared client-storage helper exists and the Home chat draft is session-scoped, keyed by org and user, and removed at sign-out (per its own comment); no Space composer draft persistence, no per-thread read positions, no sidebar, layout or mute sync, no LWW semantics for preferences, no IndexedDB or service worker usage outside demo files, and no offline queue or content cache (consistent with ZDR).

items.approach: Frontend Plane: extend src/shared/session/client-storage.ts and a Space draft store (sessionStorage or org+user-keyed localStorage, text only, never for ZDR orgs, purged at sign-out). Application Plane: per-user Space state table alongside spaceReadMarkers (mutes, sections, per-thread read markers) with updated_at LWW and a future-skew clamp; profile-level settings stay in user-core preferences. Offline queue and content cache only after a ZDR-posture check in the client; the queue re-requests the content-bound Control decision (2-minute TTL) at replay and drops stale sends after a short expiry so an old message does not fire an agent turn hours later.
dependencies: Org ZDR posture available in the client
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane with Application Plane for synced per-user state
items.risks: ZDR conflict if content is ever persisted on the device; a stale cache could show revoked rooms, so re-authorize before render. Plane split between Control preferences and Application per-Space state must be explicit. Global presence and per-thread read frontier UX is owned by F-t1-042 (R-t1-01-09).

items.title: Long-tail polish: role-aware agent templates and persona library, owner-reviewed config proposals, catch-up summaries, external MCP surface
items.summary: Small, independent improvements once the core is in place: job-first agent creation with role/tool-tagged templates and a self-introduction; a persona library with agent teams and an export format built from an explicit field allowlist so secrets cannot be serialized; agent-proposed configuration changes that the owner reviews in a prefilled dialog; assistive AI in the room (time-windowed catch-up summaries with decisions and action items, rewrite, suggested actions); and an MCP server exposing Space tools to external agents with per-tool scopes.
items.whyItMatters: Each of these appears in only one or two references and adds modest value, but they make the product feel finished: faster agent setup, safer reuse of agent definitions, and the AI helpers people expect in a chat product.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (templates); buzz (allowlist snapshot, config proposals); teams (assistive AI); slack (hosted MCP server)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Each is 1 or 2 of 5 (unique or differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grok Bot: 74 eligibility-tagged templates (universal, job-role, selected-tools), onboarding answers injected as short system fragments, idempotent creation via a client-generated id with an optional kickstart introduction. Buzz: versioned manifest where only explicit fields are copied (asserted by tests), memory export levels none|core|all through the owner-gated path, definitions private unless marked shared; agent CLI emits typed config requests that the client parses with an allowlist schema into an owner dialog, deduped and bounded. Teams: summaries over 1/7/30-day windows with decisions and action items, rewrite with tones, suggested action chips. Slack: streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint with OAuth user tokens per tool scope, admin approval of clients and per-call audit.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceCreateAgentDialog.tsx:20-132 (three static templates: Meeting Scribe, Status Agent, Knowledge Helper)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:3913-4055 and src/features/spaces/components/SpaceBindAgentDialog.tsx:26-153 (org definitions can be re-bound into rooms)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/mcp.rs:1-30 (MCP client-side registry only; no MCP server for Space tools found)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces (no catch-up or summarise UI found by search)
verevonToday.gap: No role-aware template catalogue or self-introduction, no persona library, agent teams or export/import, no owner-reviewed proposal flow, no catch-up summaries, rewrite or suggested actions in rooms, and no hosted MCP surface for external agents.

items.approach: Frontend: template catalogue with eligibility tags stored as a template id on the definition; owner review dialog fed by an Application proposal object; catch-up and summary panel that calls the Model Plane with the room read decision (not stored under ZDR). Application: definition export with an explicit field allowlist covered by a leak test, and an agent team as a list of definition ids bound together. Gateway: an MCP endpoint mapping tools onto the agent-callable action classification from item F-t1-044 (R-t1-07-09), with per-tool scopes and admin client approval.
dependencies: Item F-t1-044 (R-t1-07-09) (agent-callable classification) for the MCP surface
Item F-t1-012 (R-t1-07-08) (summaries must not leak across the audience)
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (templates, summaries, MCP endpoint); Application Plane (definitions, proposals)
items.risks: Secret leakage if the export allowlist is not test-enforced; summaries leaking across audiences; external agents holding user tokens must be narrowly scoped.

items.title: Long-tail polish: voice and video clips with transcripts, image markup, per-viewer translation, room lenses
items.summary: After the attachment pipeline exists, add short voice and video clips with inline playback and transcripts, a canvas markup step before sending an image, an on-demand per-viewer translation of a message that is not stored for others, and a per-room layout lens (threads versus posts, plus an announcement mode that restricts who may reply).
items.whyItMatters: Voice clips suit mobile and pair with agents summarizing them; translation fits mixed Norwegian and English teams and agent output; markup helps screenshot feedback to agents; an announcement lens suits project and case Spaces. None blocks the core room.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (voice notes with streaming STT and word-level transcript jump); teams (translation, Posts versus Threads lens); buzz (image markup)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Voice/video clips 4 of 5 sources (table-stakes in the references); translation 2 of 5; room lenses 2 of 5; image markup 1 of 5
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Clips: recorder feeds the attachment pipeline, a transcription job stores the transcript as derived content linked to the clip, the player maps word timestamps to seek and offers speed control. Translation: Translate(entry_id, target_lang) runs inference with source hints and the result is shown only to the viewer (Slack states viewer-only; Teams has an admin policy flag). Lens: a room attribute layout=threads|posts switches the renderer, the change emits a system message, and an optional reply restriction (owner or moderator) serves announcement rooms. Markup: canvas strokes in natural-image coordinates, re-encoded before upload.

verevonToday.gap: A voice feature exists in src/features/voice but is not wired into rooms; no attachments, translation or markup in Space. Every post already renders as a thread card (effectively a Posts layout) and no layout flag was found in SpaceRoomTimeline or SpacePage. A translate route was not found in the Space UI, and the gateway was only spot-checked.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: reuse src/features/voice recorder and the F-t1-013 (R-t1-01-04) pipeline for clips; transcript through Model Plane inference inheriting room ACL and ZDR retention; image markup as a canvas editor before upload. Translation: a gateway route that calls Model Plane inference on demand, shown only to the requester, never persisted under ZDR, behind an org policy flag. Lens: a layout flag on the Space (Application Plane metadata) and a Control role policy for reply restriction; emit a system entry via F-t1-052 (R-t1-01-10) when it changes.
dependencies: Model Plane transcription and translation inference
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane with Model Plane inference and Control role policy
items.risks: Transcript and translation retention under ZDR; cost of per-view translation; lens switching must not hide entries a viewer is entitled to see. Overlaps category 03 (agent voice participants).

items.title: Federated search across connected providers under the asker's authority
items.summary: Extend the gateway fan-out from F-t1-069 (R-t1-04-08) with an integration-corev2 provider backend so a Space can search connected systems (for example Google, Microsoft, Salesforce content) as the asking user. Each backend gets its own Control decision, results are never cached or stored, and the UI shows which sources failed or were limited.
items.whyItMatters: Connected-provider search makes a Space an "ask the whole company" surface, and the owner-plane fan-out fits the no-cross-plane-DB rule. It is a later differentiator that needs message search and populated Space knowledge first.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 sources; differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: qm createCoreSearch(backends) runs a SearchBackend {name, search} registry concurrently with per-backend timeouts, tags hits by backend and type (message|conversation|file|page|external), and pushes failed or truncated backends into failed[] and limited[] arrays. Slack shows the product outcome (Enterprise+ search over Google, Microsoft and Salesforce) but the evidence is DOC only.

verevonToday.gap: No federated search surface. Only the Knowledge tab composes multiple sources (documents plus wiki via the retrieval binding) and it already reports per-section gaps. Provider content from integration-corev2 is not searchable from a Space, and whether integration-corev2 exposes search-shaped provider actions was not checked.

items.approach: Gateway (Frontend Plane BFF) orchestrator backends: Session Core messages, Data Plane documents and wiki, integration-corev2 provider search actions called as the asking user (per-backend Control decision, as in F-t1-038 (R-t1-04-03)). Response contract {hits, failed[], limited[]}. Never cache third-party results (provider terms and ZDR).
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (gateway orchestrator); Ingestion Plane (integration-corev2) for provider actions
items.risks: Latency of the slowest backend; third-party retention rules (Slack forbids storing results); heterogeneous ranking scores.

items.title: Meeting recording to governed object storage with a state machine, a mandatory recording indicator and expiry (defer behind transcripts)
items.summary: After calls and transcripts exist, add optional recording: SFU egress writes to object storage under the Space data owner, a recording record tracks started, processing, saved, failed and expired with size and expiry, every participant sees a recording indicator while it runs, an expiry job deletes the media, and access follows the meeting record. Recording stays off unless the meeting AI and recording policy allows it.
items.whyItMatters: Some organisations need replay and compliance evidence, but for an agent-first product the transcript and recap carry most of the value with far less sensitive data, so recording should follow, not lead.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Teams (REA): complete state machine started, stopped, processing, saved to cloud storage, expires in N days, upload errors by cause, duration and size limits
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 (Teams, Slack); differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: SFU egress (composite or per-track) to object storage; recording record {id, meeting id, state, storage ref, expires_at, size}; mandatory banner or badge for all participants; expiry job deletes media; access follows the meeting ACL.

evidence: apps/Channel Plane/docs/meeting-intelligence.md:18-58 (DOC: raw AV stored in access-controlled MinIO, but only for uploaded files in the MVP)
Baseline v-space-ui and v-space-backend (SRC): no calls, so no recording
verevonToday.gap: No recording, no storage lifecycle and no indicator. The only planned raw-AV storage is for uploaded files.

items.approach: Data Plane registers the recording artifact in MinIO; SFU egress runs under the Application Plane call record; Control Plane policy decides whether recording is allowed under the org ZDR posture and requires explicit recording consent in the F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-03) policy; Frontend shows the indicator in the call bar and announces start to all participants. An expiry job in the Data Plane owner deletes media and records a receipt.
dependencies: Object storage with retention and deletion receipts
items.planeOwner: Data Plane
items.risks: Raw media is high-sensitivity and conflicts with ZDR tenants. Consent law varies by jurisdiction. Retention must interoperate with Space deletion receipts.

items.title: Live in-meeting AI layer: captions, an optional interpreter agent and a facilitator agent (agenda, timers, live context)
items.summary: Once live ASR exists for F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-02), publish caption events to the call with language auto-detect, add an interpreter as an agent participant that translates and publishes a TTS track per target language, and add a Facilitator agent template beside Meeting Scribe that tracks an agenda posted by a human, nudges on time and goal, and surfaces Data Plane context when an entity is mentioned. Everything is opt-in, ephemeral and gated by the meeting AI policy.
items.whyItMatters: Accessibility and multilingual teams (the UI is already Norwegian and English), and a visible agent-in-the-room moment that human-only call tools cannot copy. It reuses the live transcript, Space agents and Data Plane retrieval instead of adding stores.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Teams (REA): captions with spoken-language auto-detect, AI interpreter with a named roster identity, agenda and timer smart actions
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Captions and interpretation 1 of 5 (Teams, unique); facilitator behaviours 2 of 5 (Teams, Slack), differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Streaming ASR per active speaker emits caption events on the realtime channel; the interpreter is an agent participant that subscribes to audio, translates and publishes per-language audio; a facilitator bound to the meeting reads live transcript and chat, triggers on an agenda message, elapsed-time checkpoints and entity mentions, and posts suggestions as drafts or ephemeral messages.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/api/speech-client.ts:6,91 (SRC: only governed TTS through Azure Speech; no captions)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceCreateAgentDialog.tsx:43-54 (SRC: Meeting Scribe template, text conversation only)
verevonToday.gap: No captions, interpretation or live meeting context. Space agents run on explicit invocation and schedules; nothing listens to a live session.

items.approach: Model Plane: streaming ASR variant of the F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-02) job that emits partial segments; Application Plane fans out caption events to the call; the interpreter is a case of the agent participant from F-t1-067 (R-t1-03-06) phase B; the Facilitator is a new template in SpaceCreateAgentDialog whose agent subscribes to transcript events of the meeting record under the F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-03) policy and posts suggestions only as ephemeral drafts.
dependencies: F-t1-067 (R-t1-03-06) phase B for the interpreter
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Latency and cost of streaming ASR per call. Interruption noise from facilitator nudges, so keep them opt-in and ephemeral. Slack evidence is marketing-level and low confidence.

items.title: Call polish and operability: call-health feedback, browser audio and video processing, in-tab push-to-talk and mute keys, wake lock and busy guard, call sounds and Join notifications
items.summary: A bundle of small web-native follow-ups to F-t1-029 (R-t1-03-01). Use browser audio constraints and SDK-provided noise filters instead of custom ML. Sample WebRTC getStats into a call-health panel and a short reason-code feedback prompt when thresholds are crossed. Add in-tab push-to-talk and mute keys. Acquire the Screen Wake Lock during calls and register busy reasons (call, upload, pending approval) that guard beforeunload. Add join, leave and ring sounds and a notification Join action.
items.whyItMatters: These make calls reliable and pleasant without building any desktop shell. The reason-code feedback pattern also suits rating agent runs, and the busy-reason registry protects long agent runs and approvals watched in a tab.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack (SRC): push-to-talk with separate press and release, restart veto with reason codes, port-bound keep-awake lease, sound pack; Teams (REA and SRC): metric-triggered feedback and cloud-delivered audio DSP
others: Buzz (SRC): global push-to-talk in its desktop engine
Teams (SRC): most OS entry points for joining meetings
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Per capability 1 to 2 of 5 (A/V enhancement Teams, call health Teams, hotkeys Slack and Buzz, restart veto Slack, sounds and entry points Slack and Teams); differentiator or unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Web equivalents: getUserMedia noiseSuppression, echoCancellation and autoGainControl constraints; getStats sampling for RTT, jitter and loss; keydown and keyup push-to-talk while the tab is focused; navigator.wakeLock during calls; a busy registry consulted before any app version swap or navigation; short audio cues; Web Notifications with a Join action and a web+verevon protocol handler for deep links.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/voice/voice-recorder.ts:36-41 (SRC: VOICE_AUDIO_CONSTRAINTS already enables echoCancellation, noiseSuppression and autoGainControl)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/voice/VoiceModeDialog.tsx:512 (SRC: only a dialog-level keydown handler; tap-to-talk, no push-to-talk)
Grep this session of verevonv3/src for wakeLock, registerProtocolHandler, new Notification and PushManager: no non-test matches; no service worker or PWA manifest in verevonv3/public
verevonToday.gap: Browser audio processing is on for dictation only. No call media to measure, no feedback prompt, no push-to-talk, no wake lock, no busy-reason guard, no call sounds, notifications or deep links. The comparator open question is answered: there is no service worker, so no skipWaiting deferral exists or is needed today; updates arrive on reload. Verevon is web-only, so global hotkeys and OS jump lists are out of reach.

items.approach: Frontend Plane only, after F-t1-029 (R-t1-03-01): add noise-filter options to the media-devices module, a getStats sampler feeding a health panel and an Application Plane feedback record that is reused for agent-run feedback, in-tab key handlers (space to talk, M to mute) that do not collide with the composer, a small busy-reason registry plus Wake Lock, sound cues behind a user setting, and notification Join actions once Space notifications exist. Do not store voice profiles or other biometric-like data.
dependencies: Space notifications (notifications category) for Join actions
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Wake Lock is not supported everywhere and must always be released. Notification permission fatigue. Call telemetry must stay aggregate for privacy. Shortcut conflicts with the room composer.

items.title: Read-only snapshot share of a room or thread with an allowlisted projection
items.summary: Let a user share an immutable snapshot of a room outcome (org or link scope) that contains only user messages, final replies and copied attachments, never reasoning, tool output or raw payloads, behind an unguessable token. Revalidate that the creator can still read the source on every view and serve it from a session-less, no-store, noindex route with a strict CSP. Disallow under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: It is a safe way to hand a case outcome to a customer or auditor without exposing agent traces, matching Verevon's ZDR and audit posture. It is not a table-stakes room feature and matters mainly for case Spaces with external parties.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 5 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: share_snapshots {token, created_by, scope (org|link), entries[] (allowlisted projection), file_copies[]}; the render path loads no session; every read re-checks that the creator is still an internal member with access to the source thread, else 404; file ids are share-specific copies.

verevonToday.gap: No thread or Space share or export; only the user GDPR export and erase routes exist.

items.approach: Model Plane Session Core produces the allowlisted projection; Data Plane copies attachments under share-specific ids; the Frontend serves a session-less read-only route with the hardened headers. Refuse creation under ZDR and honour revocation and retention.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (Session Core)
items.risks: Leaking internal content through links, so enforce retention, revocation and the creator re-check.

items.title: Versioned publish lifecycle for agent-built apps and shared agent definitions
items.summary: Follow the adoption plan's S5.4 slice for governed internal app build and publish: the Model builds in a credential-brokered Space workspace, emits an immutable build artifact and manifest, and Application stores app and version metadata with rollback as a pointer flip and private-until-shared visibility. In the same lifecycle, give shared agent definitions draft and published revisions with a Publish changes action, pinned by Space bindings.
items.whyItMatters: It lets agents ship durable internal tools for a team, a strong Grok-Bot-style differentiator, and gives shared agents the human-authorized publish step the authority model requires. It is expensive and not core to the chat room.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (SRC) for deployments; Grok Bot (SRC) for pages and agent draft/publish
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: publish apps: 2 of 5, differentiator; agent definition lifecycle: 1 of 5, unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: publish(dir) produces an immutable version blob and manifest; the deployment row points at current_version; rollback is a CAS pointer flip; a DeployProvider interface (apply, reconcile, destroy, resolveEndpoint, logs); the owner scope decides access and the created-in scope is provenance; per-deployment credentials limit data replication to its own prefix. Agent definitions keep draft and published revisions, the UI flags draft differing from published, and a visibility enum controls audience with typed outcomes (PUBLISHED, ALREADY_PUBLISHED, NOT_SHARED, BUSY).

verevonToday.gap: Studio is a gateway-local, ephemeral canvas of layout blocks with social-draft export, with no publish, versioning, hosting or visibility model. Governed app build and publish is a deliberately post-foundation plan item (S5.4). Whether shared agent definitions have draft versus published revisions was not verified; the agent blueprint UI lists Draft, Published and Rollback as a label only.

items.approach: Follow S5.4 ownership: Model builds in the sandbox, Application owns app, version and share metadata and the Space projection, Infra owns sandboxed hosting and routing on an isolated origin, Control owns human grants, and Data stores versioned bundles. For agent definitions add draft and published revisions in the Model Plane agent registry with a Control decision to publish to the org, and have Space bindings pin a published revision.
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (with Model Plane, Infra and Control)
items.risks: Hosting untrusted generated code (isolation, CSP, egress), cost and data residency. Revision pinning across many bindings. Heavy for the current stage.

alreadyPlanned.where: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md:2263-2272 (S5.4 governed internal app build/publish, status [~]; apps only). Agent definition draft/publish is not planned.

items.title: Multi-window coordination: pop-out run console, cross-org unread counts, idle presence signal
items.summary: Open the agent run console and a Space thread as compact pop-out routes (?popout=1) via window.open, coordinate tabs and windows with one SharedWorker or BroadcastChannel leader that owns the SSE connection and the presence heartbeat, derive an active/away signal from visibility plus input idle time (Idle Detection API where permitted), and add a per-org unread-count endpoint so the org switcher can show badges without switching.
items.whyItMatters: Watching an agent work in a side window while chatting in the Space is a natural cooperation pattern, and guests from partner companies need to see activity in both orgs. Routing approvals to a present human needs a trustworthy presence signal. Several windows must not multiply SSE connections.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (window manager with tagged windows, per-type placement, pop-out chats and calls; multi-tenant isolated instances with shared notifications)
others: slack (rail with Ctrl/Cmd+1..9 switching and tray badge; safe child-window option allowlist)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Pop-out 2 of 5 (differentiator); multi-workspace unread 3 of 5 (common); OS idle/lock signals 1 of 5 (unique).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Window tags opened through a bridge with allowlisted options, each loading the same SPA route in a compact layout with shared state via the server stream; an aggregator streams unread per account; native idle/lock events forwarded as host events (web substitute: visibility plus idle timers).

verevonToday.gap: Org switching is one active org at a time (server-side switchOrganization) with no cross-org unread and no keyboard switching. Document visibility only slows navbar polling; no idle-based presence or online/offline banner was verified. The run console exists as a lazy route, but no pop-out or compact route was found (window.open is used only for search results and OAuth popups, per the comparator); whether it can render standalone was not checked.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: compact route variants for AgentRunConsole and the Space thread plus a SharedWorker/BroadcastChannel multiplexer in front of shared/api/sse.ts and the presence heartbeat. Application Plane: presence heartbeat consumer (see F-t1-042 (R-t1-01-09); personal data, org-scoped and optional) and a per-org unread projection returning counts only, each computed under that org's own ACL (see F-t1-055 (R-t1-02-12) for the switcher UI). Shell adds placement memory later via F-t1-090 (R-t1-11-10).
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (unread and presence projections: Application Plane)
items.risks: Multiple SSE connections per user raise gateway load without the multiplexer; the org switcher must never leak another org's Space names into the current org context; presence is personal data and must be optional.

items.title: Shell-only conveniences: quick composer, global hotkey and push-to-talk, window state, close guard
items.summary: Once the Tauri shell exists, add an always-on-top mini composer window that posts to the same gateway run endpoint as the Space composer (landing in the user's personal Space so it stays auditable), a validated global shortcut with key-up events for push-to-talk to the voice feature, and window-state memory. Ship the web-first part now: a beforeunload guard when the Space composer holds unsent text or a run is awaiting approval.
items.whyItMatters: A personal agent one keystroke away is the Grok Bot half of the Space vision, and push-to-talk suits the existing voice feature. These need OS-level hooks a browser tab cannot provide.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (transparent always-on-top mini composer that sends to the selected Bot, switchable from a menu)
others: slack (flag-gated tray-click overlay; validated global-shortcut API with key-down/key-up; bounds clamped to a live display)
teams (close prompts for unsent messages and calls)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Window management 3 of 5 (common); quick composer 2 of 5 (differentiator); global shortcuts 1 of 5 (unique).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Frameless transparent window loading a minimal composer route with its own capability set and a typed call that submits a prompt to the selected agent; native global-shortcut registration with validation and key-up events; persisted bounds per window type validated against live displays; close policy with prompt cases.

verevonToday.gap: No native shell, so no window management, global shortcuts or quick composer; a web equivalent of the close prompt (beforeunload on unsent composer text or a running agent) was not found.

items.approach: Frontend Plane inside the F-t1-073 (R-t1-11-09) workspace: secondary window plus tauri-plugin-global-shortcut and tauri-plugin-window-state; the mini composer route posts through the existing run endpoint with org and ZDR context carried; push-to-talk reuses src/features/voice. Web-first guard is a small beforeunload handler on the Space composer. Overlaps in-tab push-to-talk keys in F-t1-086 (R-t1-03-11).
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Prompts typed outside a Space must still carry ZDR and org context; shortcut collisions with other apps; over-eager beforeunload prompts annoy users.

items.title: Realtime and media operability after push ships: shared connection per browser, drain on deploy, capability discovery, stream-stall self-test, perf marks, media cache policy
items.summary: Once the push stream exists: share one connection across tabs (leader tab via Web Locks and BroadcastChannel, or SharedWorker) with frame batching; autoscale on active connections and drain with a close frame plus client resume; advertise capabilities and limits in the connected frame; add a diagnostics stream with timed heartbeats so the client detects SSE buffering by customer proxies and shows IT guidance; report web vitals and a space_open mark; and verify the media route supports Range, ETag and private caching with no-store for ZDR Spaces.
items.whyItMatters: Operational hardening that matters only after the substrate ships; Verevon's own nginx tier is already stream-friendly, so the risk sits in customer networks.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Buzz (shared socket with frame coalescing, HPA on active-websocket gauge, NIP-11 capability document); Slack for drain (cell and AZ drain in about 5 minutes; DOC); QM for ack-after-durable ingress (AckGate, 2.5 s cap, durable staging, redelivery on failure) and single background-owner record; grokbot (in-app Network Debugger with IT guidance for SSE and HTTP/2) for network diagnostics; teams (shared scenario marks and INP-style telemetry) for performance; buzz (media grants with range requests) for media
others: Teams (shared workers, BroadcastChannel and Web Locks across windows; published limits with feature degradation by room size)
Grok Bot (about 260 typed dynamic configs with client fallbacks; utility-process coordinator over MessagePort)
buzz (Playwright suite and E2E bridge that mocks transport)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-09-11] 3 of 5 for off-thread/shared sync, scale-out and protocol evolution (common); 2 of 5 for load shaping and ack-after-durable ingress (differentiator); 1 of 5 for server-driven tuning [R-t1-11-12] Network diagnostics 2 of 5, startup performance 2 of 5, authenticated media 2 of 5 = differentiators.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-09-11] Web equivalent: a leader tab elected via Web Locks owns the single SSE and posts coalesced batches to other tabs over BroadcastChannel. HPA on the active-connection gauge; on deploy the old build stops claiming and sends close frames so clients reconnect with resume. GET capabilities or a connected-frame field lists supported features and limits and absence means unsupported. A registry maps config name to schema and fallback. Ingress holds the platform ack until the event is persisted, or after a cap writes the raw envelope to a durable map and acks. [R-t1-11-12] Connectivity probe classes (DNS, TLS, proxy, stream stall) with remediation text; scenarioStart/Mark/Stop emitting success, failure or abandoned; media URLs carry short-lived authorization and forward Range headers with a content-keyed cache.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-09-11] SRC: timings are hard-coded constants (6 s poll, 30 s recheck); a per-tab store avoids duplicate polls within a tab but no BroadcastChannel, Web Locks or SharedWorker usage was found outside demo files; the gateway /api/v1/capabilities route is the Model Plane skills catalog, not realtime capability discovery; agent-binding delivery targets are a schema stub and Channel Plane is docs-only. Unknown: gateway replica and autoscaling manifests, leader election for background loops, room size limits, and cron jitter in capability-core. [R-t1-11-12] The SSE reader supports Last-Event-ID resume but a grep of sse.ts finds no heartbeat, stall or timeout detection and no connectivity self-test. The Verevon-owned nginx tier is already stream-friendly (proxy_buffering off, 3600 s read timeout on /api/), so the risk sits in customer-side proxies and TLS inspection. Performance telemetry, route-level chunking intent and the media route (Range support, cache headers, ZDR no-store) were not assessed. Playwright configs including a real-authority one exist; a scripted SSE fixture for Space events was not found.

items.approach: [R-t1-09-11] After F-t1-003 (R-t1-09-01): (1) leader-tab connection manager in the SPA (SharedWorker is limited on iOS Safari, so prefer Web Locks); (2) check gateway deployment manifests for replicas and HPA metric and add an active-connection gauge, drain with close frame and jittered resume; (3) add features and limits to the stream connected frame, with an ignore-unknown-kinds rule in the client; (4) move poll and watchdog timings into one typed config registry (overlaps feature flags in F-t1-006 (R-t1-02-05)) with fallbacks; (5) coalesce per-room fan-out above a member threshold and add jitter to capability-core cron; (6) when Channel Plane or F-t1-075 (R-t1-06-10) external channels start, apply ack-after-durable staging. [R-t1-11-12] Frontend Plane: /diagnostics/stream endpoint in the gateway plus a stall detector in sse.ts and a settings-page self-test with an allowlist document; web-vitals and space_open marks posted to the monitoring domain; audit the gateway media route for cookie auth, Range, ETag, private cache-control and no-store for ZDR; optional scripted SSE fixture so Playwright can assert agent-activity rendering deterministically.
dependencies: F-t1-035 (R-t1-11-01) (service-worker shell cache, if perf marks compare cached and cold opens)
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (gateway and SPA) with Application Plane (load shaping)
items.risks: [R-t1-09-11] Reconnect storms after drain need jitter. Config sprawl if the registry is not kept small. SharedWorker support gaps on some browsers. [R-t1-11-12] Stale service-worker caches skew perf data; caching private media on shared machines; mock fixtures drifting from real contracts.

items.title: Delivery health: channel failover and a 'why am I not notified' diagnosis
items.summary: Track per-device and per-channel health {consecutive_failures, failover_at} in the S4.4 ledger and fall back along an order such as push, then in-app, then email digest, retrying the primary after a TTL. Pair it with a Settings and bell banner that lists typed reasons notifications are not arriving (DND active, browser permission denied, push subscription expired, room muted, channel failing), computed client-side for browser state and server-side for preferences and last failed attempt.
items.whyItMatters: Cuts support load and builds trust that agent alerts will arrive. Silent channel switching confuses users unless it is paired with a diagnosis, which is why the two belong together. Only worthwhile after push and email exist.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack (only source)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 5 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Slack keeps a consecutive-failure counter (5 triggers telemetry), records a failover timestamp for a week and clears it at the next start so the native path is retried, and policy can force native. Its warning call returns typed reason codes, cached 30 s when warnings exist and 1 h when clean.

verevonToday.gap: notification-core records per-attempt status but a grep of its Go sources found no failover or channel-health logic, and no per-user delivery-status or diagnostics endpoint was found in its HTTP routes (INF from grep).

items.approach: Application Plane: add channel health and fallback order to the ledger from F-t1-060 (R-t1-05-10), plus a read endpoint exposing server-side reasons (preferences, DND, last failed attempt). Frontend Plane: compute browser-side reasons (permission, subscription) and show a banner in Settings and next to the bell.
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (health state); Frontend Plane (banner)
items.risks: Low; silent failover without the diagnosis would confuse users. The Space definition treats notification polish as a non-goal (docs/space-defenition.md:352-353).

items.title: Multi-org and external collaboration horizon: org archive and transfer, shared cross-org rooms, managed external chat connections
items.summary: Do the cheap part first: org lifecycle states (archived, owner transfer) in org-core. Later, after guests, add org-to-org links with host-org-owned shared rooms and external trust cues, with QM's rule that an external audience restricts agents to a context without org memory or keys. External chat workspace connections belong to the future Channel Plane, not to be built elsewhere.
items.whyItMatters: Slack Connect and Teams shared channels are enterprise differentiators, and a parent org over several orgs matters for managed-service customers. Verevon's customers are single companies today, so this is a long-horizon investment; org archive and transfer are the useful cheap slice.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: slack (Enterprise Grid, Slack Connect), buzz (operator lifecycle), qm (external audience isolation, managed Slack connections)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: tenant hierarchy 2 of 5, shared channels 3 of 5 (common), external connections 1 of 5; differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Two-level tenancy org -> workspaces with policy resolving org then workspace; operator lifecycle as a state machine on the tenant row (active, archived, deleting with fence generation, deleted) with transfer as an owner swap. Shared rooms: shared_room(host_org, room_id) plus org_link(host_org, guest_org, status); the host org's policy governs posting and apps, members authenticate in their own org, and the client shows an external marker and a consent pane on first contact. QM: a reconciler swaps the Slack adapter on config version change with rollback.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/settings/components/OrgDeletionDangerZone.tsx (org deletion exists, no archive or transfer)
verevonToday.gap: Single-level org tenant with deletion; no archive or ownership transfer, no parent org, no shared or cross-org rooms, no external chat connections (planned, blocked).

items.approach: Control Plane: org-core lifecycle (archived, transfer_pending) and owner-transfer flow first; defer a parent-org table until a customer needs it. After guests exist, org-to-org links and host-org-owned rooms with decisions that carry both orgs' policies, plus agent audience isolation as soon as any external participant can exist. External chat connections: wait for the Channel Plane; do not build adapters elsewhere.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane
items.risks: ZDR, residency and retention differ per org and one org's ZDR must hold for content its members post, which is hard to fit under per-org deny-by-default policies. Hierarchical policy resolution interacts with deny-by-default effect policies. The Channel Plane is docs-only, so this cannot be built as if it existed.

alreadyPlanned.where: External chat connections: apps/Channel Plane/docs/vision.md (docs-only); QM adoption plan S5.1 ADR adopted, S5.3 blocked

items.title: Assurance long tail: hash-chained audit, formal decision model, supply-chain gates, EU-posture pinning, credential expiry states
items.summary: Five independent assurance items for regulated buyers, taken after the audit export exists. (1) Chain audit rows (entry_hash over seq, actor, action, metadata, prev_hash) with a signed daily head checkpoint and a verify endpoint. (2) Model Space decision issuance in TLA+ or PlusCal, checking 'Space access never widens an owner ACL' and 'no effect without a fresh decision'. (3) Add supply-chain gates: dependency cooldown, cargo-deny and govulncheck across all Rust and Go services, signed images. (4) State an EU-only posture and pin model-provider region per org. (5) Credential lifecycle states with expiry warnings in agent settings.
items.whyItMatters: None of these block the Space, but they answer the questions enterprise security questionnaires ask and make Verevon's signed-authority design verifiable. Each facet is small and independent.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Hash chain and formal specs: 1 of 5 each (buzz); supply chain: 2 of 5 (buzz, qm); residency: 2 of 5 (slack, teams); credential lifecycle: 1 of 5 (grokbot).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Audit: entry hash over the tenant id, sequence, time, event, actor, action, canonical metadata and previous hash, with an external signed anchor. Formal: spec the multi-party protocol, mutate the spec to prove the invariants are not vacuous, replay service traces against the model. Supply chain: 7-day package cooldown, prod dependency audit, signed images with digest pins. Residency: per-org home region in Control that routes data-plane calls. Credentials: state, expires_at and a warn or enforce mode with owner notice.

evidence: apps/Control Plane/audit-core/internal/store/schema.sql:11-33 (payload_hash per event, but no prev_hash or entry_hash chain; a grep found none)
A search to depth 4 of apps/ found no TLA+, Alloy or Tamarin files

.github/workflows/verevonv3-security.yml:26-51 (pnpm audit at high), quarry-v2-ci.yml:231-240 (cargo audit and govulncheck), secret-scan.yml and dependabot.yml; no release-age policy or image signing found by grep of workflows

apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/spaces/authority.go:149-153 (a residency string is bound into every decision) and apps/Control Plane/org-core/internal/org/types.go:60-68 (dormant data_residency column); no routing or provider pinning seen
apps/Ingestion Plane/integration-corev2 credential model: expiry states not checked
verevonToday.gap: Some supply-chain checks exist for the frontend and Quarry only; the rest is absent or unchecked. Residency is a label with no enforcement.

items.approach: audit-core: add prev_hash and entry_hash with per-org serialised append and a signed checkpoint using existing key infrastructure. Repo CI: min-release-age, cargo-deny and govulncheck for every service, image signing in the deploy pipeline. Model Plane inference routing: per-org provider-region pinning plus a documented EU-only deployment statement (full multi-region stacks are out of scope). integration-corev2 and Frontend: credential state, expiry and warnings, aligned with the S3.4 credential broker. Formal model: write the decision protocol spec alongside the Space authority ADR.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (audit-core) with Support Plane (CI), Model Plane (routing) and Ingestion Plane (credentials)
items.risks: Append serialisation limits audit throughput; checkpoint key management; formal models drift from code unless trace-checked; CI friction; sub-processor residency (Novu, Convex) limits what 'EU-only' can claim.

alreadyPlanned.where: Credential expiry and revocation are in apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md S3.4; the other facets are not planned.

items.title: Long-tail Space UX, build on demand: multiview tiling, agent-led first-run welcome, What's New and admin notices, non-web link interstitial
items.summary: Four independent slices, none of which blocks the vision. (a) Multiview: tile several rooms or agent sessions with a dockview-style layout once AuxPane and run components are self-contained. (b) Welcome: seed the org room with an agent introduction and role/tools questions that feed the three agent templates. (c) What's New panel and admin-only notices for policy rollout. (d) Route non-http(s) links in agent-posted content through a confirmation with per-host memory.
items.whyItMatters: Multiview is a real edge for operators supervising several agents (QM only); a welcome post where an agent introduces itself removes the empty-room first impression; admin notices help owners learn which deny-by-default agent policies to enable; and a link gate reduces risk from model-generated links.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (multiview with tile limits and per-pane density); Grok Bot (onboarding flow and fail-open gate); Teams (feedback, What's New, admin campaigns); Slack (protocol interstitial with per-host allowlist)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: multiview 1 of 5 (QM); onboarding 2 of 5 (Grok Bot, Buzz); What's New 1 of 5 (Teams); link interstitial 1 of 5 (Slack); differentiator to unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Multiview: dockview-core layout with MAX_TILES = 16, per-pane drag payloads and a serialised layout synced per user. Onboarding: gate state machine checking -> probe -> landed | onboarding | shell with a saved seen flag that fails open for returning users. What's New: feed items with an index and campaigns targeted by role and flag. Interstitial: intercept non-http(s) schemes, show a modal, store an allowlist of {protocol, hostname} per user.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/onboarding/components/steps/IntroStep.tsx and apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpacesIndexPage.tsx:36-47 (org onboarding and self-healing /spaces exist; no Space first run)
verevonToday.gap: Multiview absent; no Space-specific first run (welcome content, agent introduction, role/tools questions); a grep for whats-new/WhatsNew finds nothing, though "feedback" appears in 36 files of unknown purpose; how agent-posted non-web links are rendered (markdown link sanitiser in chat components) is not checked.

items.approach: Frontend Plane for all four. Multiview after AuxPane (F-t1-001 (R-t1-12-01)), push realtime (a 6 s poll per tile multiplies polling cost) and self-contained room and run components. Welcome: seed a post and template agent proposals that a human confirms (agents may not create bindings themselves), with claims derived from observed facts, not timers. What's New from a static release feed, admin notices through Control role targeting. Link gate: extend the markdown link sanitiser so non-http(s) schemes never auto-open.
dependencies: AuxPane shell (F-t1-001 (R-t1-12-01)) and push realtime (category 09) for multiview
Human-only post path (category 01) and existing agent templates for the welcome
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Tile polling cost; agents must not self-create bindings; notice noise. Verify the link-rendering and feedback surfaces before scoping slices (c) and (d).

items.title: Reverse channel so a user's own computer can run agent tool requests without inbound ports (later; cloud browser first)
items.summary: If the "agent has its own PC" vision extends to the user's machine, add a local executor daemon that keeps an outbound SSE open through the gateway, receives Model-proposed tool requests, checks them against a local policy, executes, and posts results back with the request id, with heartbeat, a polling fallback and supervised restart. Do this only after the cloud sandbox and browser path is solid, and keep the rule that the Model proposes and the executor decides.
items.whyItMatters: It is the one reference capability that makes an agent act on the real desktop and the most distinctive part of the Grok Bot half of the vision, but it adds a large local-execution attack surface and only Grok Bot ships it. The gateway already streams live browser frames and supports human takeover for cloud browser runs, which covers most needs first.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (daemon opens GET /local-exec/requests as SSE, POSTs results back; one daemon serves several accounts; discovery record with pid and generation; respawn limits)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 5; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Daemon keeps an outbound SSE with heartbeat; on a request frame it executes under local policy and POSTs the result with the request id; if the stream fails it polls a pending endpoint; the app adopts or replaces the daemon via a discovery record.

verevonToday.gap: No local agent or daemon was found by the comparator (not exhaustively searched). SRC: for cloud browsers the gateway exposes live-frame streams, human_takeover and agent_control capabilities; the space baselines list an agent PC or browser inside the room as absent and only RustDesk remote-support configuration exists.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane executor (Quarry-style) that only executes Model-proposed actions after a local policy check, with an outbound SSE through the gateway and a request/response contract using Control-signed grants and receipts; reuse the browser live-frame channel for viewing. Decide first whether a Space agent should ever reach a user machine, then design the policy model.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane
items.risks: Large security surface (local code execution and credential exposure); must preserve the Model-proposes, executor-decides split and ZDR for anything captured locally.

dropped.reason: Agent outbound phone calls: out of Space scope, single-source medium-confidence evidence (Grok Bot strings and RPC names) and a telephony dependency; the only reusable part, consequence-stated wording on irreversible-effect approval cards, is folded into the approvals item.

waves.goal: Foundations and quick wins: a human-first room with shared threads on a live push substrate, ZDR and Space policy that actually bind, and cheap fixes people notice at once (error boundaries, room admin, artifacts in the room, send idempotency, CSP, avatar, audit read check).
